artigo.texto: Understanding how ions move through solid materials is key to advancing technologies such as batteries, fuel cells and sensors. A team of scientists led by the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Argonne National Laboratory has demonstrated a cutting-edge method for gauging the activity of ions, revealing a new level of detail about how they move and interact. The team tested the technique, which they have called 4D quasielastic neutron scattering (4D-QENS), at the Spallation Neutron Source, a DOE Office of Science user facility at DOE's Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL). The results show that 4D-QENS provides critical insights that will help improve the theoretical models needed to design next-generation solid-state batteries and related technologies. Some materials allow charged atoms or molecules - called ions - to move quickly. This property makes them suitable as electrolytes in solid-state batteries, which could store more energy and offer greater safety compared to conventional batteries - most of which use liquid electrolytes to move ions during charging and discharging. But a clearer understanding of the mechanisms underlying ionic conduction would help scientists optimize solid-state battery performance. Historically, researchers generally believed that ionic motion in solids was essentially an independent, diffusion-based process. Researchers are now exploring the idea that correlated motion - movement driven by interactions between ions - is key to ultrafast conductivity. However, direct experimental observation remains elusive. Ionic motion is best studied by quasielastic neutron scattering (QENS), which involves directing neutrons at a material sample and measuring the changes in direction and energy as they scatter off the sample. Those changes reveal movements of atoms or molecules within the material. Such studies have provided important insight into the independent, diffusion-based dispersion of ions. The 4D-QENS technique involves rotating a single-crystal sample as it is exposed to the neutrons. This results in data that allows the researchers to generate a complete picture not only of how ions are moving but also of interactions that drive correlated motion. "The idea of doing these sample rotations has been around at pulsed neutron sources for about 15 years, but it has not been applied to QENS before," said Raymond Osborn, senior physicist at Argonne and lead author of a study unveiling this new method. "With 4D-QENS, we show new effects that we would never have seen without such large, contiguous volumes of data." To test the method's potential, the researchers performed 4D-QENS on single-crystal samples of strontium chloride, a salt that becomes a fast-ion conductor at temperatures above 1,200 degrees Fahrenheit. Though strontium chloride is not a candidate for future applications, its well-studied properties made it an ideal model crystal on which to test the technique. The study delivered a refined understanding of ion movement from one site to another within the crystal lattice structure - hopping - that agreed with previous studies. But it also revealed direct evidence of correlated motion among ions that can either facilitate movement through the material or lead to traffic jams that would be detrimental in a battery. A deeper understanding of such correlated motion through 4D-QENS is crucial to help improve solid-state electrolytes. The unique properties of neutrons, which are electrically neutral with a mass similar to the atoms and ions, are key for this technique. Minute changes in neutron velocity, accompanied by significant changes in direction, allow researchers to chart ion movements in considerable detail. That led researchers to the Spallation Neutron Source at ORNL, the world's most powerful pulsed neutron source. The volume of data from such measurements further increased with the recent power upgrade of the Spallation Neutron Source, along with ever more powerful DOE computing resources such as the Argonne Leadership Computing Facility (ALCF), also a DOE Office of Science user facility. "The questions that we were able to ask about ion conductivity even a few years ago were much more limited in scope. Now we're measuring 3D volumes plus energy transfer, making it 4D," said Stephan Rosenkranz, Argonne Distinguished Fellow and group leader in the Materials Science division. "These comprehensive datasets are allowing new modes of data analysis. Those modes demand computing resources that can match the quality of the data." This type of analysis would be appropriate in future applications of 4D-QENS to more complex materials that are directly relevant to solid-state electrolytes and other energy technologies, the researchers said. The work, supported by DOE's Office of Basic Energy Sciences, is detailed in the journal PRX Energy. In addition to Osborn and Rosenkranz, Argonne authors include Jared Coles, Omar Chmaissem, Matthew Krogstad, Daniel Pajerowski, Feng Ye, Duck Young Chung and Mercouri Kanatzidis. Along with Argonne and ORNL, the team's affiliations include Northern Illinois University and Northwestern University. Christina Nunez is a freelance writer and editor who covers science, technology, and innovation at Argonne and other research facilities under the U.S. Department of Energy. Her work also appears at National Geographic and other publications. She has been writing for Argonne since 2018. The Argonne Leadership Computing Facility provides supercomputing and AI capabilities to the scientific and engineering community to advance fundamental discovery and understanding in a broad range of disciplines. Supported by the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE's) Office of Science, Advanced Scientific Computing Research (ASCR) program, the ALCF is one of two DOE Leadership Computing Facilities in the nation dedicated to open science. artigo.texto: MELBOURNE, Australia, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Aeson Power demonstrated the versatility of sodium-ion technology across energy storage and automotive applications at All Energy Australia 2026, held at the Melbourne Convention and Exhibition Centre. At Booth G101, the company presented its latest solutions, highlighting sodium-ion technology's growing role in Australia's energy storage market. Aeson Power's Sodium battery in All-Energy Flexible Sodium-Ion Solutions for Residential Energy Storage A key feature was the APSI2500-based sodium-ion battery system, designed for residential energy storage applications. Combining sodium-ion batteries with Aeson Power's proprietary Ecocase and Ecocab components, the system supports flexible capacity configurations to meet different household energy storage needs. With sodium-ion technology's safety advantages and wide-temperature operating capabilities, the system offers households a flexible energy storage option with safety as a key consideration. Intelligent Energy Storage for Commercial and Industrial Applications Aeson Power also presented the HaloDyne Na 120/119, an all-in-one liquid-cooled sodium-ion energy storage system for commercial and industrial applications. Its sodium-ion chemistry and multi-level fire protection are designed to enhance system safety. With 1C high-rate charging and discharging, the system delivers up to twice the rated power of a comparable 0.5C system with the same battery capacity. This makes it well suited to peak demand management, multi-peak energy arbitrage, and microgrid frequency regulation, where high power output can help reduce the battery capacity needed for specific applications and improve space efficiency. Sodium-Ion Technology for Automotive Starting Applications The exhibition also featured the NaForce sodium-ion starter battery series, demonstrating the growing commercial adoption of sodium-ion technology in the automotive sector. As part of Aeson Power's established product portfolio, NaForce reflects the company's efforts to bring sodium-ion innovation into practical, real-world automotive applications. Together, the three product lines illustrated the versatility of sodium-ion technology, from flexible residential energy storage configurations to integrated commercial energy storage and automotive starting solutions. Through continued product development, Aeson Power aims to deliver reliable performance, safety-conscious design, and flexible integration across evolving energy and automotive markets. Aeson Power's sodium-ion solutions attracted strong interest from visitors at All Energy Australia 2026, prompting engaging discussions with industry professionals throughout the exhibition. About Aeson Power Aeson Power is an Australian pioneer in next-generation battery technology, serving global automotive and energy markets with advanced sodium-ion solutions. Aeson Power designs, develops, and markets high-reliability battery solutions for automotive, energy storage, and more. For more information, visit www.aesonpower.com PR Newswire Asia Ltd. artigo.texto: SUZHOU, China, Nov. 4, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- BloombergNEF (BNEF) has released its Q4 2026 Tier 1 list of global energy storage manufacturers, with LONGi securing its 10th consecutive quarterly listing. The recognition reflects its track record in global project delivery, system integration and commercial execution. LONGi Secures 10th Consecutive BNEF Tier 1 Energy Storage Listing This quarter, BNEF introduced stricter project financing requirements, requiring qualifying projects to secure non-recourse financing from at least two commercial banks. The higher threshold places greater emphasis on project bankability and commercial viability, adding significance to LONGi's continued inclusion. Full-Stack Innovation Strengthens System-Level Capabilities Under its LONGi ONE strategy, LONGi has developed a full-stack, in-house 5S technology platform spanning iCCS, BMS, PCS, TMS and EMS. This enables native system integration and coordinated management across utility-scale, commercial and industrial (C&I), and microgrid applications. By combining proprietary technologies with integrated system design, this approach supports reliable performance and efficient project execution. A unified responsibility framework and Long-Term Service Agreements (LTSA) provide support throughout the project lifecycle. Global Projects Demonstrate Versatility Across Applications LONGi's global projects demonstrate the adaptability of its solutions across diverse power markets, grid requirements and operating environments. In Australia, the 5MW/20MWh Lunio Energy project in South Australia was connected to the grid in September 2026 and entered the National Electricity Market (NEM), enabling participation in electricity market trading. In Germany, a project in Stralsund integrated energy storage with an existing solar-thermal plant, delivering frequency response in under 50 milliseconds to support grid stability and power quality for critical infrastructure. LONGi also demonstrates its capabilities in challenging environments. In Finland, a microgrid solution achieved black start in under two minutes, supporting independent power supply in extreme cold. In coastal Italy, a 50.16MWh storage system integrated with a 35MWp solar plant features comprehensive anti-corrosion protection, maintaining over 99% system availability in high-salt and high-humidity conditions. Advancing Global Energy Storage Capabilities From proprietary technologies and integrated solutions to global project delivery and lifecycle services, LONGi continues to strengthen its capabilities across the energy storage value chain. The launch of its new smart manufacturing base also further enhances manufacturing and delivery capacity for global markets. Looking ahead, LONGi will continue to advance its LONGi ONE strategy, combining full-stack innovation, global project experience, smart manufacturing and localized services to deliver efficient, reliable energy storage solutions and support the global energy transition. artigo.texto: MELBOURNE, Australia, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LONGi Energy Storage showcased its utility-scale, commercial and industrial (C&I), and microgrid solutions at All Energy Australia 2026, demonstrating its integrated capabilities across diverse energy applications. Under its LONGi ONE strategy, LONGi Energy Storage continues to advance technology innovation and localized services to support Australia's energy transition. LONGi Energy Storage at All Energy Australia 2026 Solutions for Diverse Energy Applications As Australia expands renewable energy deployment, energy storage is increasingly important for grid flexibility, energy cost optimization and reliable power supply. OneMatrix Solution addresses utility-scale applications, including renewable energy projects, standalone grid-side storage and electricity market operations. Featuring flexible modular design and LONGiBank 3.0, it supports 2–8-hour duration and customized system configurations. Cluster-level independent management, AI-powered battery health diagnostics and intelligent O&M help improve operational efficiency and support long-term asset performance. The solution has received TÜV Rheinland certifications under IEC 62619, IEC 63056, and an IEC/EN 60730-1 Annex H report, reinforcing its safety credentials for international markets. Hi-MO One Pro supports C&I applications with flexible 2-24-hour configurations for solar-plus-storage, peak-valley arbitrage, and backup power. Featuring LONGi's proprietary iCCS and liquid-cooling technology, it supports grid-connected and off-grid operation, helping businesses optimize energy costs and enhance power supply security. OneNexus H2 and M5 serve remote areas, mining operations and other locations with limited grid access. By coordinating solar, battery storage and diesel generation, they help increase renewable energy utilization, reduce diesel dependence and strengthen power supply resilience. Project Experience Demonstrates Local Market Value In Strathalbyn, South Australia, the Lunio Energy BESS project was connected to the grid in September 2026. Comprising four LONGiBank 2.0 systems with a total capacity of 5 MW/20 MWh, the project participates in Australia's National Electricity Market (NEM), optimizing charging and discharging in response to electricity demand and market prices. Advancing LONGi ONE Through Localized Services LONGi continues to integrate proprietary technologies, system solutions and intelligent O&M under its LONGi ONE strategy, providing support from solution design and delivery through lifecycle operations. Through its "2830 Plan," LONGi aims to establish 30 comprehensive local service centers worldwide by the end of 2028, strengthening local responsiveness and lifecycle support. With its full-stack capabilities, diverse solution portfolio and expanding local service network, LONGi Energy Storage will continue working with Australian customers and partners to deliver flexible, reliable and sustainable energy solutions. artigo.texto: Abstract Decarbonizing agriculture without compromising productivity is a major challenge under rising input costs and labor scarcity. Autonomous battery-powered agricultural robots (ABARs) could help by reducing dependence on conventional machinery and enabling more precise application of inputs, but their system-level economic and environmental performance remains unclear. Here, we integrate total cost of ownership and life cycle assessment to evaluate a small ABAR for cradle-to-farm-gate crop production of strawberries, onions, lettuce, and peanuts under organic and non-organic management. Across modeled scenarios, benchmarked costs range from 76% below to 17% above literature-based reference ranges, while greenhouse-gas emissions fall within or below reported ranges. Variable inputs dominate both outcomes, contributing 72–90% of costs and 72–95% of global-warming impacts, with seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation water as main drivers. These results suggest that ABAR value depends less on the platform than on the ability of autonomous operation to reduce input use and labor demand. Similar content being viewed by others Introduction Agriculture faces growing pressure to increase output while reducing emissions and resource use. Food systems account for more than one-fifth of global greenhouse gas emissions1, while agricultural production is increasingly constrained by climate change, soil degradation, and rising and uncertain input costs, particularly in energy and fertilizer markets2,3. At the same time, demand for agricultural products is projected to rise by up to 50% until 20504. Meeting this challenge is central to several United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), including zero hunger (SDG 2), responsible consumption and production (SDG 12), and climate action (SDG 13)5,6, and is increasingly framed as part of broader efforts to keep food production within planetary and resource boundaries7,8,9,10. Against this backdrop, digital and automated technologies are progressively being advanced as routes to more resource-efficient agriculture11,12,13. Autonomous agricultural robots, in particular, could improve safety, reduce labor requirements, and apply inputs more precisely than conventional machinery, with potential benefits for both costs and environmental impacts13,14,15,16. Rapid advances in battery-electric propulsion, charging concepts, and artificial intelligence (AI) have accelerated their technical development17,18,19. Yet, it remains unclear under which conditions these systems deliver meaningful economic and environmental gains. Their deployment depends not only on technical feasibility, but also on reliability, maintenance, charging logistics, infrastructure, regulation, safety, and operator capabilities18,20. Among these emerging systems, autonomous battery-powered agricultural robots (ABARs) are especially relevant for small to medium-sized farms and for crops in which irrigation, fertilization, and weed control remain important drivers of costs and emissions. By combining compact electric platforms with sensors and automated control, ABARs may complement or replace conventional machinery in selected field operations while enabling more targeted application of water and agrochemicals. Like other clean technologies at an early stage of development, ABARs still face technical, operational, and regulatory challenges. Their potential to reduce both greenhouse gas emissions and production costs, therefore, needs to be assessed at the crop-system level. Evidence to date remains fragmented. Existing studies have assessed specific robots, regions, or individual operations, or have focused on either environmental or economic performance in isolation20,21,22,23,24. As a result, ABARs remain insufficiently characterized at the crop-production-system level when environmental and economic outcomes are evaluated together within a single, consistent framework spanning multiple field operations. Here, we develop a parameterized ABAR model and integrate comprehensive life cycle assessment (LCA) and total cost of ownership (TCO) for cradle-to-farm-gate production of strawberries, onions, lettuce, and peanuts under organic and non-organic management. The model includes simplified tool and module proxies for preparation, sowing, mechanical and chemical weed control, irrigation, and fertilization, which together define the cradle-to-farm-gate system boundary summarized in Fig. 1. Harvesting is excluded from the ABAR platform model because harvesting technologies, labor requirements, and mechanization levels are strongly crop-specific and, for several of the crops considered, remain partly manual25,26,27,28. We quantify costs and greenhouse-gas emissions per kilogram of crop and benchmark against reported ranges for conventional systems. This framework allows us to identify where ABARs may already be competitive, where their performance remains constrained, and whether their benefits arise primarily from the robot platform itself or from reductions in variable inputs and labor demand. Results Model of the automated farming robot The ABAR model in this study reflects recent industrial autonomous farming robots29,30, but is intended as a simplified, parameterized representation rather than a one-to-one model of any specific product (Fig. 2). Its dimensions (0.85 meters (m) × 0.70 m × 0.70 m; Length × Width × Height) are based on an existing compact ABAR platform29 to anchor the geometry, while the included components, their sizing, and the operational parameterization were defined for this study based on the assumptions described in “Methods”. The robot runs on wheels and incorporates a battery-electric drivetrain sized for high-power operations such as field preparation. Onboard perception and positioning are provided by a camera, global positioning system (GPS), and lidar (light detection and ranging), with embedded computing, enabling autonomous control. artigo.texto: Graphene batteries have earned a reputation as a promising material for improving battery performance. Its remarkable electrical conductivity, enormous surface area, and ability to distribute heat make it attractive for batteries and supercapacitors. Meanwhile, rare earth elements are better known for powering electric motors, wind turbines, and industrial equipment through their magnetic properties. At first glance, the two have little in common. Graphene is a form of carbon, while rare earths are a group of 17 metallic elements. They perform different functions, and rare earths are not generally necessary ingredients in graphene-enhanced lithium-ion batteries. But researchers are discovering something more interesting than an indirect connection through manufacturing equipment: certain rare earth compounds can work directly with graphene to improve experimental energy-storage electrodes. Studies published in 2025 and 2026 suggest that combining graphene derivatives with rare earth oxides may help address limitations in conductivity, charge storage, and cycling stability. The research is still developing, but it raises an intriguing question: Could two seemingly unrelated materials become partners in next-generation energy storage? Table of Contents Different Materials, Complementary Strengths A conventional lithium-ion battery stores and releases energy through the movement of lithium ions between electrodes. Its performance depends heavily on electrode chemistry, conductivity, ion transport, and thermal stability. A graphene battery can help address some of those challenges. Composed of carbon atoms arranged in a single-atom-thick honeycomb lattice, graphene has excellent electrical conductivity and a large theoretical surface area. In practical energy-storage applications, graphene-related materials can serve as conductive additives, protective coatings, or structural components in composite electrodes. Rare earth compounds offer different advantages. Certain rare earth oxides, particularly cerium oxide (CeO₂), exhibit useful electrochemical properties associated with their ability to participate in oxidation-reduction reactions. These reactions can contribute to charge storage in specially designed electrodes. However, metal oxides can suffer from limited electrical conductivity or other material constraints. This is where graphene becomes interesting. By incorporating rare earth oxide particles into graphene-based structures, researchers can potentially combine the electrochemical activity of the oxide with the electrical and structural advantages of the carbon material. Rather than competing for the same function, the two materials may compensate for each other's weaknesses. Cerium and Graphene: A Partnership Taking Shape One of the clearest examples appeared in a May 2025 study published in the Journal of Colloid and Interface Science. Researchers developed a composite consisting of cerium oxide nanoparticles distributed across graphene oxide nanosheets. They tested the material as a battery-type cathode for a supercapacitor. The distinction matters. A battery-type electrode uses electrochemical reactions that resemble aspects of battery charge storage, but the complete device in this study was a supercapacitor, not a conventional lithium-ion battery. The researchers found that combining redox-active cerium oxide with graphene oxide produced favorable electrochemical behavior, including low ion-diffusion resistance and promising cycling stability. The findings demonstrated how a rare earth compound and a graphene derivative could complement one another within the same electrode. The study, Cerium Oxide Nanoparticles Decorated on Graphene Oxide Nanosheets as Battery-Type Cathode Material for Supercapacitors (opens in a new tab), provides a direct experimental connection between rare earth materials and graphene-based energy storage. More recently, a May 2026 study in Solid State Sciences investigated composites combining multiple rare earth oxides with reduced graphene oxide. Its optimized electrode material achieved a reported specific capacitance of 1,598 farads per gram at a current density of 1 ampere per gram. That result is encouraging, although it describes electrode performance under specified experimental conditions. It cannot be interpreted as the energy-storage capacity of a commercially available battery. Together, these studies suggest that rare earth–graphene combinations deserve further investigation, particularly in supercapacitors and hybrid energy-storage systems. Batteries and Supercapacitors: Where Could the Partnership Matter? Batteries and supercapacitors both store electrical energy, but they excel at different tasks. Lithium-ion batteries generally provide greater energy storage for their size or weight, making them useful when sustained operation matters. Supercapacitors typically charge and discharge much faster and tolerate large numbers of cycles, but store less energy. Researchers are investigating hybrid devices that combine different charge-storage mechanisms to improve the balance between energy density, power delivery, and durability. Graphene-based materials are promising in this field because they can support rapid electron transport and provide accessible surfaces for charge storage. Rare earth oxides could contribute additional electrochemical activity, depending on the particular compound and electrode design. Potential applications include regenerative braking, industrial power systems, and equipment requiring rapid bursts of electricity. However, the technology faces several hurdles before commercial adoption. Researchers must demonstrate that promising electrode-level performance translates into complete, practical devices. They must also address manufacturing costs, material consistency, long-term stability, and scalability. artigo.texto: The International Flow Battery Forum (IFBF) has opened its call for papers and presentation proposals for its 2027 conference in Barcelona, Spain. The 18th edition of the forum will take place at the Barceló Sants Hotel on 22–24 June 2027, with online access available for remote delegates. Proposals must be submitted by 15 January 2027. IFBF is inviting proposals for presentations, keynote addresses, interviews, panel discussions and posters covering the latest commercial and technical developments in flow batteries. Suggested subjects include regulation and legislation, project bankability, manufacturing methods, materials and component supply chains, new applications and measures to improve battery performance, reliability and cost. The organiser is also seeking contributions examining how research can translate into operational improvements and commercially viable flow battery projects. Speakers will be asked for a standalone paper for inclusion in the IFBF Book of Papers All selected presenters will be expected to attend the conference in Barcelona. Speakers will also be asked to prepare a short standalone paper for inclusion in the IFBF Book of Papers. Proposals are being accepted through the Oxford Abstracts submission portal. The conference language will be English. IFBF said it expects the event to attract more than 300 delegates, over 50 speakers, at least 25 exhibition stands and more than 50 poster presentations. The programme is intended to bring together battery manufacturers and developers with utilities, grid operators, investors, researchers and potential customers for long-duration energy storage. BEST reported from IFBF 2026 in Budapest that the sector was moving into a scale-up phase, although access to finance, supportive regulation and dependable supply chains remained significant challenges.

artigo.texto: From January to September this year, the volume of batteries used in electric, plug-in hybrid, and hybrid vehicles registered globally reached 994.5 GWh, a 19.7% increase compared to the same period last year. While the combined market share of seven Chinese companies rose to 73.0%, the combined share of the three domestic firms—LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI, and SK On—fell to 12.6%. Battery usage at 994.5 GWh According to SNE Research, an energy market research firm, on the 2nd, global battery usage from January to September 2026 was recorded at 994.5 GWh. The data covers batteries installed in pure electric vehicles (EVs) as well as plug-in hybrid vehicles (PHEVs) and hybrid vehicles (HEVs). Usage in September alone reached 145.1 GWh, setting a monthly record. However, the growth rate compared to the same month last year was 15.8%, down from 18.3% in August, indicating a slight slowdown in monthly growth momentum. Chinese firms' market share reaches 73% The combined market share of seven Chinese battery manufacturers rose to 73.0%, up 3.5 percentage points from a year ago. Conversely, the combined share of the three Korean companies—LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI, and SK On—fell to 12.6%, a decrease of 4.1 percentage points. By company, China's CATL maintained the top spot with 81.9 GWh in usage. This represents a 24.9% increase from the same period last year, and its market share expanded from 37.5% to 39.1%, driven by increased supply to overseas automakers. BYD ranked second with 150.9 GWh. Its usage grew by 7.4%, but because this fell short of the overall market growth rate, its market share dipped from 16.9% to 15.2%. The combined market share of CATL and BYD reached approximately 54%.

artigo.texto: LG CNS has secured lease agreements for 100% of its artificial intelligence (AI) data center capacity in Indonesia ahead of completion. Meanwhile, the company said it would invest gradually in its graphics processing unit (GPU) services business after assessing demand and commercial viability. During its third-quarter earnings conference call on Oct. 30, LG CNS announced that its AI data center in Jakarta, Indonesia, is scheduled for completion in early November. The company added that the facility has already secured tenants for its entire capacity. “We secured customers to lease the entire facility before completion, establishing a stable revenue base from the start of operations,” said Yoo Ki-woong, vice president of LG CNS’ AI and Cloud Business Division, during the conference call. He explained that the company is pursuing additional data center construction projects in Indonesia and exploring expansion into North America and Europe. The Indonesian data center is LG CNS’ first overseas AI data center construction project. In 2024, the company signed a data center consulting and design contract with local operator KMG. It subsequently secured a 100 billion won infrastructure construction contract in August 2025. KMG is a joint venture established by Indonesia’s Sinar Mas Group and Korea Investment Real Asset Management. LG CNS participated in the project through LG Sinar Mas Technology Solutions, its joint venture with Sinar Mas Group. The first-phase data center has 11 above-ground floors, a total floor area of 46,281 square meters and a power intake capacity of 30 megawatts (MW). It can accommodate more than 100,000 servers. Project owner KMG plans to expand total power intake capacity to 220 MW. In North America and Europe, LG CNS plans to focus on prefabricated modular data centers. “We are pursuing business cooperation through our U.S. subsidiary and local partners,” Yoo said. “We plan to enter the market using modular data center technology designed to support Nvidia’s next-generation AI platform, Vera Rubin.” According to the company, the modular approach reduces on-site construction work compared with conventional methods and allows facilities to be expanded in stages according to customer demand. However, LG CNS intends to manage investment risks in its GPU services business separately from its broader AI infrastructure expansion. LG CNS chief financial officer (CFO) Song Kwang-ryun expressed a positive view of the medium- to long-term growth potential of GPU-as-a-Service (GPUaaS) during the conference call. He said the company is reviewing business opportunities involving LG Group affiliates and external enterprises but must consider the substantial upfront investment costs and rapid pace of technological change. “We will proceed cautiously, focusing on projects with established commercial viability,” Song said of future investments. LG CNS previously decided at a Sept. 11 board meeting to invest 381.4 billion won in GPUs and infrastructure equipment, including Nvidia’s Vera Rubin. The equipment acquisition is scheduled for June 30, 2027. The company appears to intend to determine the scale of future GPUaaS investments based on actual demand and profitability, separately from the GPU investment already approved. GPUs require substantial upfront capital, and rapid equipment replacement cycles mean customer acquisition and utilization rates can significantly affect investment returns. Meanwhile, AI and cloud revenue reached 961.5 billion won in the third quarter, accounting for 57.8% of LG CNS’ total revenue of 1.6643 trillion won.

artigo.texto: Dongwha Electrolyte, a subsidiary of Dongwha Enterprise, will participate in a 130 billion won next-generation battery research project. The company will focus on developing electrolytes for sodium-ion batteries and establishing quality standards for the technology. Dongwha Electrolyte said November 3 that it would join the Market-Leading Next-Generation Battery Innovation Strategy Research Group (K-BIC). It is the only electrolyte manufacturer among the participating organizations. K-BIC is part of the Global TOP Strategic Research Group support program, jointly promoted by the Ministry of Science and ICT and the National Research Council of Science and Technology. The project has a total budget of 130 billion won and aims to secure fundamental technologies for next-generation batteries and accelerate their commercialization. Dongwha Electrolyte will participate in the second phase of the research project titled "Development of Ultra-Low-Cost, Long-Life Non-Lithium Batteries," led by the Korea Institute of Energy Research. The project aims to develop low-cost sodium-ion batteries priced at less than $50 per kilowatt-hour (kWh). The company will be responsible for electrolyte manufacturing and supply, defining key quality characteristics and establishing quality standards. The research group will expand its scope beyond conventional materials development to include cell development, the expansion of mass-production processes and safety validation. Kim Jong-hoon, CEO of Dongwha Electrolyte, said, "We will secure sodium-ion battery materials technologies that address the needs of the energy storage system (ESS) industry and expand our portfolio of next-generation products."

artigo.texto: Hyosung Goodsprings, a pump manufacturing subsidiary of Hyosung Group, will supply high-efficiency cooling pumps for SK Telecom’s (SKT) artificial intelligence (AI) data center in Ulsan. The pumps reduce power consumption by regulating the circulation of cooling water used to dissipate heat generated by servers. The company has secured orders covering the Ulsan data center’s 100-megawatt (MW) capacity. With SKT planning to expand its domestic AI data center capacity to 15 gigawatts (GW) by 2035, Hyosung Goodsprings’ cooling pump shipments are expected to increase further. According to industry sources on Nov. 4, Hyosung Goodsprings has secured contracts to supply sensorless inline pumps for both the 40MW first-phase facility (Building A) and the 60MW second-phase facility (Building B) at SKT’s Ulsan AI data center. Sensorless inline pumps automatically adjust motor speeds according to server cooling loads. They operate at higher speeds when cooling demand increases and slow down when demand decreases. This eliminates the need to operate continuously at maximum output, reducing unnecessary power consumption. The pumps also control operating conditions without separate flow sensors, simplifying equipment configuration and maintenance. The integrated inverters are supplied by ABB, a Swedish-Swiss power technology company. Hyosung Goodsprings has also added a total harmonic distortion (THD) monitoring function to its sensorless inline pumps. THD measures the extent to which an electrical waveform deviates from its normal shape. The function allows operators to monitor electrical conditions without separate measuring equipment, simplifying facility management. The number of cooling pumps required increases with a data center’s power capacity. A 40MW data center typically requires about 20 to 30 pumps. Applying the same standard, SKT’s 100MW Ulsan data center would need more than 50 pumps. With a set of pumps for a 40MW facility costing approximately 1.5 billion won, the total supply value for the 100MW Ulsan data center is estimated at around 4 billion won. AI data centers generate substantial heat by operating large numbers of servers equipped with high-performance graphics processing units (GPUs). Server overheating can degrade computing performance or cause equipment failures, making cooling systems essential. Data center cooling systems operate by using cooling water to absorb heat generated by servers and release it outside the facility. Cooling pumps circulate the water through pipes and maintain the required flow rate. With cooling systems accounting for approximately 40% of a facility’s total energy consumption, pump efficiency plays an important role in reducing operating costs. SKT plans to expand its domestic AI data center investments, starting with Ulsan. The company intends to establish AI data center clusters with capacities exceeding 2GW in the Yeongnam region and 1GW in the southwestern region, before gradually expanding domestic capacity to 5GW starting in 2029. Its goal is to reach 15GW by 2035. Applying the same cooling equipment requirements, the total demand for pumps could reach approximately 600 billion won. Hyosung Goodsprings could see substantial revenue growth if it secures additional orders for SKT’s future data centers. The company’s revenue declined slightly to 230.1 billion won last year from 236.3 billion won a year earlier. Operating profit, however, increased approximately 48% to 20.9 billion won from 14.2 billion won over the same period. Hyosung Goodsprings has also secured several domestic data center operators as customers beyond SKT. The company supplies cooling pumps to facilities including the 35MW Deogi-dong Internet Data Center (IDC) in Ilsan, the 80MW GPC IDC in Hwaseong, the 50MW TIMBUKTU IDC in Ansan and the 25MW Global Cloud Center (GCC) IDC in Ansan. Hyosung Goodsprings is an unlisted, wholly owned subsidiary of Hyosung specializing in industrial pump manufacturing. In addition to cooling pumps for data centers, it produces large industrial pumps for oil refining, petrochemical facilities and power plants, as well as pumps for nuclear power plants. Major customers include ExxonMobil and Aramco.

artigo.texto: Sunwoda Solid-State Battery Survives 200°C Heat Test Without Fire Sunwoda solid-state battery: the 20 Ah Xin Bixiao cell passed a 200°C hot-box test with 400 Wh/kg and 1,200+ cycles, now in carmaker testing. Published 2 min read Chinese battery maker Sunwoda says its 20 Ah Xin Bixiao solid-state cell did not catch fire or explode when heated to 200°C (392°F) in a hot-box safety test. The Sunwoda solid-state battery also reaches more than 400 Wh/kg and over 1,200 charge cycles, figures the company links to electric cars with a range above 1,000 km (about 620 miles). The update came from Sunwoda Electric Vehicle Battery (SEVB), the group’s automotive unit, in an October 30 reply on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange investor platform. SEVB said the cell has completed design and process verification and is still being evaluated by carmakers, which it did not name. As CarNewsChina notes, customer testing first started in May 2026. How the Sunwoda Solid-State Battery Is Built Xin Bixiao uses a polymer-composite electrolyte instead of the sulfide chemistry that rivals such as CATL are pursuing. The cell combines a 12-micron polymer-composite membrane with a nanoscale high-entropy silicon anode, and Sunwoda says it reaches its cycle life at an external pressure below 1 MPa. That low pressure matters. Solid electrolytes can lose contact with the electrodes as materials swell and shrink during charging, so some sulfide designs need constant clamping force inside the pack. Sulfide materials also react with moisture and can release toxic hydrogen sulfide, which makes factories harder to run. After 1,200 cycles the cell keeps more than 80% of its original capacity. Sunwoda estimates that would cover more than a decade of use for a driver who covers about 20,000 km (12,400 miles) a year. Results Are for One Cell, Not a Car The important caveat is scale. The heat, energy density and lifespan figures come from a single cell, not a full battery pack installed in a vehicle, and Interesting Engineering points out that the company has not committed to a launch date for its high-density cells. Earlier lab results, such as a NASA solid-state battery built for extreme cold, show how long the path from cell to product can be. Production is also small for now. SEVB has connected a pilot line with an annual design capacity of 0.2 GWh, enough for roughly 2,600 to 2,700 electric cars a year. Its roadmap lists a second-generation sulfide battery for 2027 and a cell above 500 Wh/kg for 2030, both still development targets. What It Means for the EV Battery Race CATL, the world’s largest EV battery maker, reaffirmed on October 27 that it aims for small-batch production of sulfide solid-state cells in 2027. Sunwoda’s polymer route gives carmakers a second option, at a time when many Chinese automakers are losing money and looking for any edge on range and safety. Sunwoda is also working on cells of at least 450 Wh/kg for electric aircraft (eVTOL) that can deliver 1,000 W/kg of continuous power, alongside a fast-charging LFP pack that goes from 10% to 70% in about five minutes. Other chemistries are moving too, including a sodium metal battery that keeps 90% capacity after 1,000 cycles. For buyers, solid-state cars with these specs are still years away, but the safety data is a step in the right direction.

artigo.texto: 'KODEX All Solid State Battery ESS TOP2 Plus' ETF Surpasses KRW 300 Billion in Net Assets Nearly KRW 200 billion increase over the past month Investing across the ESS value chain and all-solid-state batteries Three-month return of 22.2%, the highest among peers Samsung Asset Management said on November 3 that its KODEX All Solid State Battery ESS TOP2 Plus exchange-traded fund (ETF) surpassed KRW 300 billion in net assets, reaching KRW 334.2 billion. Since the product was listed on June 23, cumulative net purchases by individual investors have reached KRW 76.7 billion, including KRW 24.4 billion in net purchases over the past month alone. As a result, net assets increased by nearly KRW 200 billion over the past month, the largest increase among domestic equity ETFs. The fund is believed to have continued attracting inflows on the back of a clear recovery in earnings at its key holdings and the medium- to long-term growth prospects of the ESS and all-solid-state battery industries. It also posted a 22.2% return over the past three months, ranking first among ETFs in similar categories, including secondary batteries and all-solid-state batteries. The ETF invests about 50% of its assets in two leading domestic battery cell makers, Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solution. Strong third-quarter results recently announced by both companies, along with their success in securing global orders, have further enhanced their investment appeal. Samsung SDI returned to profitability in the third quarter of this year, posting revenue of KRW 4.6856 trillion and operating profit of KRW 407.8 billion, driven by increased sales of ESS and battery backup units (BBUs) for AI data centers. LG Energy Solution also reported a marked improvement in results, with preliminary third-quarter revenue of KRW 9.6434 trillion, up 59.0%, and operating profit of KRW 756 billion, up 25.7%. The remaining approximately 50% of the portfolio is invested across ESS component and equipment makers and all-solid-state battery materials companies, aiming to capture supply-chain spillover benefits from increased orders for major cell makers. It holds ESS value-chain companies such as Sangsin EDP, HanJung NCS, Seojin System, and SFA Nexel, which are positioned to benefit from expanded mass production and capital investment. In the all-solid-state battery sector, it also holds key materials companies including ISU Specialty Chemical, Daejoo Electronic Materials, LOTTE Energy Materials, POSCO Future M, and L&F. artigo.texto: HERMANTOWN, Minn. (KQDS-TV) -- Hermantown’s City Council unanimously approved of Google’s proposed Data Center at a special meeting held on October 30. For the first time the council limited access to the council chamber halls, only allowing the first 85 people a chance to give public comment. The meeting was originally held on Monday, October 26, but was rescheduled after Hermantown Residents and members with Stop the Hermantown Data Center (SHDC) chanted “Let them speak” delaying council proceedings. Just minutes before doors opened to the media and the public on Friday, SHDC held a press conference expressing their concerns on how the council handled the process. “Corporate money and greed has divided us into an us versus them, red versus green mentality that doesn’t actually exist. We stand with you in support of local jobs and fair wages to provide your families and your home, just not at the expense of ours,” said Sarah Lofald, the Vice President of SHDC. “Not based on government secrecy, lies, corruption, deceit, and corporate greed. Hundreds of citizens have flooded city emails inboxes, demanding that officials deny further permitting, relocate meetings to a larger venue, accommodate residents with disabilities or limited internet access, and halt the data center project altogether.” Inside the chamber halls, 60 people spoke during the council’s 4-hour long public comment period that started at 6:30 p.m. 55 people spoke in opposition to, with only 5 openly siding with Google. People who did not speak before the council were able to give someone else an extra 3 minutes to address the council. One Hermantown Resident in support of the project highlighted the opportunities to learn more about Google’s technology through their open houses and council proceedings. “This agreement demonstrates to me personally that Google wants to be a responsible and good neighbor,” said Eric Palmer. “Related investments and jobs are here for the long term. This is in addition to the economic benefits and increased tax revenue to help support the city and school.” Another resident asked the council to consider the overwhelming, continual turnout of residents and community members opposing the project when casting their vote. “This is the point where I’d like to remind you that representative democracy only works when you, the representatives, actually represent your constituents, the majority of your constituents,” said Sarah Winter. Hermantown Mayor Wanye Boucher asked multiple times for those within the chamber halls to keep their cheers to a minimum or else restrict the number of people able to speak. Three people were escorted out refusing to leave the podium after their 3 minutes were up. Meanwhile outside city hall, dozens of community members and tribal members waited outside, anxiously awaiting the council’s decision. The beat of drums helps keep the crowd in unison as they chant, “Shut it down.” “I have all the same concerns that everyone else does about the Data Center: water pollution, energy usage, direct quality of life impacts for those living nearby with sound emissions,” said Hermantown Resident Amelia Cohoes. “With Google masking their identities, signing NDAs, working in secret with the council. It just feels like a direct slap to the face to the democratic ideals that I believe in.” The council spent over an hour going over each of the 6 agenda items. The council voted unanimously on each item, officially moving the Google Data Center across the finish line. “There was a lot of hope that maybe the city would listen to its people by restricting the number of us people who could be in the chamber,” said Lofald. “It was pretty easy to see that they really didn’t want to listen to us.” After Friday's meeting, members from the Duluth Building Trades Council and the Hermantown Area Chamber of Commerce released statements in supports of the council's decision. “We want to thank the City Council for its thoughtful consideration and for having the courage to make this important decision,” said Jack Carlson, President of the DuluthBuilding Trades Council. “This project creates opportunities for skilled workers, local businesses, and families throughout our region. Now it's time to get to work and begin realizing those benefits.” “This is an exciting moment for Hermantown and our region. The project before the City Council today is stronger because of the input provided by residents, community leaders, and state agencies throughout the process. We believe this investment will create meaningful opportunities for our workforce, businesses, schools, and community for generations to come,” said Kim Parmeter, President and CEO of the Hermantown Area Chamber of Commerce. “We also recognize that projects of this scale bring real concerns, particularly for nearby neighbors. Those concerns deserve continued respect and attention as the project moves forward. While no major investment comes without trade-offs, we believe the long-term benefits for our community and region make this an opportunity worth embracing,” said Parmeter.

artigo.texto: Prefeito de Nova York critica avanço dos data centers de IA em meio às eleições: "Nosso risco, recompensa deles" Zohran Mamdani afirma que resistência à construção de data centers une democratas e republicanos e alerta para os custos ambientais e econômicos da inteligência artificial Atualizado A expansão dos data centers para sustentar o avanço da inteligência artificial se tornou um dos temas de debate nas eleições de meio de mandato dos Estados Unidos, realizadas nesta terça-feira (3). Às vésperas da votação, o prefeito de Nova York, Zohran Mamdani, afirmou que a crescente oposição à construção dessas instalações representa um raro ponto de convergência entre democratas e republicanos, preocupados com os impactos da tecnologia sobre o consumo de energia, as tarifas de eletricidade e o meio ambiente. Em entrevista à revista Wired, publicada nesta terça-feira, Mamdani afirmou que a resistência aos data centers lhe dá esperança justamente por ultrapassar as tradicionais divisões políticas americanas. "Eu e Ron DeSantis não temos muita coisa em comum, mas existe uma oposição semelhante ao desenvolvimento desse tipo de data center", disse, em referência ao governador republicano da Flórida. Para o prefeito, a insatisfação reflete uma preocupação crescente com os custos da infraestrutura necessária para alimentar os sistemas de IA. "O que estamos vendo é uma oposição ao que esses data centers significariam para a vida cotidiana das pessoas, para suas contas de eletricidade e para o meio ambiente", afirmou. Mamdani, que já manifestou apoio a uma suspensão de um ano na construção de novos data centers no estado de Nova York, também criticou a falta de transparência das empresas de tecnologia sobre o consumo energético de seus sistemas. Segundo ele, a escassez de informações dificulta avaliar os custos reais da inteligência artificial para a sociedade. O prefeito resumiu sua crítica à política adotada para o setor nos últimos anos com uma expressão: "Nosso risco, a recompensa deles". Na avaliação de Mamdani, a população acaba exposta aos impactos da expansão da IA, enquanto os benefícios econômicos ficam concentrados nas empresas responsáveis pela tecnologia. As críticas também se estendem à sustentabilidade financeira da corrida pela inteligência artificial. Questionado sobre a possibilidade de o setor estar vivendo uma bolha, Mamdani respondeu afirmativamente e comparou o atual momento da indústria à bolha imobiliária que antecedeu a crise financeira de 2008. O prefeito ainda questionou a capacidade das próprias empresas de tecnologia de estabelecer limites para o setor. Ao ser perguntado se confiava em executivos como Sam Altman, CEO da OpenAI, respondeu simplesmente: "Não". Para Mamdani, o avanço da inteligência artificial exige uma resposta mais firme do poder público, especialmente diante do que considera uma ausência de regulação adequada em nível federal.

artigo.texto: Google deu um passo importante rumo aos data centers espaciais: acaba de executar IA em órbita Com o Project Suncatcher, a gigante das buscas deu início aos testes para operar seus próprios chips de inteligência artificial diretamente no espaço O Google deu um passo rumo aos data centers espaciais ao executar com sucesso um modelo de IA em órbita. Por meio do Project Suncatcher, em parceria com a Planet e a SpaceX, a empresa utilizou um chip TPU em um satélite para rodar o modelo Gemma e gerar uma resposta enviada à Terra. O teste pioneiro valida a viabilidade técnica de transferir o processamento de inteligência artificial para o espaço, aliviando a infraestrutura terrestre de alto consumo de energia e resfriamento contínuo. Nós nos acostumamos a utilizar a inteligência artificial em tarefas cotidianas, como tirar dúvidas rápidas ou traduzir um texto. Fazemos isso diretamente do celular ou do computador, quase sem pensar na colossal infraestrutura que viabiliza cada uma dessas respostas. Por trás dessa facilidade aparente, opera uma cadeia física complexa que exige energia constante, resfriamento robusto e conectividade contínua. Enquanto essa capacidade se expande em solo terrestre, surge um novo horizonte computacional: transferir parte dessa carga de processamento para o espaço. O Google deu um primeiro passo concreto nessa direção. Em 30 de outubro, a empresa anunciou ter recebido, diretamente da órbita da Terra, uma resposta gerada pelo seu modelo aberto Gemma 4 por meio de uma unidade de processamento neural (TPU) — um chip dedicado com especificações de data center. O satélite, desenvolvido em parceria com a Planet e lançado em 1º de outubro em uma missão da SpaceX, integra o Project Suncatcher, programa voltado a pesquisas em computação orbital. Embora ainda não represente um data center espacial em pleno funcionamento, a validação técnica cumpriu seu papel: solicitou-se à IA a criação de um haikai temático sobre o cosmos. Durante uma janela de comunicação com a estação em solo, a equipe enviou o comando: escrever um haikai sobre a experiência no espaço. O haikai é um poema curto tradicional de origem japonesa, estruturado em três versos. A resposta foi transmitida quando o satélite ... artigo.texto: CATL Lays Out Solid-State Timetable as Australian Storage Launch and Hungary Court Win Broaden Its Base Published on 11/01/2026 at 18:40 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL has told investors it expects to turn out fully solid-state batteries in small production runs by 2027, a disclosure made on the interactive platform of the Shenzhen Stock Exchange on Tuesday. The company was careful to frame the target as small-series output rather than mass manufacturing, and stressed that it remains committed to research and development in the technology. The solid-state roadmap sits alongside an unusually busy stretch of partnership announcements. On 19 October, CATL agreed with Yinwang Intelligent Technologies and its battery-swapping subsidiary to build an intelligent system for exchanging electric-vehicle batteries. Three days later, on 22 October, it signed a deeper cooperation agreement with Beijing Automotive Group covering a swap system that, according to The Business Times, is designed to serve one million vehicles. BAIC will bring compatible models into CATL's Choco-Swap network, and its dealer network will help roll out the swapping stations. Heavy Trucks Get Their Own Platform Commercial vehicles are a separate front. CATL unveiled its Tianxing II battery platform for heavy trucks on 20 October; the company says its Qiji system can swap a truck battery in roughly five minutes. The build-out targets are ambitious: 900 heavy-truck swap stations in China by the end of 2026, 2,000 by 2027, and 10,000 over the longer term. A further agreement on 21 October with Shaanxi Transportation Holding Group covers swap infrastructure for heavy trucks as well as solar installations with storage and charging equipment along motorways, plus services spanning the battery life cycle and recycling. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? TENER+ Makes Its Debut in Australia Away from swapping, CATL introduced its TENER+ energy storage system, with 9 MWh of capacity, globally on Thursday at All Energy Australia. Media reports said the company also signed letters of intent at the show with Hitachi Energy, EPEC Group and UNSW Sydney to support large battery storage projects in Australia. In Hungary, a court on Friday dismissed a lawsuit brought by residents against the Debrecen battery plant, according to Reuters. The residents were no longer entitled to sue after the permitting documents were revised, and the court found no procedural irregularities in the approval process. The ruling removes a legal burden less than a month after trial production began. Revenue Outpaces Earnings The quarter's figures show top-line momentum running well ahead of the bottom line. Revenue for the third quarter of 2026 came in at RMB 165.22 billion, up 58.6% year on year. Net profit attributable to shareholders reached RMB 21.25 billion, a gain of 14.5% — leaving profit growth trailing revenue growth by a wide margin. artigo.texto: FILE PHOTO: A smartphone with a displayed AMD logo is placed on a computer motherboard in this illustration taken March 6, 2023. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/ File Photo Nov 4 (Reuters) - Advanced Micro Devices rose 7.3% in premarket trading after the US chipmaker forecast faster growth through 2027, reassuring investors that demand for AI infrastructure remains strong. AMD, which recently joined the ranks of trillion-dollar companies, has gained about 126% this year and is poised to add about $58 billion in market value if premarket gains hold. The company's strong outlook highlighted growing momentum in its server processor business, signaling that spending on AI computing was extending beyond Nvidia's accelerators, which dominate the market. "We see demand across the data-center business, across our CPU business, as well as our data-center AI business," CEO Lisa Su said, adding the company had been preparing for that growth for several years. Su said on Tuesday that the company expects overall revenue to rise more than 80% in 2027, which is higher than the 77% growth analysts estimate, according to LSEG data. AMD's product roadmap and expanding software ecosystem position it to capture a meaningful share of the AI market, while strengthening its role as the leading alternative to Nvidia and supporting further gains in server CPUs, said analysts at TD Cowen. Last week, rival Intel's shares plunged more than 20% after the company reported weak PC demand, fueling concerns about its reliance on the PC market and relatively limited exposure to AI. Analysts at Morgan Stanley are cautious about assuming current growth in the CPU server business will continue indefinitely amid an industry-wide shortage, but they believe AMD is executing better than competitors and could continue to capture a larger share of the market. The company's third-quarter data-center revenue jumped 97% to $8.55 billion, topping analysts' expectations of $8.20 billion. The Santa Clara, California-based company trades at about 31 times forward earnings, compared with 14 times for Nvidia and 16.5 times for Broadcom. (Reporting by Kanishka Ajmera in Bengaluru; Editing by Shinjini Ganguli)

artigo.texto: Core Scientific currently faces pending air quality enforcement from the state for alleged violations including excessive emissions while temporarily running backup generators at its AI data center in Denton. The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality alerted Core Scientific on July 24 to a notice of enforcement that stemmed from the tech company running eight emergency generators between April and June while resolving manufacturing defects in 93 site transformers, city staff reported to Denton City Council on Friday. If violations are serious enough to warrant action, the TCEQ can enforce compliance and seek penalties through two types of enforcement actions: administrative orders, which are allowed if Core Scientific agrees to TCEQ’s terms and conditions, or referral to the Texas Attorney General’s Office for enforcement through the court and potential civil penalties. Core Scientific didn’t respond to a request for comment by Monday evening. Mayor Pro Tem Nick Stevens asked city staff to look into Core Scientific’s possible violations last week, during the final public hearing for a moratorium that would pause development of new data centers in Denton for 90 days. He reminded the staff that effects on the environment were one of the reasons he pitched the idea of a data center moratorium in June. Stevens alerted the public to TCEQ’s notice of enforcement in a social media post Friday, writing that Core Scientific had “allegedly exceeded their maximum emission rates, exceeded hour limits on emergency generators, failed to obtain a federal permit required for major sources of air pollution and failed to maintain records demonstrating their compliance.” Denton has two data centers previously approved by the council. Core Scientific’s center is nearing full buildout with a contract for up to 394 megawatts of power, while Qumulus’ modular AI data center, which hasn’t broken ground yet, has contracted up to 20 megawatts of power. “If [Core Scientific’s] emissions are five times higher than what the permit allows — or I think one of the things that was said in the staff report was that they haven’t been even keeping files of some of these errors — I mean, there’s a huge environmental hazard,” Stevens told the Denton Record-Chronicle on Monday. “I certainly don’t want residents to feel gaslit, where they’ve been coming to the dais for years saying this is an environmental hazard and repeatedly told it’s not. “Hopefully, it puts that conspiracy theory to bed.” In late June, the TCEQ conducted an investigation of two Core Scientific data center sites in Denton to evaluate compliance with air quality regulations. The company had obtained authorization to construct and operate emergency generators, as well as the associated fuel storage, in February 2025 and subsequently modified emission rates. Matthew Klentzman, a senior construction project manager for Core Scientific, told the TCEQ in late April that the company had identified “a systemic internal manufacturing defect affecting ninety-three transformers,” according to the July 22 TCEQ investigation report. “The defect was determined to be a credible risk of additional transformer failures which could result in loss of data center operations, equipment damage and broader system instability,” Luke Jones, an environmental investigator for TCEQ, wrote in the July 22 report. “Therefore, Core Scientific determined it would be necessary to operate four of their emergency generators on a temporary basis until corrective actions could be taken.” In April, Jones reported that he requested records via email and made follow-up requests on May 7, May 18 and May 26, when the records were finally provided. Jones reviewed the records and determined that not all of the requested information had been provided, noting that it appeared four additional emergency generators had been used to provide power during what the TCEQ called a non-emergency event between April 9 and June 23. During this period of operation, the TCEQ reported that the eight generators resulted in total emissions of 384.13 tons of nitrogen oxides, 50.10 tons of carbon monoxide and 2.51 tons of particulate matter. TCEQ reported that these amounts exceeded the certified limits of 24.9 tons per year of nitrogen oxides, 8.17 tons per year of carbon monoxide and 0.85 tons per year of particulate matter for all emergency generators at the site. As the TCEQ indicated, Denton County is in the Dallas-Forth Worth ozone non-attainment area, which is classified as severe for ozone levels. TCEQ also indicated that Core Scientific operated eight of its emergency generators for non-emergency use for more than the 100 hours per year allowed. TCEQ said four generators were running between 1,352 and 1,371 hours at one building on the property and four generators were running between 527 and 1,024 hours at another building. In addition, the TCEQ requested records of volatile organic compounds emissions from the storage and handling of diesel fuel during Core Scientific’s operation with the emergency generators between April 9 and June 23, as well as the 12-month period prior to then, “No emissions calculations were provided,” according to the violation. artigo.texto: Energy storage in Italy continues to gain capacity, approaching 20 GWh cumulatively, at the same time, the country added 4.83 GW of new photovoltaic capacity between January and September 2026, according to data compiled by ITALIA SOLARE from Terna records. The expansion of the solar market continued during the third quarter, with 1.74 GW of new photovoltaic capacity connected, representing a 37% increase compared to the 1.269 GW registered in the same period of 2025. In the first nine months of the year, new solar installations reached 4,834 MW, distributed among 147,632 newly connected systems, as a result, Italy’s cumulative photovoltaic capacity reached 48,347 MW at the end of September. The data comes from ITALIA SOLARE and is based on records from the Gaudì database in Terna, with a cut-off date of September 30, 2016. Italy accelerates new photovoltaic installations The sector’s growth is also reflected in the number of installations connected to the grid, during the third quarter, 58,459 new photovoltaic systems were added, compared to 38,660 in the previous quarter. Meanwhile, connected capacity increased by 5% compared to the second quarter, this trend demonstrates greater activity across the various segments of the Italian solar market, however, large-scale plants and commercial and industrial projects accounted for the majority of the new capacity added during the period. Large-scale projects are leading solar growth The photovoltaic installations systems of 1 MW or more contributed 2,241 MW between January and September 2026. This capacity corresponded to 473 plants and represented 46 % of the country’s new solar additions. The commercial and industrial (C&I) segment, comprised of systems with capacities between 20 kW and 1 MW, added 1,697 MW through 11,905 installations. Its share reached 35 % of the new photovoltaic capacity. Meanwhile, residential installations up to 20 kW added 897 MW through 135,254 connections, equivalent to 19% of the growth recorded during the first nine months of the year. This distribution highlights the weight of higher power projects in the expansion of the Italian market, while the residential segment continues to contribute a significant volume of new installations. The third quarter maintains the momentum of solar projects Between July and September, the photovoltaic plants large-scale projects added 858 MW of new capacity. Of this total, 394 MW came from projects between 1 MW and 10 MW, while the remaining 464 MW came from installations larger than 10 MW. During the same period, commercial and industrial projects added 543 MW, while the residential segment contributed another 341 MW. These results confirm the leading role of large-scale installations in the growth of Italian photovoltaic power and also show that commercial and industrial projects continue to make a significant contribution to the expansion of solar generation. Energy storage in Italy is approaching 20 GWh Electricity storage also saw progress during 2016. As of September 30, Italy had 984,829 connected electrochemical systems, with a cumulative energy capacity of 19,983 MWh and a total capacity of 8,338 MW. According to the published data, 12,552 MWh corresponded to storage systems associated with photovoltaic installations, while the remaining 7,368 MWh belonged to independent installations. Between January and September, 1,953 MWh of new storage capacity was connected. Of this volume, 1,486 MWh were linked to solar installations and 467 MWh corresponded to independent systems. During the third quarter, the systems associated with photovoltaic installations incorporated 480 MWh of energy capacity and 252 MW of power. These new connections comprised 31,039 systems and represented a 15% growth in capacity compared to the same period in 2025. The evolution of photovoltaic generation and energy storage reflects the expansion of both segments within the Italian electricity system. As installed solar power increases, so do the resources available to store electricity and manage its availability. This combination is becoming increasingly important in the evolution of the country’s energy infrastructure. Source: Solar Quarter Photo: Shutterstock

We’ve seen enough: If this was the data center election, it was a really bad night for the industry. Democratic campaigns and their affiliated Super PACs spent bigly on data center-themed attack ads. The ads came in various flavors. Some ads painted a vote for tax cuts as aiding data center developers. Others brought up candidates’ previous support for data centers or stock the candidate may have held in the tech industry or AI infrastructure developers. As Election Day approached, the data center industry sought to bat back claims that their sector’s poor reputation with the electorate would sway the results. People may have soured on their industry, they argued, but people weren’t going to vote based on that position. Results are still coming in, but so far congressional races heavily featuring these data center attacks are heavily going in Democrats’ favor. In addition, these races have so profoundly shifted that it’ll be challenging for the industry to argue they played no role in the outcome. Some of the most illustrative examples are obvious. In Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms campaigned on a statewide data center moratorium and won control of the governor’s mansion, becoming the first black woman to ever lead a U.S. state. Similar results in Ohio where Amy Acton flipped party control of the governor’s seat with a campaign that included going hard against data centers. In Pennsylvania, two Democrats who focused on data centers in their races have flipped Republican districts: Scranton mayor Paige Cognetti and firefighter Bob Brooks. In New Jersey, Cape May mayor Zack Mullock rode data center attacks to defeat Rep. Jeff Van Drew, the biggest opponent of the offshore wind industry. In Virginia, Democrat Shannon Taylor rode data center-laden attacks to take control of the Richmond area congressional seat from Rep. Rob Wittman. If you’re arguing this election was decided by data centers, your best proof point: Democrat Gina Hinojosa has taken control of the governor's mansion in Texas, defeating incumbent Greg Abbott, who’d sought recently to take a hard line against the industry. Hinojosa ran on going further, calling to pass a law completely pausing data center development across one of the industry’s favorite states. She won a decisive victory. So did Democratic Texas Agriculture Commissioner candidate Clayton Tucker, who I explained months ago became one of anti-data center Facebook’s favorite online personalities. But it makes sense that data centers would matter a lot in Texas, which could be compared to Virginia in terms of their buildout. When you inspect the election results more closely, they tell a more complicated story about the upper boundaries of these data center attacks. For decades, Greenville and Spartanburg County have been GOP vote strongholds and reliable for both Republican congressional candidates and statewide campaigns. The congressional district gave Donald Trump at least a 20-point cushion in the 2024 presidential election, according to Decision Desk HQ. Last week, I explained for subscribers to The Fight how Courtney McClain, a novice candidate living one mile from a controversial data center proposal, was running against incumbent Rep. William Timmons. I couldn’t find much in the way of online ad spending on either side in this race and it’s never been on the radar of most political observers as a campaign that could somehow flip party control. But the data center debate in Spartanburg County has been immense. Tonight, Timmons kept his ordinarily ruby red district by slim single digits after running even for most of the night. But this swing was essentially the same as the national margin. And because Timmons didn’t lose, this actually feels like a crucial distinction – data centers were not deciding races themselves in all cases. Democrat Annie Andrews defeated Republican Darlene Graham in a result driven by Democratic overperformance and GOP underperformance in this area, but it’s challenging to tie this result to the data center issue at all. Anything from the economy and the Iran War to Graham’s deceased brother and his baggage could be blamed for this result from this heavily evangelical region. However, it will be challenging for the data center sector to differentiate themselves from this outcome, especially since a pro-data center Super PAC – Building the Future – publicly waded into the race in support of Graham only to lose. “Darlene Graham’s loss is a black eye for the data center industry,” wrote Teddy Schleifer of The New Yor

artigo.texto: [Newsworks = Reporter Chae Yoon-jung] LG Energy Solution announced on the 29th that it will hold the 'Battery Innovation Contest (BIC) 2026.' The Battery Innovation Contest (BIC) is LG Energy Solution's flagship global research competition program. By selecting outstanding research projects from universities and research institutes and providing funding, and involving LG Energy Solution’s research team in the research process through ongoing feedback, the program helps commercialize the academic community’s creative ideas. All universities and research institutions, both domestic and international, are eligible to participate, and the application period for this year runs from the 29th of this month to December 6. Support is available through the BIC communication program BRIDGE, and LG Energy Solution selects recipients based on the technical maturity and commercialization potential of the proposed research. Since its inception in 2017, BIC is celebrating its 10th anniversary this year by expanding its research topics to the largest scale ever, further strengthening its role as an industry-academia collaboration platform. It is expected that two-way collaboration between industry and academia will become more active through more specialized topics. The designated research topics cover all areas of future battery technology, from materials to cells, BMS, and AI, including ▲ analytical techniques for cell condition diagnosis and ▲ elucidating mechanisms to enhance safety. The R&D teams of LG Energy Solution's key business units directly selected the topics they wish to collaborate on. Since 2017, more than 50 research projects have received support through the BIC program. Among these, the research topic with proven validity is being expanded and operated as the Frontier Research Laboratory (FRL), a joint research center between LG Energy Solution and leading universities and research institutions at home and abroad. If expanded to FRL, LG Energy Solution will provide additional research funding and deploy its research personnel to support in-depth studies. At last year’s BIC, the company was recognized for its many achievements, including filing a patent related to a physical model that improves BMS computation speed. In 2019, research on long-life all-solid-state batteries that operate at room temperature was published in the world-renowned journal Science by FRL. LG Energy Solution plans to continue supporting communication and project management between industry and academia through BIC’s communication program, BRIDGE, this year. BRIDGE is an integrated, two-way system for academia and industry, designed to reduce unnecessary communication during the research and development process and to enable more efficient communication and convenient project history management. By implementing a structured system, the technology for collaborative projects was protected while minimizing offline work to enhance research efficiency. Prior to this, LG Energy Solution recently signed a strategic memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Energy at its headquarters in Park One, Yeouido, Seoul, to collaborate on ESS projects in Europe and North America. Under this agreement, LG Energy Solution plans to collaborate with Endriggs to supply a total of 2 GWh within the next 24 months, targeting approximately 1.5 GWh in Europe and 0.5 GWh in North America.
