artigo.texto: Chemist who transformed energy storage nabs Canada’s top science prize University of Waterloo chemist Linda Nazar is 2026 winner of $1M Herzberg medal When Linda Nazar learned she would receive Canada’s most prestigious scientific award, she could hardly believe it. “I felt quite honestly both humbled and inspired,” the University of Waterloo chemist told Quirks & Quarks. “It’s a real honour and I’m thrilled and deeply appreciative of receiving this and frankly I was surprised.” But the award might not come as a surprise to anyone familiar with her track record. Nazar has been collecting honours throughout her career. She’s a fellow of the Royal Society of Canada, the Royal Society (U.K.) and was made an Officer of the Order of Canada in 2015 for her contributions to battery research. On November 4, she’ll add another to the collection: the $1-million Gerhard Herzberg Canada Gold Medal, the highest honour awarded by the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC). The medal was one of 26 prizes announced by the federal agency on Thursday. It recognizes Nazar’s pioneering work developing next-generation batteries, with discoveries that have helped advance the design of safer, more efficient batteries for electric vehicles, energy storage for power grids and beyond. Awarded annually, the medal celebrates researchers “whose work has had a transformative impact on their field,” according to a statement from NSERC. “Through visionary leadership, industry collaboration and mentorship, Dr. Linda Nazar has built a globally influential research enterprise at the intersection of chemistry, materials science and engineering,” said NSERC President Professor Alejandro Adem in the statement. “We celebrate her remarkable contributions and the profound influence she continues to have on science and the research community.” Those contributions, her counterparts say, have helped tackle one of the biggest challenges in the transition to renewable energy: developing batteries that can store more power, last longer, cost less and operate safely. Michael Pope, an associate professor at the University of Waterloo who co-directs the university’s Ontario Battery and Electrochemistry Research Centre alongside Nazar, says her cutting-edge research and “pioneering discoveries have advanced our fundamental understanding of battery chemistry.” “[Her discoveries have] led to the development of entirely new battery materials and technologies,” Pope said in a statement to CBC. “Having worked closely with Linda, I have witnessed first-hand her extraordinary passion for science, unwavering dedication to discovery and genuine love of research, making this recognition incredibly well deserved.” How Nazar got here Nazar's path into battery research wasn't necessarily part of some big grand plan. In fact, it began, she says, with a side quest on Friday afternoons. After earning a bachelor's degree in chemistry from the University of British Columbia in 1978, and a PhD from the University of Toronto six years later, Nazar went on to complete a postdoctoral fellowship at Exxon Research Labs in Annandale, N.J. At the time, she says the lab was among the first working to develop rechargeable lithium-ion batteries. As a side project, Nazar says she would head into the lab every Friday to run battery experiments. “It was just a great opportunity to kind of have some fun on a Friday afternoon,” she said. That side project would soon help spark a career at the forefront of battery innovation. By the early 2000s, Nazar's research was helping advance the understanding of lithium iron phosphate — a material that has since become widely used in rechargeable batteries, including those powering electric vehicles and laptops. An EV charging station is seen in Montreal on Friday, Feb. 20. Nazar's research has contributed to developments that could one day allow electric cars to travel farther on a single charge. (Christinne Muschi/The Canadian Press) According to Ontario's Universities, Nazar's research has contributed to developments that could one day allow electric cars to travel farther on a single charge. Ultimately, Nazar says what excites her most isn't just the science itself, but what it could make possible. She says the long-term potential for her research to benefit the environment — and humanity more broadly — is what keeps her motivated. “Charging electric vehicles via renewable sources and mitigating climate change as a result is…extremely important, extremely important,” she said. artigo.texto: Elon Musk Elon Musk calls Earth’s data centers “peanuts” next to what SpaceX is planning in orbit Elon Musk says SpaceX capex efficiency is underestimated as orbital data centers loom by 2028. Elon Musk is pushing back on one of the biggest worries hanging over SpaceX stock. In a reply on X on Sunday, Musk said the company’s capital expenditure efficiency is severely underestimated. He was responding to a Milk Road Stocks post citing analyst Kyle Reidhead, who estimates SpaceX will need to spend roughly $470 billion over the next five quarters. Reidhead built that figure around the target SpaceX set on its third quarter earnings call: 13 gigawatts or more of compute by the end of 2027. In his breakdown, Nvidia captures 83 to 89 percent of the spending. SpaceX ended the quarter with 1.7 GW of nameplate compute and guided to $35 billion to $40 billion in fourth quarter capex, as Teslarati reported. Musk did not attach a number to his claim, but the earnings call shows the argument. CFO Bret Johnsen said new compute currently pays for itself in under a year at today’s pricing, and Musk said that window could shrink to six months next year. Using that pace, Reidhead argues about $230 billion of the $470 billion could come from operating cash flow and about $60 billion from SpaceX’s roughly $90 billion cash pile, leaving around $180 billion to borrow. Musk confirmed last week that SpaceX had already closed a new $40 billion debt raise to buy GPUs. The ground buildout is not the end goal. It is what is meant to pay for the move to orbit. Replying on Friday to charts built from Sequoia partner Shaun Maguire’s SpaceX model, Musk wrote that “Terrestrial compute will be peanuts compared to orbital compute,” adding that orbital compute deployed per month “probably exceeds terrestrial around the end of 2028 and then far exceeds it in 2029.” Maguire’s model shows how steep that path is. It has capex climbing from $88 billion this year to $290 billion in 2027 and $369 billion in 2028, with SpaceX burning $77.8 billion in cash this year and $122.6 billion next year before turning $114.9 billion cash positive in 2028. Musk’s response to the model was, “I think we can do better.” The orbital half runs through Starmind. SpaceX plans to operate up to 1 million AI satellites flying in clusters of about 10, linked by roughly 10 terabits of bandwidth, with deployment of thousands of units starting as soon as late 2027 out of its Gigasat factory in Bastrop, Texas, according to SpaceX’s space safety page. Musk has said each Starmind spacecraft will carry more than 250 kW of solar power. Getting there depends on launch volume. Maguire’s model assumes 250 Starship flights in 2028, up from two this year and 38 next year. The nearer test is financial: SpaceX guided to $33 billion to $37 billion in first quarter 2027 revenue, more than double the $14.58 billion it booked in Q3, and Musk reposted that guidance again on Sunday morning.

Energy supplier Octopus and battery manufacturers CATL and Ampace have announced a 'Memorandum of Understanding' (MoU) to work together to produce the best possible combinations of hardware engineering and software intelligence. Octopus will bring tech such as the smart tariff, mobile app, and customer ecosystem platforms, while CATL and Ampace supply the battery chemistry and hardware nous. Initially, the initiative will be focused on European markets. At this early stage we don't have details of any actual products, but expect advances in cutting-edge tech like sodium-ion batteries, high-density cell designs, and long battery lifecycles — all of which should benefit customers and reduce electricity bills. Looking to the future According to Octopus founder and CEO Greg Jackson, combining the efforts of the three companies will "transform home energy storage", and offer "next-generation batteries where hardware and software work in complete harmony". Jason Zhu, the President of Energy Storage Systems at Ampace, is equally enthusiastic: the partnership will "fundamentally reshape how energy is delivered and consumed" as systems become "smarter, more connected, and more accessible". Of course we'll have to reserve judgment until actual products and offers arrive, but Octopus Energy, CATL, and Ampace all have strong track records. artigo.texto: Com a previsão de que o mercado brasileiro de Data Centers dobre de tamanho até 2030, a Powersafe, empresa nacional especializada em soluções de armazenamento e fornecimento de energia, aposta na ampliação dos negócios com baterias de alta performance para atender à crescente demanda por segurança e continuidade operacional dessas instalações. A companhia, que já fornece tecnologia para dois dos maiores operadores de Data Centers do País, apresentará suas soluções durante o DCD Connect Brasil 2026, nos dias 4 e 5 de novembro, em São Paulo. Segundo levantamento da consultoria JLL, o Brasil possui cerca de 660 megawatts (MW) de capacidade de Data Centers em construção, associados a aproximadamente US$ 17,4 bilhões em investimentos. O crescimento do setor, impulsionado pela computação em Nuvem, digitalização das empresas e Inteligência Artificial, amplia a necessidade de infraestrutura elétrica capaz de assegurar o funcionamento ininterrupto de servidores, equipamentos de processamento e sistemas de comunicação. Nesse cenário, a Powersafe destaca as baterias estacionárias Getpower das linhas GP-PLX e GP-XP, desenvolvidas para aplicações de alta taxa de descarga, especialmente em sistemas UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply), conhecidos como nobreaks. Esses equipamentos fornecem energia imediatamente após uma falha da rede elétrica, mantendo as operações até a entrada dos geradores de emergência ou o restabelecimento do fornecimento. Diferentemente de sistemas de armazenamento projetados para fornecer energia durante várias horas, as baterias de alta taxa de descarga são dimensionadas para entregar grandes quantidades de potência em intervalos curtos, geralmente de cinco a 15 minutos, conforme as características da instalação. “O crescimento da infraestrutura digital exige sistemas de energia cada vez mais confiáveis. Nos Data Centers, mesmo interrupções de poucos segundos podem comprometer operações críticas. Por isso, a escolha das baterias precisa considerar não apenas a capacidade de armazenamento, mas principalmente a potência disponível, a confiabilidade e as características de cada instalação”, afirma Leandro Alvares, diretor-executivo da Powersafe. Tecnologia de alta performance para operações críticas As soluções Getpower comercializadas pela Powersafe já estão presentes em instalações de dois dos maiores operadores de data centers do Brasil, reforçando a atuação da empresa no segmento de infraestrutura crítica. As linhas Getpower GP-PLX e GP-XP utilizam tecnologia chumbo-ácido regulada por válvula (VRLA), com eletrólito absorvido em manta de microfibra de vidro (AGM), e são desenvolvidas para aplicações que exigem alta potência, confiabilidade e desempenho em descargas de curta duração. A linha GP-PLX incorpora placas finas de chumbo puro (TPPL, do inglês Thin Plate Pure Lead), construção que favorece baixa resistência interna e a entrega de alta potência em descargas de curta duração. Já a GP-XP é apresentada como Ultra High Rate, voltada a aplicações que exigem taxas de descarga muito elevadas, especialmente em sistemas UPS. A escolha entre diferentes tecnologias de baterias, incluindo chumbo-ácido e íons de lítio, depende de fatores como autonomia necessária, espaço disponível, investimento inicial, vida útil, manutenção e requisitos de segurança. Embora as baterias de íons de lítio apresentem vantagens relacionadas à densidade energética e à menor ocupação de espaço, as soluções de chumbo-ácido de alta performance continuam sendo alternativas competitivas para aplicações que exigem elevada potência durante curtos períodos. “Não existe uma solução única para todos os Data Centers. Cada instalação possui requisitos específicos de potência, autonomia e disponibilidade. Nosso trabalho é avaliar essas condições e oferecer a tecnologia mais adequada, considerando desempenho, segurança operacional e custo total ao longo da vida útil dos equipamentos”, explica Alvares. Solução completa e logística reversa A estratégia da Powersafe para o segmento de Data Centers contempla o fornecimento das baterias e os serviços associados ao ciclo de vida dos equipamentos, incluindo estudos de dimensionamento, engenharia, instalação, testes, comissionamento e suporte técnico. Outro diferencial é a logística reversa das baterias ao final da vida útil. Por meio do programa Ecosafe, a companhia realiza a retirada e o encaminhamento de equipamentos inservíveis para processos de reaproveitamento, requalificação ou reciclagem por empresas homologadas, com rastreabilidade e atendimento às exigências ambientais. A iniciativa está alinhada à Política Nacional de Resíduos Sólidos e à Resolução CONAMA nº 401/2008, que estabelece critérios para o gerenciamento ambientalmente adequado de pilhas e baterias. “Além da confiabilidade energética, os operadores de data centers precisam considerar o custo total de seus sistemas e a destinação dos equipamentos ao final da vida útil. Nossa proposta é acompanhar o cliente desde a especificação da tecnologia até a substituição e a logística reversa, contribuindo para uma operação mais eficiente, segura e ambientalmente responsável”, acrescenta Alvares. A empresa avalia que a ampliação dos investimentos em infraestrutura digital deverá impulsionar a procura por soluções de armazenamento e fornecimento de energia nos próximos anos, tanto em novos empreendimentos quanto na modernização de instalações existentes. artigo.texto: O setor de papel e celulose está entre as primeiras atividades industriais que deverão apresentar planos de monitoramento de emissões de gases de efeito estufa em 2027, conforme o cronograma de implementação do mercado regulado de carbono no Brasil. As medições estão previstas para começar em 2028, enquanto os primeiros relatórios verificados deverão ser entregues em 2029. Em Mato Grosso do Sul, a medida envolve um setor com presença industrial relevante em municípios como Três Lagoas, onde operam Suzano e Eldorado Brasil, e Ribas do Rio Pardo, que abriga outra unidade da Suzano. Já em Inocência, está em desenvolvimento o Projeto Sucuriú, da Arauco, com previsão de início das operações no fim de 2027. A Secretaria Extraordinária do Mercado de Carbono estabeleceu o cronograma por meio da Portaria nº 3.199, que organiza as obrigações de MRV (mensuração, relato e verificação) do SBCE (Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões de Gases de Efeito Estufa). A norma, entretanto, não cita nominalmente as empresas nem determina quais unidades industriais deverão cumprir as obrigações. Caberá ao órgão gestor definir as instalações e as fontes de emissão que serão efetivamente incluídas no sistema. O anexo da portaria contempla atividades como fabricação de celulose e outras pastas para produção de papel, fabricação de papel e fabricação de cartolina e papel-cartão. O enquadramento considera a atividade efetivamente exercida pela instalação, mesmo quando ela aparece como secundária no cadastro do estabelecimento. A inclusão dessas atividades, porém, não significa que todas as empresas dos segmentos estarão automaticamente sujeitas às exigências. Segundo o documento, a presença de determinado código na CNAE (Classificação Nacional de Atividades Econômicas) não é suficiente para determinar a obrigatoriedade. O órgão gestor ainda deverá especificar quais fontes, instalações e atividades farão parte do sistema, considerando as particularidades de cada setor. OBRIGAÇÕES INICIAIS NÃO REPRESENTAM COBRANÇA IMEDIATA O cronograma estabelecido pela portaria está relacionado à preparação e à prestação de informações sobre as emissões. Neste primeiro momento, a norma não determina um preço para o carbono, limites de emissões por fábrica ou a quantidade de créditos que cada empreendimento deverá adquirir. Assim, a apresentação dos planos de monitoramento em 2027 não representa, por si só, uma cobrança imediata sobre as indústrias. O documento também não estabelece como as empresas deverão contabilizar as florestas plantadas nem determina que essas áreas gerarão créditos de carbono comercializáveis. Embora o sistema contemple o acompanhamento das remoções de gases de efeito estufa, os critérios para essa contabilização ainda não foram detalhados. O órgão gestor deverá publicar posteriormente as exigências referentes ao conteúdo mínimo, formato, prazos e procedimentos para elaboração dos planos e apresentação dos relatórios. A portaria estabelece que essas orientações sejam divulgadas com antecedência mínima de 150 dias em relação ao início de cada obrigação. IMPLEMENTAÇÃO SERÁ DIVIDIDA EM ETAPAS Além do setor de papel e celulose, a primeira etapa do cronograma contempla atividades como produção de alumínio, cimento e vidro, exploração e produção de petróleo e gás natural, determinadas atividades químicas, mineração de ferro e bauxita e usinas siderúrgicas integradas. Na segunda etapa, os planos de monitoramento deverão ser apresentados até 2029. O grupo inclui setores como alimentos e bebidas, cerâmica, refino de petróleo e geração de energia elétrica. Já a terceira etapa prevê a apresentação dos planos até 2031 para atividades de transporte rodoviário, ferroviário e aquaviário.

artigo.texto: Hinojosa, Abbott outline differing plans on data centers, housing ahead of Election Day SHERMAN, Texas (KXII) - Rep. Gina Hinojosa and Gov. Greg Abbott described different approaches to data centers and housing costs ahead of Election Day on Tuesday. Polls are open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Abbott visited Gainesville and Sherman in September. Hinojosa spoke with KXII’ 12s Ava Gibson on Friday. Candidates discuss turnout and polls Hinojosa said the turnout gives her reason to be hopeful. “I feel good. People are voting. That’s a great thing. Young people are back voting. People who didn’t vote in the last presidential election are voting because they feel like this is a change election year and they want to be a part of it. It’s a historic time,” Hinojosa said. Abbott downplayed the polls. “Polls don’t win elections, and polls are often wrong. What I’m confident about is exactly where my campaign stands and the outcome, that I’m going to win this race,” Abbott said. Data centers Data centers have become a major issue in the race. Both candidates said local communities should have a say, but they disagree on how to get there. Abbott wants the Legislature to give cities and counties the final say. He said he wants “rules and regulations that will empower local governments, such as counties or cities, to be the decision makers about whether or not any data center is ever going to be able to go up in their county or city.” Abbott said state permits are on hold. “And in the meantime, everything is on hold because of the mandates and restrictions that I have put in place, denying permits, denying the capability of going forward,” Abbott said. Hinojosa wants a moratorium or ban on new approvals until laws are passed to protect Texans. “Most importantly, Texans need a seat at the table to decide if and how data centers come into their communities,” Hinojosa said. Housing costs Housing costs are another top issue. In Grayson County, home prices have about doubled since 2015, while wages have grown about 40%. Both candidates were asked how they would make home ownership attainable again for working Texans. Hinojosa pointed to private equity firms buying single-family homes. “Texas has the worst problem with private equity coming in and buying up single family homes, middle income homes. And that’s wrong. That should not be happening because then regular Texas families can’t compete,” Hinojosa said. Abbott said more homes mean lower prices. He said cities that violate state laws on housing will face consequences. “Any city that violates these laws that we passed, they’re going to have their sales tax withheld until they come into compliance with these laws that we passed that actually does make it more affordable,” Abbott said. artigo.texto: 247 – A indústria química brasileira garantiu sua inclusão na primeira etapa do Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões de Gases de Efeito Estufa (SBCE), prevista para começar em 2027. A medida foi oficializada pela Portaria SEMC/MF nº 3.199, publicada pelo Ministério da Fazenda no Diário Oficial da União em 29 de outubro de 2026. A norma estabelece o cronograma de obrigações relacionadas ao monitoramento, à mensuração, ao relato e à verificação (MRV) das emissões de gases de efeito estufa nos setores abrangidos pelo mercado regulado de carbono. O planejamento inicial do governo federal previa a entrada da indústria química apenas na segunda etapa de implementação do SBCE, com início previsto para até 2029, em razão da diversidade e da pulverização das atividades do setor. A antecipação ocorreu após a Associação Brasileira da Indústria Química (Abiquim) elaborar um estudo técnico interno que identificou os segmentos responsáveis pelas maiores emissões de gases de efeito estufa (GEE). Com base nesse levantamento, a entidade apresentou uma proposta à Secretaria Extraordinária do Mercado de Carbono, que acolheu o pedido de inclusão antecipada. Com a alteração, a primeira fase do SBCE contemplará atividades relacionadas à fabricação de intermediários para fertilizantes e plastificantes, produtos petroquímicos básicos, resinas, fibras, resinas termoplásticas e produtos químicos orgânicos. Os demais segmentos da cadeia química continuarão previstos para a segunda etapa de implementação do sistema. Cronograma de MRV e regras do SBCE Instituído pela Lei nº 15.042/2024, o SBCE será implementado gradualmente. Nesta etapa inicial, as obrigações estarão concentradas na estruturação dos procedimentos de monitoramento, mensuração, relato e verificação das emissões. A definição dos limites de emissão e a distribuição das Cotas Brasileiras de Emissões (CBEs) ficarão para uma fase posterior, no âmbito do Plano Nacional de Alocação. De acordo com o cronograma estabelecido, as empresas deverão apresentar seus planos de monitoramento ao órgão gestor durante o primeiro ano, para análise e aprovação. No segundo ano, terá início a mensuração das emissões e remoções de gases de efeito estufa, conforme os procedimentos definidos nos planos aprovados. A partir do terceiro ano, as companhias deverão manter a mensuração e apresentar relatórios verificados referentes às emissões e remoções registradas no ano-calendário anterior. O processo permitirá acompanhar os dados ambientais das atividades abrangidas pelo sistema e estabelecer uma base técnica para a aplicação das regras do mercado regulado. A Abiquim também passará a integrar a Câmara de Assuntos Regulatórios (CAREG), contribuindo com informações e subsídios técnicos para a elaboração e a implementação das diretrizes do novo mercado de carbono. Para André Passos Cordeiro, presidente-executivo da Abiquim, o acolhimento da proposta evidencia a importância da articulação institucional acompanhada de fundamentação técnica. “Nosso compromisso agora é continuar contribuindo para que o mercado regulado de carbono seja implementado com segurança técnica, transparência e regras adequadas às características dos setores abrangidos”, afirmou. O executivo ressaltou ainda que a associação atuará na capacitação das empresas associadas, com o objetivo de assegurar o cumprimento das exigências do sistema e contribuir para o alcance das metas ambientais estabelecidas. O que muda com o mercado regulado de carbono O Sistema Brasileiro de Comércio de Emissões, criado pela Lei nº 15.042/2024, estabelece um modelo de regulação das emissões de gases de efeito estufa no Brasil. O mecanismo tem como objetivo contribuir para a redução dessas emissões por meio de regras aplicáveis aos setores econômicos definidos pelo governo federal. A implementação ocorrerá em etapas, começando pela organização dos processos necessários ao acompanhamento das emissões e remoções de gases de efeito estufa. Nesta primeira fase, a prioridade será consolidar os procedimentos de Mensuração, Relato e Verificação (MRV), que servirão de base para o funcionamento do mercado regulado. Na prática, as empresas abrangidas deverão elaborar planos de monitoramento, realizar a mensuração de suas emissões e remoções e apresentar os resultados conforme as metodologias e os procedimentos definidos pelo órgão gestor. Essas informações permitirão estruturar o acompanhamento das atividades reguladas e subsidiar as próximas etapas de implementação do SBCE, incluindo a definição de limites de emissão e a distribuição das Cotas Brasileiras de Emissões previstas no Plano Nacional de Alocação.

Armenia Solar Armenia adds interest subsidies for solar-plus-storage loans Subsidies cover 6 to 10 points Support runs for up to seven years Stock video by Los Muertos Crew via Pexels Nov 2, 2026 Armenia Introduces Interest Rate Subsidies for Solar-Plus-Storage Loans and Leases The Armenian government has introduced interest rate subsidies for loans and leasing arrangements used to acquire storage devices paired with solar systems, according to pv magazine. The provisions, which took effect last week, apply when the storage systems are intended to hold energy generated by solar plants or panels. Under the incentive, eligible businesses can receive subsidies ranging from 6 to 10 percentage points, depending on the financing arrangement and currency, for a period of up to seven years. A notice on Arlis, Armenia's online legal information system, indicates that a loan covering batteries and their components can receive an 8% subsidy when denominated in Armenian drams, while a lease can receive a 10% subsidy. For foreign currency financing, the subsidy stands at 6% for loans and 8% for leases. To qualify in each case, the battery storage systems must be used exclusively for storing energy produced by solar plants or solar panels. Armenia's Minister of Economy, Gevorg Papoyan, described the mechanism in a social media post, explaining that owners of solar plants who wish to store the energy they produce can purchase accumulators through the new state support toolkit, which subsidizes the interest rate on a loan or lease. Armenia's storage market remains at a relatively early stage. The country's Energy Law was amended in May to allow the development of energy storage systems for the first time, subject to licensing. Systems smaller than 1 MW, as well as those above 1 MW designed for self-consumption, are exempt from licensing. Renewable energy installations in Armenia are meanwhile expanding. Government statistics show that solar accounted for 16.3% of the country's electricity generation last year, and 2025 was a record year for solar deployment, taking cumulative solar capacity past 1 GW. artigo.texto: Um ataque de drone reivindicado pela Guarda Revolucionária do Irã provocou incêndio e interrupção de energia em um data center da Amazon Web Services (AWS) em Dubai no domingo (1º), segundo a agência Fars, nesta segunda-feira (2). De acordo com a Amazon, “objetos desconhecidos” atingiram uma das zonas de disponibilidade do centro de dados, gerando faíscas que deram início ao incêndio. As autoridades locais precisaram desligar a energia, incluindo os geradores de emergência, para conter o fogo. A interrupção afetou parcialmente serviços da AWS na região, que atende mais de 1,5 milhão de clientes ao redor do mundo. O incidente ocorre em meio à escalada do conflito entre Irã, Israel e Estados Unidos. No sábado (28), Israel realizou ataques contra alvos no Irã, alegando neutralizar ameaças ao país, com explosões relatadas em diferentes regiões de Teerã. O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, confirmou a participação norte-americana na ofensiva. Em retaliação, o Irã lançou múltiplos ataques com mísseis balísticos contra Israel e bases americanas na região. A tensão aumentou após a morte do Líder Supremo iraniano, aiatolá Ali Khamenei, e de altos oficiais do governo durante a operação conjunta, ampliando preocupações internacionais sobre a estabilidade regional. *Compartilhe esta reportagem do Diário da Guanabara, o melhor site de notícias do Rio de Janeiro.

artigo.texto: The Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission (GERC) has adopted the tariffs discovered through a competitive bidding process for the development of a 450 MW / 900 MWh standalone Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) in Gujarat. The approval covers projects allocated to NLC India Renewables Limited and Sun Drops Energia Limited under Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Limited’s (GUVNL) Phase-IX battery storage procurement initiative. The petition was filed by GUVNL before the Commission under Sections 63 and 86(1)(b) of the Electricity Act, 2003, seeking approval for the discovered tariffs. The procurement process was initiated after a developer selected under the earlier Phase-VII tender failed to execute the required Battery Energy Storage Purchase Agreement (BESPA) for the 900 MWh capacity. Following approval from the Ministry of Power, Government of India, GUVNL issued a fresh Request for Selection (RfS) on June 22, 2026, under Phase-IX. The projects are supported through Viability Gap Funding (VGF) provided under the Power System Development Fund (PSDF), aimed at encouraging the deployment of battery storage infrastructure. The tender received 11 online bids, of which 10 bidders successfully met the technical and financial qualification requirements. Subsequently, an e-reverse auction was conducted on August 11, 2026, with nine eligible bidders participating in the competitive bidding process. The successful capacities were allocated through a bucket-filling approach based on the L1 discovered tariff, with a two percent margin. Under the final allocation, NLC India Renewables Limited has been awarded 275 MW / 550 MWh of battery storage capacity at a discovered monthly storage rate of ₹231,989 per MW. Sun Drops Energia Limited has secured the remaining 175 MW / 350 MWh capacity at a monthly storage rate of ₹231,990 per MW. Both successful bidders submitted affidavits before the Commission confirming that they had no objections to the adoption of the discovered tariffs. After examining the bidding process and submissions made by the parties, GERC approved the tariffs for both developers under the provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003. GUVNL highlighted that the proposed battery storage projects will support Gujarat in meeting its Energy Storage Obligations (ESO) and Renewable Purchase Obligations (RPO). The installations are also expected to strengthen grid stability, improve power balancing and address the variability associated with renewable energy generation. As part of its directions, GERC has instructed GUVNL to execute the BESPAs with the successful developers within the stipulated timeframe. The agreements must incorporate appropriate provisions under the Electricity (Late Payment Surcharge) Rules. GUVNL has also been directed to submit copies of the executed agreements to the Commission and publish the final tariff structures on its official website to ensure transparency. With the tariff adoption approved, GERC has disposed of the petition, clearing the way for the implementation of the 450 MW / 900 MWh standalone battery storage projects in Gujarat. artigo.texto: Com fundo de R$ 120 milhões, Emet Capital prepara projeto para data centers Primeiro empreendimento será no Rio de Janeiro; gestora negocia terrenos em São Paulo e no Ceará, com investimento previsto de R$ 1 bilhão nos três projetos Pedro Gil Editor do Exame INSIGHT Publicado em 3 de novembro de 2026 às 11:14. Última atualização em 3 de novembro de 2026 às 16:01. A Emet Capital vai investir R$ 120 milhões no desenvolvimento imobiliário de data centers no Brasil. A gestora concluiu nesta terça-feira, 3, a captação do fundo Data Brasil Infra FIP junto a investidores estratégicos. A a B.Real Capital atuou como consultora. O primeiro investimento já tem endereço. Será em Santa Cruz, no Rio de Janeiro. O empreendimento será concluído até 2030. Além deste, há outras duas regiões mapeadas, no Ceará e em São Paulo, com terrenos em negociação. A demanda total, considerando os três projetos, deve atingir R$ 1 bilhão. Para dar vazão ao montante, o Data Brasil Infra FIP deve abrir nova janela de captação no primeiro trimestre do ano que vem. A expectativa é levantar mais R$ 100 milhões. A gestora estima outras três janelas de captação no futuro. Mudança de paradigma A tese desenvolvida pelas gestoras fundamenta-se no reenquadramento do ativo perante os investidores globais: o mercado de capitais passou a enxergar o data center não como um simples equipamento de tecnologia, mas como um imóvel de infraestrutura crítica. Nessa dinâmica de mercado, as gestoras assumem o papel de proprietárias e desenvolvedoras de "powered lands" — terrenos estrategicamente localizados e dotados de garantia de acesso a redes elétricas de alta potência. Provedores, hyperscalers e empresas de IA entram na operação como tomadores finais do produto imobiliário. Essa relação é firmada por meio de contratos de locação de longo prazo, no modelo built-to-suit. O pipeline do fundo abrange nove projetos distribuídos por São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Minas Gerais, Centro-Oeste e Nordeste, somando uma capacidade total projetada de 3.5 GW e estimativa de R$ 2,5 bilhões em investimentos nos próximos três anos. O Brasil já concentra cerca de 48% de toda a capacidade instalada de data centers na América Latina, segundo dados da consultoria imobiliária JLL. "A grande chave de valor e oportunidade no mercado de data centers hoje está na infraestrutura de energia e na localização do terreno. A construção de uma nova subestação elétrica ou a obtenção de outorgas de conexão de alta capacidade pode levar mais de dois anos", diz Raffael Faustino, diretor da Emet Capital. "O data center vive hoje o mesmo movimento que observamos nos galpões logísticos classe A há uma década: pouca oferta qualificada para uma demanda estrondosa." Segundo dados da Associação Brasileira das Empresas de Tecnologia da Informação e Comunicação (Brasscom), projetos do setor estimam que os investimentos em tecnologias digitais e infraestrutura no país podem movimentar até R$ 2 trilhões até 2029. “No Brasil, o crescimento encontra desafios adicionais, como as novas regras de conexão, restrição de disponibilidade de energia em regiões estratégicas e a necessidade de reduzir cada vez mais o prazo de implantação de novos projetos", diz Alison Takano, CEO da B.Real Capital. artigo.texto: Some residents of a proposed large data center in Enid are planning a petition drive for a recall of the City Council and Mayor who supported a data center project proposed by some local business officials while Yukon voters will decide this week on the fate of their mayor in a similar protest. While the Project Thunderbird data center proposed by Jason Singer, Aaron Singer, Chad Dillingham and Troy Phillips who make up the firm Plainsmen Holdings, has the support of the Enid Regional Development Alliance, it doesn’t have the support of some residents. The group, No Data Centers in Enid, is led by Jacob McNew, who recently said the organization has launched efforts to recall Mayor David Mason and most city commissioners. A petition effort was held Sunday in Enid to force a vote of residents to overturn the rezoning of two properties where the data center project would be located. We are seeking committed volunteers who can get involved in this campaign. As we enter a new phase of this fight, we are needing folks who can help out. There are tons of ways to get involved. Many of which don’t require a lot of time. If you or anyone you know would like to get experience in activism, please reach out! This is a great opportunity for young and old to make a difference in our community,” shared the group in a social media posting over the weekend. It followed an earlier posting. “We would like to take the time to address the biggest piece of misinformation that we frequently see online and hear in person. It is imperative that we oppose this project using only facts. Project Thunderbird is not a “done deal”. While Mayor David Mason, City Manager Jerald Gilbert and City Attorney Melissa Blanton have been in contact with Plainsmen Holdings LLC since at least January 2026, as their NDAs prove, they do not have the power alone to accept this proposal. Although they have made it quite apparent, they are not impartial to this project, it still requires city commissioners to decide whether it gets approval or not. There are more opportunities to fight back on the proposal, and we will share those opportunities on this page as they are announced. As of now, we are collecting signatures for recalls as well as a referendum to overturn the city council vote that approved the rezonings.” No Data Centers in Enid originally announced its opposition saying it wants to keep health and quality of life and that no possible tax income was worth the sacrifice. “People want to stay living in their homes, farming on their farms to provide healthy food for our people and running the ranches that provide food. We want to continue to know our kids are healthy and able to focus at school. We want to keep looking up at night to enjoy our beautiful clear and clean pollution free sky!” Project Thunderbird would sit on a 1,735 acre site and the developers say it would use behind-the-meter electricity generation. In their original announcement in September, they said the project would rely on raw pipeline water from Kaw Lake located 8 miles east of Ponca City. A similar recall election petition was successful in the city of Yukon over a proposed Beltline Energy data center that drew large opposition. City voters will decide Tuesday, November 3 on a recall of Mayor Brian Pilmore. Residents launched their recall petition in May. In addition, a petition to require voter approval for the proposed data center was recently filed with the Yukon City Clerk, according to the Yukon Progress. “It’s the most democratic way to deal with these things,” explained petition proponent Charles Scott. He said the vote would not be for a prohibition but for approval. Scott also said the petition contained 354 signatures while only 162 were required. City officials were reported to be in the process of verifying the validity of the signatures. The recall drive in Yukon already resulted in the resignation of Vice Mayor Jeff Wooton shortly after the recall effort targeted him and Mayor Pilmore. He resigned June 6, 2026.

artigo.texto: St. Marys Cement and Rodan Energy Solutions have announced a long-term agreement to develop a 50-megawatt-hour battery energy storage system at St. Marys Cement’s Bowmanville, Ont., plant. According to the companies, the behind-the-meter system will allow the facility to reduce its demand from the electrical grid during peak periods while maintaining plant operations. The batteries can be charged during lower-demand periods and supply energy during periods of higher electricity demand. Rodan will develop, own and operate the battery system and manage its ongoing energy use through the company’s FlexOps platform. St. Marys Cement will not provide upfront capital for the project. The companies said the project is intended to reduce energy costs and improve operational resilience at the Bowmanville plant, which has operated since 1968. Rodan and St. Marys Cement described the 50 MWh installation as the largest behind-the-meter battery energy storage system in Canada to date. The Bowmanville installation will be the first project of its type for St. Marys Cement parent company Votorantim Cimentos North America. The company said the project could provide a basis for evaluating similar energy storage installations at its other operations.

artigo.texto: DCF Show: Can AI Unlock Data Centers' Stranded Megawatts? Key Highlights - Hammerhead AI CEO Rahul Kar argues that the data center power shortage is partly a utilization problem, with substantial electrical capacity already allocated but not consistently consumed. - Hammerhead's ORCA platform uses reinforcement learning to coordinate facility power, cooling, and GPU workloads within existing electrical limits. - The company's reported proof of concept added 30% more GPU capacity within a fixed power allocation, increasing completed inference jobs by 18–20% while accepting longer latency for flexible workloads. - Kar says existing tenants' service-level agreements remain protected as additional inference workloads use temporarily available capacity. - Hammerhead reports that ORCA is commercially deployed, with expansion planned for 2027, backed by new distribution and research collaborations. The data center industry's race for power has become a contest against time. Developers are pursuing new generating capacity, transmission upgrades, utility interconnections, and increasingly elaborate behind-the-meter strategies to satisfy an AI infrastructure market whose demand keeps outrunning delivery schedules. Yet another possibility is emerging alongside the construction boom: Some of the power needed to expand AI computing may already be available inside operational facilities, committed to customers but not consistently consumed. That is the proposition behind Hammerhead AI, a Redwood City, California-based company developing software to coordinate electrical infrastructure, cooling systems, and computing workloads. Rather than treating a data center's power allocation as a fixed ceiling that can only be raised through construction, Hammerhead argues that more compute can be accommodated by managing existing resources dynamically. In a new episode of the Data Center Frontier Show, Hammerhead AI founder and CEO Rahul Kar discussed the company's approach with DCF Editor-in-Chief Matt Vincent, examining how reinforcement learning and workload orchestration could convert otherwise idle electrical capacity into revenue-producing AI infrastructure. The idea arrives at a consequential moment for the colocation market. DCF's analysis of CBRE's first-half 2026 data center market report found North American primary-market vacancy at just 1.4%, even as new construction reached record levels. Power commitments, delivery timelines, and access to ready infrastructure continue to determine where and when additional compute can be deployed. Hammerhead's central argument is that the industry should examine how much of its already allocated capacity can be made productive before assuming that every increment of computing demand requires another increment of physical infrastructure. The commercial opportunity is substantial. Whether it can be realized without undermining the reliability expectations of mission-critical facilities is the harder question. A Power Shortage, or a Utilization Problem? Kar begins with a distinction between the electricity infrastructure available to serve demand and the amount of that infrastructure being used at any particular time. "The grid as we know it is about 30% utilized," he told Vincent, arguing that the industry's power challenge reflects both insufficient infrastructure in constrained markets and inefficient use of existing capacity. Kar characterized the problem as two-sided. AI developers need more electricity infrastructure, but many facilities also consume considerably less power than the amount reserved or available to them. Hammerhead's business focuses on that second condition. The 30% figure requires qualification. Grid utilization varies widely by geography, system component, measurement method, and time of day. Nor does low average utilization necessarily indicate that an equivalent amount of additional continuous demand can be safely accommodated. Recent utility disclosures illustrate the distinction. According to October 2026 reporting on Virginia's first grid-utilization filings, Dominion Energy reported average annual distribution utilization of 41% between July 2025 and July 2026, compared with approximately 80% during infrequent peak periods. Appalachian Power reported considerably lower annual utilization. Those differences matter. Electrical infrastructure must accommodate peak demand, contingency conditions, equipment outages, and other reliability requirements. Average unused capacity cannot simply be treated as firm, continuously available power. The same principle applies inside a data center, where installed electrical capacity, contracted customer allocations, actual power consumption, and available operational headroom are different measurements. Vincent pressed Kar on precisely that distinction: How does an operator establish that an apparently unused megawatt is genuinely available to monetize, rather than capacity being preserved for reliability? Kar acknowledged the challenge. "Between power availability or operational headroom and when it's ready for compute monetization or producing tokens, there is a journey that needs to happen," he said. Hammerhead's answer is to combine analytical methods with AI-based control systems to determine how additional workloads can operate within existing limits. The goal is to identify usable flexibility while maintaining safeguards against conditions that could threaten established operations. That makes the company's proposition more specific than simply discovering idle megawatts. It is attempting to establish the operating conditions under which those megawatts can support additional computing activity. artigo.texto: Resumo - Milei pretende converter a Patagônia em centro de data centers dedicados à inteligência artificial - Governo promete cortar imposto de 25% para 15% e manter a IA sem regulamentação - OpenAI, Amazon, Google, Oracle e Peter Thiel já procuraram o presidente argentino - Polonesa Green Capital planeja complexo de US$ 3 bilhões em 130 mil hectares em Chubut - Campus poderia consumir 2,7 vezes a eletricidade de Buenos Aires em um ano - Mobilização 'Trelew Livre de Data Centers' e oposição no Congresso reagem ao plano O governo da Argentina quer converter a Patagônia num polo de processamento de dados voltado à inteligência artificial. Para atrair as gigantes do setor, Javier Milei, presidente do país, acena com carga tributária menor e ausência de regras sobre o tema. Empresas como OpenAI, Amazon e Google já sinalizaram interesse na iniciativa, que, em contrapartida, levanta dúvidas sobre os efeitos ambientais e sobre o benefício concreto que o investimento traria aos argentinos. A localidade oferece vantagens significativas aos data centers. Isso co, espaço de sobra em áreas vazias, temperaturas baixas e ventos fortes. Além de, por perto, as reservas de gás do xisto de Vaca Muerta, suficientes para abastecer tanto a geração de eletricidade quanto o resfriamento das máquinas. Enquanto em partes dos Estados Unidos e da Europa a população rejeita empreendimentos assim por causa da disputa pela energia, a Argentina enxerga nesses pontos uma forma de atrair investimentos. Interesse de big techs e de Peter Thiel Durante reunião com a Câmara de Comércio dos Estados Unidos, no mês passado, Milei deixou clara a posição do governo: ‘Não vamos regulamentar a inteligência artificial. Vamos deixá-la livre.’ Nos últimos meses, segundo registros de visitantes a que a Associated Press teve acesso, o presidente e sua equipe receberam executivos e investidores da área. Entre os nomes constam o investidor Peter Thiel e enviados de OpenAI, Amazon, Google e Oracle. Neste ano, autoridades argentinas foram procuradas pela Crusoe, companhia que desenvolve data centers, com o objetivo de discutir investimentos respaldados pelo governo norte-americano. No Texas, foi essa mesma firma que ajudou a erguer o maior campus da OpenAI. Há ainda as tratativas com a polonesa Green Capital, disposta a investir US$ 3 bilhões (cerca de R$ 16,05 bilhões) na construção de um empreendimento localizado na Patagônia. A proposta prevê o aluguel das instalações para que gigantes do setor tecnológico as utilizem no processamento de IA, mas nenhum cliente foi fechado até agora. Imposto menor e cobranças por soberania tecnológica Para viabilizar projetos nesse patamar, Milei apoia um programa que reduziria de 25% para 15% a tributação sobre o lucro das empresas, desde que haja investimentos de ao menos US$ 1 bilhão (cerca de R$ 5,45 bilhões) ligados à IA e a outros setores emergentes. O Senado ainda precisa aprovar a medida para que ela avance. Esse incentivo, contudo, não impõe exigências sobre como a infraestrutura será usada no território nacional. Não há obrigação de que as companhias destinem capacidade de processamento ao mercado da Argentina, nem de que informem quanto consumirão de energia e água. A soberania tecnológica figura entre os temores de pesquisadores e ambientalistas. Para Alan Rocha Varsanyi, que integra o grupo argentino Observatorio Petrolero Sur, o poder de processamento atenderá sobretudo aos interesses globais das contratantes, sem agregar nada ao avanço tecnológico interno do país. Diante da falta de normas, apontam-se também perigos como a vigilância massiva e invasões digitais. Nicolás Wolovick, que leciona ciência da computação na Universidade Nacional de Córdoba, teme que o país vire laboratório de testes para tecnologias impedidas onde a regulação é mais exigente. Resistência em Chubut e no Congresso Com 130 mil hectares de extensão, o complexo pretendido pela Green Capital em Chubut ficaria em terreno alugado junto a 14 proprietários de terras locais. Entre eles está a família de Francisco Sáenz, que trabalha como engenheiro agrônomo e cria ovelhas: diante da queda na pecuária, ele enxerga no projeto a oportunidade de uma renda extra. Antes de 2028 as obras não devem começar. Depois de pronto, o campus teria um gasto anual de energia equivalente a aproximadamente 2,7 vezes. Isso, que Buenos Aires inteira utilizou em 2025, segundo estimativa feita pela Associated Press. A Green Capital afirma que a eletricidade sairá de geração própria, feita por meio de geradores a gás, parques solares e aerogeradores. Já as autoridades da província contam que o projeto atraia investimentos na casa dos bilhões de dólares, crie empregos qualificados e aproveite o excedente da energia dos ventos. Essas garantias, no entanto, deixaram desconfiada uma parcela dos habitantes de Trelew, município próximo à área onde o empreendimento deve ser instalado. As avaliações sobre impacto ambiental ainda não terminaram e as autorizações permanecem sem aprovação; além disso, a companhia deixou de informar quanta água será usada e qual será o peso do gás na produção de eletricidade. Sem essas informações, protestos tomaram as ruas e as redes sociais sob o lema ‘Trelew Livre de Data Centers’. A mobilização chegou ao Congresso: deputados da oposição alteraram um projeto que facilitaria a compra de terrenos por quem não é do país e barraram a possibilidade de Milei autorizar que sistemas de inteligência artificial assumissem a gestão de empresas.

artigo.texto: Russian tech companies are scrambling to harden and hide their data centers underground after Ukrainian drone strikes damaged facilities housing AI supercomputers and disrupted cloud services for millions of Russian users. Meanwhile, the Kremlin is requiring data center owners to reserve computing capacity for emergency state needs and has even authorized possible use of foreign data centers. These consequences of Russia’s war against Ukraine come as the Russian military has bombarded Ukrainian cities with drones and missiles nearly night and day in recent months, along with specifically targeting Ukrainian data centers since late September. But Ukraine has retaliated with its own drone strikes on military and infrastructure targets across Russia, degrading or knocking out data centers operated by Russian tech giant Yandex, the state-owned bank Sberbank, social media site VKontakte, and the Russian Ministry of Finance. Now, state-owned telecommunications company Rostelcom has raised the possibility of moving some Russian data centers underground in talks with the nickel and palladium mining company Norilsk, according to Russian newspaper Vedomosti. The industry publication Data Center Dynamics also pointed to a recent proposal by a Russian regional governor to build data centers within open-pit coal mines while planting green public parks above as camouflage. On November 2, Putin also signed a decree ordering Russian data center operators to set aside 10 percent of available space and capacity in case the Russian government requires it, according to independent Russian news publication Meduza. That may indicate growing Kremlin concerns about the vulnerability of Russian cloud computing infrastructure during its war with Ukraine.

artigo.texto: We live in an era where our entire lives, communication, entertainment, boarding passes, and wallets are tied to rectangles of glass and metal. Yet, despite processors getting exponentially faster and screens becoming infinitely sharper, battery technology has often felt stuck in the past. I have a drawer full of heavy, degraded power banks that take hours to charge and lose their capacity as soon as you plug them in, they just don’t feel safe to use anymore. The solution has seemingly arrived from an unexpected place. The Story Behind the ChargeCore To understand why the new Laser ChargeCore Everyday series matters, you have to look at the brand behind it. Laser is a home-grown Australian technology company that have built a reputation for making emerging technology accessible without asking consumers to empty their wallets. Their latest release brings something called semi-solid-state battery technology to the everyday consumer. Interestingly “Chargecore” is front and center as the brand name with “a brand by Laser” as the tagline. If you have followed the automotive industry, you might know that solid-state and semi-solid-state batteries are the holy grail for electric vehicles. Traditional lithium-ion batteries use liquid electrolytes to move energy back and forth. This liquid can be volatile, sensitive to extreme temperatures, and prone to degradation over time. Semi-solid-state technology replaces most of that liquid with a conductive, semi-solid gel. The result is a battery that is significantly more stable, less prone to overheating, and capable of storing more energy in a smaller physical footprint. Laser saw the advancements happening in EV factories and realised that the same chemistry could be scaled down. The result is bringing the safest, most stable battery technology available and packing it into a portable charger that everyday people can actually afford. Mechanics and Daily Impact The new ChargeCore lineup features three distinct capacities to suit different needs: a 10,000mAh model, a 20,000mAh model, and a massive 27,000mAh powerhouse. In practice, this technology changes the reality of charging on the go. When you are travelling for work, keeping a Nintendo Switch or Steam Deck alive on a long flight down usually requires a bulky power bank that takes up half your carry-on space and generates an uncomfortable amount of heat. With the semi-solid-state chemistry, these Laser units remain remarkably cool even under heavy load. The thermal stability means the internal components are not constantly stressing themselves, which directly translates to a longer lifespan for the power bank itself. The entry-level 10,000mAh and mid-tier 20,000mAh units offer a 20W USB-C Power Delivery output, which is perfectly optimised for modern smartphones and wireless earbuds. But the GOAT is the 27,000mAh model, which bumps the output to 35W. That extra wattage is exactly what you need to keep larger tablets or handheld gaming consoles drawing positive power while in active use. Importantly, all three models feature an easy-to-read digital battery display (so you are never guessing what “three dots out of four” actually means) and they are all fully carry-on approved for air travel. I also like the simplicity of description on the packaging that states the the 10,000mAh = 2 phone charges, the 20,000mAh units = 4 phone charges and the 27,000mAh model = 5 phone charges. Especially if you were picking these up in an airport kiosk, knowing what you are going to get in layman’s terms is extremely important. They also come equipped with dedicated overcharge, overcurrent, short-circuit, and overheat protections. This means you can plug your premium electronics in and walk away without a second thought. It is the kind of silent feature that you never want to test, but adds immense peace of mind. If you like to match your tech with various colours they are available in Black currenlty and are soon expanding to Galactica, Grey, and Dark Cherry, the physical design is sleek, compact, and unobtrusive. Ultimately it’s a powerbank so you want it simple, light and in working order anything else is bonus. The Competition When looking at the wider market, the portable charger space is intensely crowded. You can easily walk into any convenience store and buy a cheap lithium-ion power bank. However, those legacy devices carry the inherent risks of thermal runaway if damaged, and their cells degrade noticeably faster. On the other end of the spectrum, you have premium GaN (Gallium Nitride) wall chargers, which deliver incredible speed but are useless when you are miles away from a power outlet. There are also LiFePO4 (Lithium Iron Phosphate) power banks, a technology Laser themselves championed locally in 2025. While incredibly safe and long-lasting, LiFePO4 cells are physically larger and heavier, making them better suited for camping setups than slipping into a laptop bag. The semi-solid-state ChargeCore units hit a perfect middle ground. They offer the advanced safety and stability of next-generation chemistry, the high energy density required for a compact form factor, and a price tag that severely undercuts premium competitors. Laser are also one of the first to be dropping this tech into Australia. The Final Verdict After spending time with the 10,000mAh, 20,000mAh, and 27,000mAh models, it is clear that Laser has delivered a highly impressive lineup. They have taken high-end, automotive-grade battery science and distilled it into an everyday accessory that simply works exactly as promised. The fact that the 27,000mAh model retails for just $99.95, while the 10,000mAh model sits at $49.95, makes this range exceptionally easy to recommend. If you are still relying on a heavy, aging power bank that gets uncomfortably warm in your bag, the ChargeCore Everyday Semi-Solid-State series is the perfect excuse to upgrade. Highly recommended. artigo.texto: BYD recorded its strongest monthly sales performance of the year in October, with battery electric vehicle (BEV) deliveries exceeding 300,000 units for the first time. Strong demand for fully electric models helped offset declining plug-in hybrid sales, highlighting a continued shift in the Chinese automaker’s sales mix toward battery-powered vehicles. The Chinese automotive giant sold 490,168 new energy vehicles (NEVs) in October, representing a 10.97% increase compared with the same month last year and a 5.74% improvement over September, according to the company’s latest sales data. October marked BYD’s sixth consecutive month of year-over-year sales growth and its eighth consecutive month of higher sales compared with the previous month. However, the annual growth rate continued to moderate, falling from 16.98% in September. Despite the slower growth, October was BYD’s strongest sales month since December 2024 and the fourth-highest monthly total in the company’s history. Battery electric vehicles were the biggest contributor to BYD’s October performance. The company sold 305,743 battery electric passenger vehicles, an impressive 37.38% increase from October last year and an 11.94% rise compared with September. This marked the third consecutive monthly record for BYD’s fully electric passenger vehicle sales. BEVs accounted for 63.28% of BYD’s passenger vehicle sales in October, compared with 59.81% in September and 50.95% during the same month last year. The figures demonstrate how rapidly BYD’s product mix is changing as demand for fully electric models continues to grow. The trend is particularly significant because BYD has traditionally relied heavily on plug-in hybrid vehicles alongside its fully electric lineup. October’s results suggest that battery electric models are becoming an increasingly important part of the company’s overall business. While fully electric vehicle sales reached new heights, BYD’s plug-in hybrid business faced another difficult month. The automaker sold 177,382 plug-in hybrid passenger vehicles in October, down 17.23% year-over-year and 3.37% compared with September. This represented the second consecutive month of annual declines for the plug-in hybrid segment, following a 2.36% decrease in September. Looking at the first 10 months of the year, BYD sold 1,935,700 battery electric passenger vehicles, up 5.86% compared with the same period last year. Plug-in hybrid passenger vehicle sales, meanwhile, dropped 11.02% to 1,625,969 units. Overall, BYD delivered 483,125 passenger new energy vehicles in October, an increase of 10.59% year-over-year and 5.78% month-over-month. Commercial NEV sales contributed another 7,043 units, representing a substantial 45.22% annual increase. International markets continued to play an increasingly important role in BYD’s expansion. The company exported 170,194 new energy vehicles in October, up 102.84% compared with the same month last year. However, exports were down 5.81% from September. From January through October, BYD’s NEV exports reached 1,513,154 units, representing a 93.75% increase compared with the same period last year. The export figures highlight BYD’s growing international ambitions as the company expands its presence in markets across Europe, Southeast Asia, Latin America and other regions. Although monthly exports fluctuated slightly, the nearly doubled year-to-date total demonstrates the importance of overseas markets to BYD’s long-term growth strategy. Alongside its expanding sales, BYD has been refreshing several important models across its vehicle lineup. On October 20, the company introduced the second-generation BYD Seagull, a compact electric car that received a larger body and flash-charging technology on selected versions. Just one week later, on October 27, BYD launched the third-generation Qin Plus DM-i. The updated plug-in hybrid sedan features a larger body, improved electric driving range and optional LiDAR technology. The next major launch is scheduled for November 5, when BYD is expected to introduce the second-generation Seal 07. The updated model will be offered with both fully electric and plug-in hybrid powertrains, continuing the expansion of the company’s Ocean series. These product updates are expected to help BYD maintain its competitive position in China’s increasingly crowded electric vehicle market. BYD’s October results reveal an important development in the company’s business. While overall NEV sales continue to grow, battery electric vehicles are increasingly driving that expansion, while plug-in hybrid models are losing momentum. The milestone of surpassing 300,000 electric passenger vehicles in a single month is particularly significant, demonstrating the scale BYD has achieved in the global EV industry. However, the company still faces challenges, including slower annual sales growth and intensifying competition in China. Its ability to sustain BEV momentum, refresh its product lineup and expand international deliveries will be crucial in the months ahead. With several updated models entering the market and overseas sales continuing to climb, BYD is positioning itself for another important phase of growth.

The global salt hydrates market is entering a phase of sustained expansion as demand for efficient thermal management and energy storage accelerates across buildings, industry, and renewable energy integration. Salt hydrates, including sodium sulfate decahydrate, calcium chloride hexahydrate, magnesium sulfate heptahydrate, and sodium acetate trihydrate, are increasingly valued for their ability to store and release latent heat at precise temperature ranges, making them central to phase change material (PCM) solutions. As of 2025, the market is supported by decarbonization policies, rising electricity costs, and the need to balance intermittent renewable supply with demand. The forecast period 2026–2035 points to continued growth, with thermal energy storage in construction and industrial processes acting as the primary demand engine. However, the market faces headwinds from alternative PCM materials, raw material price volatility, and technical challenges such as phase segregation and supercooling. This report provides a data-driven view of market size, structure, end-use dynamics, and regional trends, offering stakeholders a transparent framework to navigate the evolving salt hydrates landscape. The baseline scenario for the world salt hydrates market anticipates steady growth from 2026 to 2035, with a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 5.8% and a market index reaching 176 by 2035 (2025=100). This outlook is anchored in the accelerating deployment of thermal energy storage (TES) systems, particularly in the construction sector where salt hydrate-based PCMs are integrated into building envelopes, underfloor heating, and cooling systems to shift peak loads and improve energy efficiency. Industrial applications, including chemical synthesis and dehydrating agents, provide a stable demand base, while pharmaceutical excipients and food additives contribute niche but consistent volume. The supply side is expected to benefit from capacity expansions and technological improvements in encapsulation and formulation, enhancing material performance and widening addressable applications. Overall, the market is poised for robust, innovation-led expansion, with the strongest upside tied to the decarbonization of heating and cooling. Thermal energy storage represents the largest and fastest-growing end-use sector for salt hydrates, primarily through their use as phase change materials (PCMs). In 2025, demand is concentrated in building applications such as PCM-enhanced wallboards, underfloor heating, and cold storage, where salt hydrates absorb and release latent heat to shift peak loads and improve energy efficiency. The mechanism is straightforward: during off-peak hours or when renewable generation is abundant, the hydrate melts, storing thermal energy; during peak demand, it solidifies, releasing heat. This capability is increasingly valued as electricity grids face stress from intermittent renewables and rising cooling demand. Through 2035, demand-side indicators such as building energy codes, retrofit rates, and renewable capacity additions will drive adoption. The construction sector's push toward net-zero buildings and the integration of PCMs into HVAC systems are key catalysts. However, technical hurdles like encapsulation durability and phase segregation must be addressed to unlock broader commercial uptake. The sector's growth is also supported by industrial TES applications, including waste heat recovery and solar thermal storage, where salt hydrates offer cost-effective, high-density storage. As energy prices remain volatile and decarbonization policies tighten, thermal energy storage is expected to remain the dominant demand driver, with salt hydrates capturing a significant share of the PCM market. artigo.texto: [Cover photo credit to Elizabeth Landry] UK artist Bess Atwell has announced her new album, Cut A Figure, arriving February 5th, 2026, via Nettwerk. Atwell has also shared the single “Glass” alongside a video, and confirmed full world tour dates in 2027. For her follow-up to 2024’s Aaron Dessner-produced album Light Sleeper, Bess Atwell retreated from the UK to Quebec, where she lived for nine months, conceiving and writing what would become Cut a Figure. To bring the album to life, she worked with Los Angeles-based Producer and mixer Chris Coady (Beach House, Future Islands, DIIV, Foals, and more). “Glass” is “the emotional heart” of the new record, and its lyrics even inspired the album’s title. “Glass” is an Indie Pop song with lyrics “exploring how an eagerness to be understood can make someone invisible.” Bess explains: I knew I wanted to name the album after a line in this song as it feels like the heart of the record. Sometimes, an eagerness to be seen and understood can have the opposite effect – you can be so transparent that you end up invisible. When I was a teenager, I was really into doing ‘personality tests’. One test had you imagine a cube and then describe it (the cube supposedly representing how you express yourself). All my friends and family pictured various different sizes and colors, while I saw a transparent glass box floating in space.

artigo.texto: A Botetourt County citizen’s lawsuit alleges that the county violated Virginia’s Freedom of Information Act when it approved documentation advancing the Google data center project in Troutville. Robert Dallas, a retired anesthesiologist who said he lives near the Botetourt Center at Greenfield site, filed the suit on Monday, seeking to invalidate the county’s economic development performance agreement with the limited liability company behind the project. The suit asks the Botetourt County Circuit Court to “rescind all actions” carried out in connection with the June 2025 economic development performance agreement. Dallas identifies the Botetourt County Board of Supervisors, the county itself, its economic development authority and Helio Capital LLC as respondents. All were part of the performance agreement, which set in motion the land sale and the county’s support of the Google development, among other items. According to the suit, the county’s board of supervisors did not disclose on its published agenda that it would be discussing the agreement or a resolution to enact it in a closed meeting on June 24, 2025. After the board returned to public session, it voted 5-0, with no discussion, to approve them, after they were added to the agenda during the meeting, the case alleges. After a recess, the board returned to address another “walk-on” item — announcing the data center project. A final item that didn’t appear on the agenda was a board resolution approving Google’s agreement with the Western Virginia Water Authority, Dallas alleges. “At no time … did the board reasonably identify the substance of the performance agreement resolution or the performance agreement itself, despite having agreed to both at the closed meeting immediately preceding the performance agreement resolution’s being added to the agenda as a walk-on item,” the lawsuit reads. The agreement set in motion Google’s $14 million deal with Botetourt County for 312 acres in Greenfield. The tech giant plans a data center campus including three data centers, three substations, an office building, access roads, utilities, parking areas and stormwater management facilities, according to a March 10 Army Corps of Engineers notice soliciting public comment on the project. The board of supervisors engaged in “subterfuge” by adopting what the lawsuit called the key contract related to the data center, without adequate disclosure, “not only undermining the will of the people but violating the Virginia Freedom of Information Act,” the suit states. The open government and records law in question requires localities to identify such projects. Quoting Virginia law, the suit states, “Except as specifically authorized by law, in no event may any public body take action on matters discussed in any closed meeting, except at an open meeting for which notice was given as required by” the law. Dallas spoke during a Monday afternoon news conference at the Roanoke law firm Fishwick & Associates, which filed the suit on his behalf. He said that he has lived in Botetourt County for 36 years. His home is about a half-mile from the proposed Google complex, where work has already begun. He said his land is protected by a conservation easement he had recorded about three years ago. “I know this community well, and like many, I was surprised when the county suddenly announced the data center project with no public input in June of 2025,” he said. “I filed this petition because I strongly believe that the Botetourt County Board of Supervisors should follow all the rules of procedure and give citizens like me and many others the chance to make our voices heard. “The board did not do so on June 24, 2025, when they agreed to the performance agreement for the Google data center, outside of the public eye, in a closed session, and then voted to adopt it without offering even a hint of what it was. This case is about holding our leaders responsible and having open and transparent government.” Nor had it been open with county residents in the year and a half preceding that day, during which Botetourt officials “cultivated” an “atmosphere of secrecy” concerning negotiations about the project, Fishwick’s firm stated in both the lawsuit and a news release. Dallas is asking the court to rescind actions including the county issuing expedited permits and granting Google eligibility to participate in the county’s third-party inspection program. If the county chooses to adopt a similar resolution in the future, it should comply with the Freedom of Information Act, according to the suit. Botetourt County, through its spokesman, sent an email to reporters on Monday. “As this matter involves pending litigation, Botetourt County will not comment on the specific allegations or discuss legal matters,” the email read. “The county respects the legal process and remains committed to providing accurate and appropriate information to the public as the matter moves forward.” $1 billion investment from Google per data center A nondisclosure agreement was part of the process leading up to the deal, County Administrator Gary Larrowe has said. Google will pay a property tax rate of 70 cents per $100 of assessed value, same as any other landowner in the county, Larrowe has said. The county has made the performance agreement public, however. It includes Google’s commitment to make capital investments of at least $1 billion to develop each data center on the property, while promising to invest $4 million over five years in community projects that include public safety and parks and recreation items. John Fishwick, talking to reporters during the news conference, said that the law calls for a hearing on the case within seven working days.
