artigo.texto: An out-of-town data center development firm has locked down a 180-acre site approved last year for a data center campus on the Powhatan-Chesterfield line. An entity tied to Vantage Data Centers out of Colorado last month paid roughly $9.4 million for an assemblage that’s planned to eventually house the Powhatan Technology Park. The property, the majority of which is located at 1318 Page Road, was approved two years ago for a 120-acre data center project that was proposed by California-based Province Group. Then, in October of 2025, Province Group received approvals to tack on 60 additional acres to the original project site for an overall 180-acre campus. The fully assembled site is on the east side of Page Road, just north of the intersection with Anderson Highway, abutting Chesterfield County. As detailed last year in county staff reports, the total roughly 180 acres were slated to eventually house up to four detached data center buildings with a total of 2 million square feet, in what has been described as the biggest data center project the county has ever had on the table. Per a Powhatan County representative, the sale of the original 120-acre tract closed Oct. 21 for $5.7 million. A sale of the additional roughly 60-acre parcel closed on the same day for $3.65 million. The buyer was Powhatan Technology Park LLC. Vantage Data Centers confirmed its purchase of the Powhatan Tech Park site in an email on Friday. “We are evaluating opportunities for future development at the location, but we do not have any additional details to share at this time,” a company representative wrote to BizSense. “We look forward to engaging with local stakeholders and the community as planning progresses and will share more information when available.” The sale had not yet been reflected in online property records as of Friday afternoon. The previous owner of the 120-acre tract is listed in online property records as New County Line Farm LLC, an entity tied to Harold and Christina Ellis, while the previous owner of the 60-acre parcel is listed as JMS Investments LLC, which is tied to Mark and Deborah Sowers. The nature of the relationship between Province Group and Vantage Data Centers regarding the Powhatan project is unclear; however, in an email late Friday afternoon, a Powhatan County representative confirmed Province Group remains involved in the project. The Powhatan County representative also stated that the county has not yet received a site plan for the project. Province Group CEO Mark Kerslake presented the application for the 60-acre addition to the Powhatan Planning Commission a year ago. In his presentation, he noted that Province Group had an end user lined up for the previously rezoned 120-acre parcel, though it was not clear who that end user was. As of last year, buildout of the overall project from Province Group was anticipated to occur in multiple phases and take at least five years to complete. Vantage was founded in 2010, and has developed dozens of data center campuses across the U.S. and around the world. According to company’s website, it has developed or is developing three data centers in Ashburn in Northern Virginia and one in Fredericksburg. Province Group was founded in 1991 and is headquartered in Newport Beach, California. The website states that it has developed, renovated, acquired or entitled more than 75 projects with a combined value of more than $850 million, including projects in states like California, Colorado, Florida, Georgia and Washington. The proposed Powhatan project was seemingly the company’s first development in the Richmond area. Elsewhere in the region, data center news abounds. Google revealed publicly last week that it is currently doing due diligence on a roughly 1,000-acre site within West Creek Business Park in Goochland County for a potential, 1,200-megawatt data center development. The announcement comes as several other data center developments within Goochland’s tech overlay district are being weighed, to the concern of hundreds of residents on both sides of the Goochland-Henrico county line. Google has also begun construction on a data center campus on a 300-plus-acre site at 2700 Bermuda Hundred Road in eastern Chesterfield next to Meadowville Technology Park, and has several other data center facilities planned for the western end of Chesterfield.

artigo.texto: Pickens County council holds first reading on six-month data center moratorium PICKENS, S.C. (FOX Carolina) - Pickens County Council held the first reading Monday on a proposed six-month moratorium on data centers. What the moratorium would do The moratorium would prevent any new data center development in the county for six months. County leaders worked on defining a data center during Monday night’s meeting. The debate over data centers has been happening across the Upstate. Anderson County adopted a similar six-month moratorium. Residents weigh in Residents attended the meeting. One resident said: “Why wouldn’t we be totally in support of data centers? But let’s manage this. Can we even benefit from it?” “All this needs to be set out in an ordinance up front and not negotiated after the construction’s already begun and the problems are arising,” another resident said. “And that’s what’s happening today in Spartanburg. It’s already designed. It’s out there. People are furious. And they’re negotiating now what the terms are. In many ways. You don’t want to be in that position and put this council in a terrible spot.” What’s next Monday’s vote was only the first reading of the moratorium. A date for the second reading has not been announced. RELATED NEWS: Feel more informed, prepared, and connected with FOX Carolina. For more free content like this, download our apps. artigo.texto: A Lackawanna County judge recently denied a developer’s court challenge that sought to compel Jessup to approve plans for six data centers along Breaker Street after the borough denied them. Judge Terrence R. Nealon rejected West Conshohocken-based Breaker Street Associates LLC’s contention that its proposal for a nearly 210-acre data center campus should be deemed approved due to issues with the timing and substance of Jessup’s denial of its plans last year. Although Breaker Street Associates could have successfully argued deemed approval because Jessup did not properly deny its initial application submitted in June 2025, the developer lost the ability to do so by voluntarily submitting revised plans in July 2025 and October 2025, restarting the 90-day window for the municipality to rule on the applications, Nealon’s Oct. 22 order states. “The owner has not established that it is clear and free from doubt that there is no genuine issue of material fact and that it is entitled to mandamus relief in the form of a deemed approval,” Nealon wrote. “Accordingly, the owner’s motion for peremptory judgment will be denied.” Breaker Street Associates, which shares a West Conshohocken address with Catalyst Commercial Development LLC, wants to build six data centers, ranging from 148,480 square feet to 187,500 square feet, south of Breaker Street off Hill Street, in addition to a 10,000-square-foot admin/security building and a 17.44-acre switchyard/substation area, according to court filings on the project. The location of the switchyard/substation played a key role in Jessup’s denial of the project. Data centers were previously principally permitted in the borough’s mixed-use zoning district south of Breaker Street until council amended its zoning ordinance last year to regulate and restrict data centers. However, the switchyard/substation fell into residentially zoned land north of Breaker Street, which never permitted data centers. The Jessup Zoning Hearing Board denied an appeal from Breaker Street Associates last year that sought zoning relief for that electric infrastructure; the developer is appealing the denial separately. Another firm linked to Catalyst Commercial Development, Sunnyside Road Associates LLC, also proposes a data center next to the Lackawanna Energy Center natural gas power plant on Sunnyside Road near Alberigi Drive. Although Jessup council conditionally approved preliminary land development plans in June for Sunnyside Road Associates to build a 50-foot-tall data center next to the power plant, the developer is appealing the zoning hearing board’s denial of a 20-foot height variance that would have allowed it to build a 70-foot-tall data center. Attorneys Richard M. Williams and Kevin M. Walsh Jr. of Hourigan, Kluger & Quinn in Kingston filed the mandamus complaint June 18 asking the court to approve Breaker Street Associates’ plans and to compel Jessup to approve them. Attempts to reach Williams and Walsh were unsuccessful Monday afternoon. Breaker Street background Breaker Street Associates submitted its initial land development application June 11, 2025, followed by revised applications and plans July 23, 2025, and Oct. 2, 2025, in response to comments from the Lackawanna County Regional Planning Commission. Jessup’s zoning officer denied the initial application June 16, 2025, because of the infrastructure in a residential area. The planning commission sent Breaker Street Associates a letter June 24, 2025, informing the developer that the commission had reviewed its application but would not be accepting it because of the non-permitted use in the residential zone. The planning commission has 90 days to rule on an application, with the countdown beginning after the commission’s next meeting, or in this case, on June 18, 2025, setting a Sept. 16, 2025, deadline. In its mandamus complaint filed this year, Breaker Street Associates argues that the planning commission’s letter was improper under the Pennsylvania Municipalities Planning Code, or MPC, which provides the legal framework for municipal zoning, because it failed to cite specific provisions of Jessup’s Subdivision and Land Development Ordinance, or SALDO, used to deny it. The lawsuit further argues that the borough never ruled on its July 23, 2025, application. As a result, both the June 11, 2025, and July 23, 2025, applications should be deemed approved, according to the filing. The complaint does not reference the revised application submitted in October 2025. Nealon’s order Nealon recognizes in his order that Jessup denied Breaker Street Associates’ initial June 2025 application “without describing the unsatisfied requirements or citing the relevant provisions of the statute or ordinance supporting that denial.” “The Planning Commission’s letter decision does not cite the provisions of the MPC, SALDO, or Zoning Ordinance upon which the Planning Commission relied in rejecting Breaker Street’s land development application,” he wrote. If Breaker Street Associates had relied on only its initial application, it could have sought deemed approval. By voluntarily submitting revised plans with significant changes, it twice reset the 90-day timer, leading to Jessup properly denying the third application in October 2025, according to Nealon’s order. “Breaker Street could have chosen to rely upon its original application on June 11, 2025, and if it considered the Planning Commission’s letter of June 24, 2025, to be insufficient … it had the option to stand firm through September 16, 2025 (i.e., 90 days after the Planning Commission’s next regular meeting on June 18), and assert that its original land development application was deemed approved as of September 17, 2025. artigo.texto: Fórum CarbonWise 2026 Encontro acontece a 12 de novembro e debate oportunidades para transformar o sequestro de carbono numa atividade económica e apresenta plataforma digital para a gestão de projetos. Lisboa, 2 de novembro de 2026: A agricultura e a floresta podem assumir um papel relevante no desenvolvimento do mercado voluntário de carbono, criando novas oportunidades para a valorização do território e dos recursos naturais. Como transformar esse potencial em projetos credíveis e com valor económico é uma das questões em debate no Fórum CarbonWise 2026, que se realiza a 12 de novembro, no Instituto Superior de Agronomia (ISA), em Lisboa. O encontro vai reunir empresários, especialistas, académicos e agentes do mercado para discutir as condições necessárias ao desenvolvimento de projetos de sequestro e armazenamento de carbono, envolvendo diferentes setores de atividade, entre os quais a agricultura e a produção florestal. A iniciativa pretende promover a discussão sobre os desafios associados à criação destes projetos, desde a definição de metodologias e a monitorização dos resultados até aos processos de validação, certificação e comercialização de créditos de carbono. Um dos destaques do Fórum será a apresentação da plataforma digital CarbonWise, desenvolvida para apoiar a gestão integrada de projetos de sequestro de carbono. A ferramenta pretende simplificar processos, assegurar a rastreabilidade da informação e aproximar os diferentes intervenientes ao longo da cadeia de valor do mercado voluntário de créditos de carbono. «O potencial económico do sequestro de carbono só poderá concretizar-se se conseguirmos transformar projetos em ativos credíveis, com metodologias claras, métricas fiáveis e acesso ao mercado. A tecnologia tem aqui um papel determinante para simplificar processos, aumentar a transparência e aproximar todos os agentes ao longo da cadeia de valor», afirma Tiago Braga, anfitrião do Fórum CarbonWise 2026 e CEO do ITGEST Group. Agricultura, floresta e mercado de carbono O desenvolvimento de um mercado de carbono credível exige a participação de diferentes agentes, desde os promotores dos projetos aos agricultores e produtores florestais, passando por empresas, instituições financeiras, entidades certificadoras, universidades e organismos públicos. O Fórum CarbonWise 2026 pretende criar um espaço de partilha de conhecimento e contacto entre estes intervenientes, contribuindo para um mercado mais acessível, transparente e credível. O programa inclui três blocos temáticos: Metodologias de Sequestro e Armazenamento de Carbono; Plataforma do Projeto CarbonWise na Gestão dos Projetos de Sequestro; CarbonCoin e a Bolsa de Transações de Créditos (Marketplace). Serão ainda abordados temas como a gestão digital de projetos, a certificação, as métricas digitais e o papel das instituições financeiras na comercialização de créditos de carbono. A participação é gratuita, as inscrições estão abertas para participação presencial ou por streaming. As vagas presenciais são limitadas. CarbonWise Fórum 2026 Data: 12 de novembro de 2026, a partir das 14h00 Local: Salão Nobre do Instituto Superior de Agronomia, Lisboa Participação: Presencial ou por streaming Inscrições: Projeto integrado na Agenda Mobilizadora CircularTech, financiado pelo Plano de Recuperação e Resiliência e pela União Europeia.

artigo.texto: As more governments put increasing pressure on tech companies to develop more sustainable data centres, to ensure they do not place a further burden on the grid, several tech firms are investing in developing new energy capacity and incorporating other innovative ideas into their facility development. This has led Google to suggest that the development of its new U.S. data centre in Minnesota, and associated energy development, will have a positive benefit on the region’s transmission network. Google has proposed an agreement with Xcel Energy to support significant wind, solar and battery storage development alongside its new 780-MW Project Skyway data centre. The tech giant plans to finance Xcel's addition of 1.4 GW of wind, 200 MW of solar power and 300 MW of battery storage to the grid. While the combined capacity of these projects exceeds the data centre's projected electricity demand, wind and solar generation fluctuate depending on weather conditions, and battery storage does not generate additional electricity. Xcel Energy says the new energy resources will serve the wider grid, benefiting other customers as well as the data centre. Google plans to cover the associated costs under the proposed agreement, including payments for capacity it does not fully use. The aim is to get the residents of Pine Island, Minnesota, on board with its development plans, particularly as 71 per cent of Americans surveyed in a Gallup poll earlier this year opposed the construction of a data centre in their local area. Developing such a significant renewable energy project will also help Google meet its target of operating entirely on carbon-free energy by 2030. The proposed agreement includes minimum demand charges and exit fees, meaning that Google will be required to finance the development of the infrastructure even if the demand for AI decreases. Under the proposed agreement, Google would pay minimum monthly charges based on at least 75 per cent of its contracted capacity, even if its electricity consumption falls below that level. If the company terminates the agreement early, it could face exit fees equivalent to as much as eight years of minimum demand charges. Amanda Rome, executive vice president and chief customer officer at Xcel Energy, explained, “Nobody wants to have a big buildout and then have nowhere for that power to go and nobody to pay for that power… That’s where these protections come in.” The Clean Energy Accelerator Charge (CEAC) agreement model uses the same structure as the Clean Transition Tariff (CTT) Google developed with NV Energy. It is currently pending approval from the Minnesota Public Utilities Commission. In its statement about the agreement, Google’s Head of Energy Market Innovation, Briana Kobor, said, “Google’s partnership with Xcel Energy reimagines how data centres can be served, enabling us to be a catalyst for electricity innovation and helping to ensure our growth supports a cleaner, more affordable energy future for the communities we call home.” The rapid rollout of data centres in the United States is driving up the country’s electricity demand to unprecedented levels. The U.S. DOE Office of Science national laboratory, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, estimates that data centres could account for 11.8 per cent of total U.S. electricity by 2030. Meanwhile, the Energy Information Administration (EIA) projects that electricity consumed by data centre servers could reach between 446 billion and 818 billion kilowatt-hours (BkWh) annually by 2050, accounting for between 22 per cent and 33 per cent of commercial building electricity consumption. This is driving demand for new clean energy capacity to ensure that data centres are not powered by fossil fuels – although several companies still depend on gas-powered plants. As utilities respond to the growing power demand by rapidly building out the grid, which costs billions of dollars to do, they are ultimately expecting the demand for AI data centres to continue. However, if the demand for AI wanes or the government decides to regulate the sector more strictly, electricity demand could fall, potentially leaving consumers to foot the bill for infrastructure upgrades. In addition, the use of clean power in data centre operations is not the only sustainability concern. In October last year, the Minnesota Centre for Environmental Advocacy filed a lawsuit against the city of Pine Island, claiming that the environmental study for the development was vague, initially omitted Google as the end user, and failed to disclose impacts on energy, water, noise, and generators. The initial Alternative Urban Area Review (AUAR) indicated that the new data centre would use approximately 55.7 million gallons of water per year, thereby increasing the city’s total water consumption by approximately 50 per cent. Meanwhile, environmental groups have voiced concerns about the lack of comprehensive groundwater impact analysis. Meanwhile, opponents have questioned whether wastewater discharges may potentially run into the Zumbro River. In a Pine Island survey conducted between 1st and 31st August, 75.8 per cent of participants are against the construction of Project Skyway. While Google has made bold promises to upgrade the grid through clean energy projects, residents and environmental groups have broader concerns about consumer protections and the projects’ environmental impact. So, while Google may be attempting to develop a more “sustainable” data centre, it is failing to win over local residents, who remain concerned about the long-term implications of building a giant AI data centre. artigo.texto: INVERGY Signs Multiple Solar Inverters, BESS Supply Agreements at REI Expo 2026 INVERGY India has signed multiple MoUs and supply agreements with renewable energy companies, including LNK Energy, Enerture Technologies, Plethora Power, RAVC Solutions, SLnko Energy, Sunkind Energy and Indygreen Technologies at REI Expo 2026, covering solar inverters and battery energy storage systems. November 04, 2026. By Mrinmoy Dey INVERGY India has announced that the company has entered into multiple strategic partnerships and supply agreements with renewable energy companies at REI Expo 2026, strengthening its business presence across solar inverters and battery energy storage systems (BESS). The agreements cover collaboration, equipment supply and project execution, creating opportunities for the company to expand its business and support India's growing clean-energy infrastructure requirements. INVERGY signed two Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with LNK Energy, establishing a framework for collaboration across solar PV and battery energy storage systems. The agreements were formalised in the presence of Varun Karad, Co-Founder and CEO, REnergy Dynamics. The MoUs were signed by Deepak Pandey, Founder and Managing Director, INVERGY India, and Kushaagra Nandan, Co-Founder, LNK Green Energy. The company also signed a supply agreement with Enerture Technologies for solar inverters and battery energy storage systems. The agreement was signed by Deepak Pandey and Bhairaw Kumar Mandal, Founder and CEO, Enerture Technologies. The agreement establishes a framework for supply across both product categories, supporting Enerture’s project requirements while creating opportunities for INVERGY to expand its business in solar and storage. INVERGY further signed an MoU with Plethora Power to advance a proposed solar project across multiple sites in Maharashtra. The agreement establishes a framework for project planning and execution, combining INVERGY's technical capabilities with Plethora Power's local coordination and site-level support. The MoU was signed by Deepak Pandey and Vaibhav Tyagi, Managing Director and CEO, Plethora Power. In another development, INVERGY signed an MoU and supply agreement with RAVC Solutions for solar inverter supply. The agreements aim to support business expansion and address RAVC's evolving project requirements. The signing involved Deepak Pandey and Ram Anuj Verma, Director, RAVC Solutions. RAVC brings expertise across solar engineering, procurement, construction and operations. INVERGY also entered into a solar inverter supply agreement with SLnko Energy to support its project requirements. The agreement was signed by Deepak Pandey and Pradeep Kankarwal of SLNKO Energy. SLNKO's engineering, procurement, EPC and project management capabilities are expected to complement INVERGY's inverter technology portfolio. The company signed another solar inverter supply agreement with Sunkind Energy, supporting future procurement and supply requirements for solar projects. The agreement was signed by Deepak Pandey and Hanish Gupta, Founder and Managing Director, Sunkind Energy. Additionally, INVERGY India signed an MoU with Indygreen Technologies to establish a framework for future engagement in business development, technology and knowledge exchange. The agreement was signed by Deepak Pandey and Prasoon Chaudhary, Director, INVERGY, and Inderjit Singh, Founder and Managing Director, Indygreen Technologies. Indygreen's expertise in solar PV and lithium battery manufacturing technologies complements INVERGY's capabilities in solar inverters and energy storage. artigo.texto: Trending MAYVILLE - Due to legal questions, county lawmakers tabled a proposal that would prohibit the Chautauqua County Industrial Development Agency from providing tax breaks to future data centers. The Democratic caucus had proposed a resolution titled "Adopting a Uniform Tax Exemption Policy ... Providing that the Chautauqua County Industrial Development Agency Shall Not Consent to Real Property Tax Exemptions, Mortgage Recording Tax Exemptions, or Sales and Use Tax Exemptions for Data Center Projects." The resolution did not go before any committees before being brought up to a vote at its October meeting. There does not appear to be any urgency on the matter. Currently the state is under a moratorium on any new data centers, which was issued by Gov. Kathy Hochul and runs through July, 2027. During the legislature meeting, Legislator Bob Bankoski, D-Dunkirk, acknowledged the legal issues surrounding the topic. "The county attorney believes that the county does not have the legal authority that the proposed resolution would purport to exercise," he said. He recommended the resolution be sent to committee for further evaluation. The full legislature unanimously approved sending the resolution to committee. According to the state Department of Taxation and Finance website, an Industrial Development Agency is a public benefit corporation established under state law (such as in New York) to promote local economic growth, job creation, and business investment. Because of this, IDA legal counsel Milian Tyler questioned the resolution's authority, to which county attorney Nathan Harp acknowledged. Before the decision was made to send the resolution to committee, Legislator Fred Larson, D-Jamestown, said data centers are very unpopular and the resolution should be seen as the legislature providing its own input. "Americans today are reluctant to accept additional data centers in their communities," he said. The only community that has had any sort of discussion on having a data center is the town of Portland, which local residents have strongly opposed. Town officials later said no formal proposals have been made. During the public portion of the legislature meeting, Portland resident Carla Rodriguez, who is running for county legislator District 7, said she opposes data centers. "I believe economic development is important. It must be beneficial to our residents and not place an additional financial burden to our taxpayers. Data centers consume a significant amount of electricity and often create very few permanent jobs," she said. Back in 2018, the county legislature passed a resolution requesting the county IDA to approve no further Payment In Lieu Of Taxes agreements for wind energy projects larger than 5 megawatts rated capacity. When the resolution was passed, George Borrello was the county executive at the time. Following the 2018 vote, he acknowledged the issue with authority of the county IDA. "We do not have the ability to mandate policy. That being said, this body is certainly sending this recommendation, and I fully expect the IDA board to follow that recommendation," he said in an interview eight years ago.

artigo.texto: Principais Conclusões - O S-1 da Anthropic, tornado público em 26 de outubro, afirma que a empresa agora arrenda seus próprios data centers e os chips de IA dentro deles, além de alugar poder computacional da Amazon e do Google da Alphabet. - Isso transforma um dos dois maiores clientes de IA da AWS em um rival parcial e limita quanto da crescente conta de computação da Anthropic a AWS pode conquistar além de seu contrato atual. - O compromisso de $110 bilhões da Anthropic com a AWS vai até 2036, enquanto a Amazon gastou $132 bilhões em capex em 2025 e espera cerca de $220 bilhões em 2026. - Os resultados da Amazon de 29 de outubro mostraram o crescimento da AWS acelerando para 39% e sua carteira de pedidos em aberto subindo para $578 bilhões, e o CEO Andy Jassy projeta crescimento da AWS acima de 40% tanto em 2027 quanto em 2028. Amazon (AMZN) tem um novo concorrente na nuvem, e é um de seus maiores clientes. O S-1 da Anthropic, tornado público em 26 de outubro, diz que a criadora do Claude agora arrenda chips de IA diretamente e os opera em data centers arrendados e operados para ela, construídos sob suas próprias especificações. Isso vem além de alugar poder computacional da Amazon e da Alphabet (GOOG). A Anthropic chama o esforço de Anthropic Direct. O S-1 nomeia a Fluidstack, a empresa por trás do acordo de $50 bilhões em data centers no Texas e Nova York que a Anthropic anunciou em novembro de 2025, como uma parceira que desenvolve e opera data centers para ela, e a Anthropic planeja assinar mais contratos de arrendamento. No episódio de 27 de outubro do Prof G Markets, o investidor Paul Kedrosky resumiu o que isso significa: "Eles estão essencialmente replicando a AWS, Amazon Web Services, em ambas as direções." Ele quer dizer que a Anthropic está construindo tanto os produtos que os clientes usam quanto a nuvem por baixo deles. Em sua visão, a Anthropic tem pouca escolha. Depender de seus maiores concorrentes a deixa exposta, então ela precisa fazer investimentos duplicados para parar de depender deles, tanto estrategicamente quanto pela fatia que eles tomam nas vendas através de seus marketplaces de nuvem. Ele espera que os gastos acelerem daqui para frente. Para a AWS, isso significa um grande cliente planejando uma saída parcial. A Amazon Construiu para Esta Demanda A Anthropic se comprometeu com $110 bilhões para a AWS até 2036, vinculados aos chips Trainium da Amazon, e $114,5 bilhões para o Google da Alphabet até 2033, de acordo com a leitura do S-1 pela CNBC. A Amazon gastou pesadamente para estar pronta para contas desse tamanho. Seus gastos de capital mais do que dobraram de $52,7 bilhões em 2023 para $132 bilhões em 2025… E a administração espera cerca de $220 bilhões em capex em caixa em 2026, um número que reafirmou em 29 de outubro. O TIKR Acompanha 60 Analistas na Amazon. Quantos Dizem "Comprar"? Veja a divisão completa das recomendações de Compra, Manter e Venda na Amazon, junto com as estimativas de receita e lucro do Wall Street, tudo em um só lugar. Mais de 500.000 investidores usam o TIKR para pesquisar ações como esta. Veja as Recomendações dos Analistas para a Amazon Essa construção consumiu a maior parte do fluxo de caixa livre da Amazon, que caiu de $32,9 bilhões em 2024 para um magro $7,7 bilhões em 2025… Pela própria métrica da Amazon, o fluxo de caixa livre nos 12 meses até 30 de setembro foi uma saída de $42,4 bilhões, contra $7,6 bilhões três meses antes. Portanto, cada dólar de demanda de IA que a AWS mantém importa para quando esse gasto se pagar. O Anthropic Direct não aparecerá muito no próprio capex da Anthropic, no entanto. O S-1 diz que ela obtém os chips através de arrendamentos de equipamentos e os edifícios também através de arrendamentos, então a construção aparece como compromissos de arrendamento de longo prazo em vez de gastos antecipados. Os Contratos São um Piso A AWS mantém esses $110 bilhões de qualquer maneira. O S-1 da Anthropic diz que seus acordos de computação de longo prazo a obrigam a pagar pela capacidade independentemente de quanto ela realmente use, então, por enquanto, o Anthropic Direct adiciona data centers além do que a Anthropic já deve à Amazon. A AWS também não está sem compradores. Jassy disse em 23 de outubro que a capacidade da AWS está praticamente esgotada até 2027, com uma boa parte de 2028 já comprometida. O potencial de alta é o que encolhe. A carteira de pedidos em aberto da AWS mais do que dobrou de $244 bilhões no final de 2025 para $496 bilhões em 30 de junho de 2026, conforme a Anthropic e a OpenAI adicionaram $100 bilhões ou mais em compromissos cada uma. Esse tipo de salto da Anthropic fica mais difícil de repetir uma vez que ela preenche seus próprios edifícios primeiro. Além disso: a Amazon possui uma grande parte da Anthropic, uma participação que ela contabilizou em $190,4 bilhões em 30 de junho. A Anthropic diz que operar seus próprios data centers pode trazer vantagens de custo de longo prazo. Kedrosky diz que suas margens só se sustentam se o custo computacional de cada token continuar caindo. Se possuir seus próprios data centers ajudar nisso, a Amazon recupera parte do benefício como acionista. O que o Q3 da Amazon Diz Sobre o Risco da Anthropic Os resultados de 29 de outubro da Amazon responderam parte da pergunta. A receita da AWS cresceu 39% para $46,0 bilhões, seu sexto trimestre consecutivo de crescimento mais rápido, com uma margem operacional de 38,7%. A carteira de pedidos em aberto saltou para $578 bilhões de $496 bilhões em três meses, e Jassy a chamou de "bem diversificada." Ele também projetou crescimento da AWS acima de 40% tanto em 2027 quanto em 2028. A Amazon não disse quanto desses $82 bilhões veio dos dois laboratórios. Os próprios data centers da Anthropic não prejudicarão a AWS este ano ou no próximo, e o contrato protege a Amazon até 2036. artigo.texto: Siga A Crítica de Campo Grande no Google Veja nossas notícias com mais destaque nas suas buscas. Siga A Crítica de Campo Grande no Google Veja nossas notícias com mais destaque nas suas buscas. Veja o resumo da notícia - O Brasil se destaca como destino para investimentos em data centers, impulsionado por energia renovável e crescimento tecnológico. - A expansão acompanha o avanço da inteligência artificial no país, com o Brasil sendo o terceiro maior mercado do ChatGPT. - Grandes empresas de tecnologia, como Google, Amazon e Microsoft, já anunciaram bilhões em investimentos na infraestrutura brasileira. - A demanda interna e as dificuldades de construção nos EUA aumentam o interesse pelo mercado brasileiro de data centers. - A legislação Redata oferece redução de impostos para equipamentos de data centers que cumpram requisitos de investimento local. - Apesar dos benefícios, a expansão levanta questões sobre a dependência tecnológica e impactos ambientais dos projetos. O Brasil pode se tornar um dos principais destinos para novos investimentos em data centers, estruturas responsáveis pelo processamento e armazenamento de dados utilizados por serviços digitais e inteligência artificial. Enquanto comunidades dos Estados Unidos resistem à construção dessas instalações, o mercado brasileiro atrai empresas internacionais pela oferta de energia renovável, pelo crescimento do consumo de tecnologia e por mudanças na legislação tributária. A expansão acompanha o avanço da inteligência artificial no país. Segundo dados da OpenAI citados pela revista Fortune, os brasileiros enviam aproximadamente 215 milhões de mensagens diárias ao ChatGPT. Com isso, o Brasil ocupa a terceira posição entre os mercados da plataforma em número de usuários semanais, atrás apenas dos Estados Unidos e da Índia. As grandes empresas de tecnologia já ampliam seus investimentos no território brasileiro. O Google pretende dobrar sua infraestrutura de computação em nuvem no país até 2030. Já a Amazon Web Services investiu mais de US$ 3,8 bilhões em data centers desde 2011 e anunciou outros US$ 1,8 bilhão até 2034. Além disso, a Microsoft destinou US$ 2,7 bilhões à infraestrutura de nuvem e inteligência artificial ao longo de três anos. Até agora, a demanda interna tem sido o principal motor da expansão dos data centers na América Latina. Entretanto, especialistas avaliam que as dificuldades para construir novas instalações nos Estados Unidos podem aumentar o interesse pelo Brasil. Carlos Barrera, presidente da Atlas Renewable Energy, considera a região uma alternativa para empresas que enfrentam limitações de capacidade no mercado norte-americano. Energia e incentivos fiscais atraem investimentos Um dos principais diferenciais brasileiros está na geração de eletricidade. Segundo relatório do Ministério de Minas e Energia mencionado pela Fortune, quase 87% da energia elétrica produzida no país vem de fontes renováveis. Além disso, o custo da eletricidade é inferior à metade do registrado nos Estados Unidos, fator importante para instalações que precisam funcionar continuamente. Por outro lado, a expansão exigirá investimentos na rede de transmissão para conectar os novos empreendimentos ao sistema elétrico. Também existem preocupações sobre possíveis aumentos nas contas de luz. Assim, a disponibilidade de energia não elimina os desafios de infraestrutura que acompanham o crescimento do setor. Para estimular os projetos, o governo federal sancionou, em 15 de setembro, uma legislação que reduz impostos sobre equipamentos destinados a data centers que cumpram determinados requisitos. O programa, chamado Redata, busca diminuir os custos de instalação e aumentar a capacidade de processamento de dados no território nacional. Pelas regras apresentadas na reportagem, as empresas beneficiadas devem oferecer pelo menos 10% dos serviços computacionais elegíveis a clientes brasileiros. Além disso, precisam investir em pesquisa e desenvolvimento no país o equivalente a 2% do valor dos equipamentos contemplados pelos incentivos fiscais. Expansão também levanta questões ambientais O governo brasileiro espera que a instalação de mais data centers reduza a dependência de serviços estrangeiros. Atualmente, cerca de 60% dos dados digitais brasileiros são processados fora do país, segundo o Ministério do Desenvolvimento. Dessa forma, ampliar a infraestrutura nacional também faz parte da estratégia de fortalecer a capacidade tecnológica brasileira. Entretanto, a política desperta questionamentos. A pesquisadora Ana Carolina de Assis Nunes, do instituto Data & Society, observa que o Brasil pretende diminuir sua dependência tecnológica, mas oferece benefícios fiscais a empresas estrangeiras que já dominam o mercado. Na avaliação dela, esse cenário exige atenção aos efeitos econômicos e sociais dos investimentos. A expansão também enfrenta resistência ambiental. Antes da entrada em vigor do Redata, procuradores federais recorreram à Justiça contra um projeto de data center ligado ao TikTok. Eles solicitaram um estudo de impacto ambiental e uma consulta ao povo indígena Anacé antes do funcionamento da instalação. Apesar desses obstáculos, executivos do setor avaliam que a presença de data centers pode gerar benefícios além da capacidade de processamento, como melhorias na conectividade e maior disponibilidade de serviços digitais. O avanço dos projetos, porém, dependerá da capacidade brasileira de conciliar investimentos, oferta de energia, proteção ambiental e desenvolvimento tecnológico.

artigo.texto: The SunEnergyXT 500 Lite is an all-in-one storage system for balcony power plants and small PV systems, featuring 3 kWh of usable capacity, four MPP trackers, a bidirectional inverter, and an emergency power outlet. It costs 999 euros (MSRP) and has been available from SunEnergyXT retailers since November 2, 2026. The enclosure houses all the hardware from the 5-kWh SunEnergyXT 500 model. You can unlock the missing 2 kWh later via the app for 399 euros, if needed. Sounds like an affordable entry point. Whether it actually is, however, depends on what you’re comparing it to. We’ve done the math. The most important facts at a glance - SunEnergyXT 500 Lite: 3 kWh usable, MSRP 999 euros (about 333 euros per kWh) - Same hardware as the SunEnergyXT 500; software upgrade to 5 kWh for 399 euros - Cells operate only between 20 and 80 percent state of charge; according to the manufacturer, at least 13,000 cycles - 800 W to the home electrical system, 2,400 W at the emergency power outlet, UPS switchover in 10 ms - Up to 2,500 W PV input, grid charging at 2,400 W for dynamic electricity rates - The Lite Plus upgrade costs 1,398 euros; the standard 500 model is currently available for 1,299 euros Same hardware, smaller operating range SunEnergyXT does not install a smaller battery in the 500 Lite. Instead, the firmware limits the usable range: The LFP cells operate continuously between 20 and 80 percent State of Charge (SoC). With a rated capacity of 5,024 Wh—as specified by SunEnergyXT for the 500 series battery—60 percent works out to almost exactly 3 kWh. So the math adds up. This has two consequences. The good one: A battery that never gets completely full or completely empty ages more slowly. SunEnergyXT specifies at least 13,000 charge cycles for the Lite. For the standard 500, it’s over 10,000 cycles, measured at an 80 percent depth of discharge, 25 °C, and 0.5C. The press release does not specify the conditions under which the 13,000 cycles were determined. Both models come with a ten-year warranty. The downside: You’re carrying the entire unit around with you. Even the Lite weighs about 58 kg and measures 536 × 379 × 307 mm. Anyone hoping for a lighter storage solution for their balcony won’t find it here. The unlockable model itself isn’t new to SunEnergyXT. With the 500 PRO AC Core, the MPP trackers are disabled by default and can be activated via an app upgrade; with the 500 Lite, it’s now the capacity that’s restricted. The 2 kWh upgrade costs 399 euros and is available as an in-app purchase; you don’t need to replace any hardware. The SunEnergyXT app has supported the Lite since version 1.8.8, released on October 21. SunEnergyXT has not specified whether, after the upgrade, approximately 4.8 kWh will be usable—as with the 500—or whether the 13,000-cycle specification will still apply. We assume that the specifications for the standard 500 will then apply. SunEnergyXT 500 Lite: Technical Specifications One detail doesn’t quite add up: The press release lists three occupied inputs, each rated at 800 W, as an alternative to 4 × 625 W. In the FAQ for the 500 Series, however, SunEnergyXT specifies 800 W per channel when only two inputs are occupied. Anyone who wants to distribute their modules across three trackers should check the data sheet before purchasing. 500 Lite or the SunEnergyXT 500? The Breakdown The 500 Series now consists of four models. Two are suitable for balcony power plants: the 500 Lite and the SunEnergyXT 500. The 500 PRO, with 2,400 W of grid feed-in capacity, is best handled by a professional installer; the 500 PRO AC Core is an AC-coupled retrofit storage system that comes from the factory without active PV inputs. Based on the MSRP of the 500, you save 301 euros with the Lite Plus Upgrade. However, hardly anyone pays the MSRP: SunEnergyXT itself and retailers have been selling the 500 for 1,299 euros for months now. At that price, you’d pay an extra 99 euros for the Lite Plus upgrade and end up with the same storage unit. Per kilowatt-hour, the Lite is therefore the more expensive model. Its selling point is the lower starting price, not the better deal. Anyone who already knows they need 5 kWh should buy the 500 right away. 3-kWh balcony power plant storage: Who is it enough for? 3 kWh may sound like a small amount compared to the 500, but for a balcony power plant storage unit, it’s a solid capacity. The MOVA LumeGret A2000, for example, starts at 1.92 kWh for 849 euros. With two to four modules on the balcony and a household that uses a few kilowatt-hours in the evening and at night, the Lite is well utilized. Larger storage units often remain half-empty in the winter and on overcast days anyway. The Lite is particularly appealing to three groups: - You have a fixed budget of around 1,000 euros but still want emergency power and grid charging. - You’re starting with just a few modules and want to expand later without replacing the unit. - You already own a SunEnergyXT BK215 Plus and are looking for a second battery for a different application. On the other hand, if you’re looking for a simpler all-in-one system with a smaller battery, there are alternatives. At the other end of the spectrum is the Anker SOLIX Solarbank Max with 7 kWh for 2,199 euros. Connection and Registration According to VDE-AR-N 4105:2026-03 With an output of 800 W when connected to the grid, the 500 Lite is classified as a small-scale generation system under the new VDE-AR-N 4105:2026-03 standard. You can handle the registration with the grid operator yourself using the simplified procedure; registration in the market master data registry is mandatory in any case. However, the press release omits a point that SunEnergyXT itself mentions in the FAQ for the 500 series: The connection is only compliant with the standard if made via an energy outlet, such as a Wieland outlet. A standard Schuko outlet alone is not sufficient. If you do not yet have an energy outlet, a qualified contractor must ins

artigo.texto: Coastal Georgia voters in Chatham and Effingham counties flipped a key state House of Representatives seat from Republican to Democrat on Tuesday, amid a wave of anger about higher prices and over a local Republican decision to approve a $20 billion data center in the area. The win for David Dillie, 24, over incumbent Bill Hitchens, a 79-year-old U.S. Marine Corps veteran, represents the first Democratic victory for House District 161 in 14 years. Unofficial voting totals show Dillie winning by 51.8% to 48.2%. Browse 2026 Elections: Candidate lists, news Stories on projects, policy, legislation Dillie, a pipefitter and first-time candidate, successfully rode an anti-establishment wave that surged in the district after Effingham County’s development authority announced a deal with OpenAI to build a hyperscale data center near multiple residential communities in the rapidly developing area. He also appears to have benefitted from the growing diversity of Pooler, where young professionals have moved in droves in recent years because of rising costs of housing in Savannah. “We can’t talk about change unless we are part of the change,” said Chelsey Barnes, a local law enforcement officer and mother of two who came to vote before lunchtime at Rice Creek Elementary School. Dillie also successfully fought off a challenge to his candidacy based on unfounded allegations that he had voted twice in two separate states this year. Georgia Secretary of State’s Office confirmed the combined total of early votes, absentee ballots and in-person votes is more than 3.9 million, marking a turnout of 51.3%. The turnout rate of eligible voters in Georgia in the 2022 midterm general election was 51.9%, just over four points higher than the national average. Dillie’s victory in the district next to House Speaker Jon Burns’ constituency illustrates how the powerful House leader will have to navigate a smaller majority to pass key legislation in 2027.

artigo.texto: AI data center boom supercharges Korean power equipment industry Surging U.S. demand for data centers and grid upgrades is driving strong earnings and exports for Korean power equipment makers HD Hyundai Electric and LS Electric. Two workers monitor the automated process at HD Hyundai Electric's smart transformer factory in Ulsan in an undated photo.HD HYUNDAI ELECTRIC The global rush to build electricity-hungry AI data centers is driving a surge in earnings for Korean electrical equipment manufacturers. HD Hyundai Electric posted an 18.5 percent jump in third quarter revenue this year compared to the same period last year, according to its preliminary earnings report on Tuesday. It earned revenue of 1.18 trillion won ($878 million). Its operating profit also surged 15.1 percent from last year’s third quarter to 284.5 billion won. Its cumulative operating profit for the first nine months reached 829.8 billion won, which puts the company on track to surpass 1 trillion won in annual operating profit for the first time if the momentum continues. LS Electric’s revenue also surged 54.4 percent on year to 1.88 trillion won in the third quarter. Its operating profit more than doubled to 233.5 billion won. The company also extended its streak of quarterly operating profits to 100 consecutive quarters, a run that began in the fourth quarter of 2001. The strong earnings reflect converging demand drivers, particularly in the United States, where rapid expansion of AI data centers and semiconductor plants has coincided with efforts to replace aging power grids. The consequential demand surge has benefited manufacturers of transformers and other electrical equipment. Korea's electrical equipment exports jumped 74 percent from $4.54 billion in 2021 to $7.9 billion last year, according to trade statistics from the Korea International Trade Association. Exports reached a monthly record of $980 million in September, up 39.9 percent from the previous year. “Demand for distribution transformers has grown, particularly in the semiconductor industry, and sales of power distribution equipment have increased in North America,” HD Hyundai Electric said. “Revenue from the battery energy storage system project on Anjwa Island in Shinan County, Jeonnam-Gwangju, which we secured last December, has also begun to contribute significantly to our results.” LS Electric similarly attributed its strong performance to an increasing number of high-value projects, including power solutions for AI data centers and extra-high-voltage transformers. Both companies are ramping up efforts to expand their presence in North America. LS Electric is leveraging its manufacturing presence in Utah and Texas. The company recently signed a long-term deal worth 168.9 billion won to supply high-voltage switchgear to a U.S. tech giant. Its cumulative orders from U.S. fuel cell maker Bloom Energy have surpassed $500 million. HD Hyundai Electric announced plans to invest an additional 198 billion won to expand its Cheongju Power Distribution Campus in North Chungcheong. The expansion is intended to boost production capacity to meet growing North American demand for distribution transformers. “Big Tech customers continue to request additional orders,” an HD Hyundai Electric representative said during an earnings conference call on Tuesday. “We expect revenue from distribution transformers to at least double next year.” Yet concerns about overheating investment in AI data centers could pose a risk to the industry's growth. At least 47 data center projects in the United States were delayed or suspended this year, largely because of financing difficulties and opposition from local communities, according to the Financial Times on Oct. 18. artigo.texto: Topeka mayor says city employees held unauthorized meeting over proposed data center TOPEKA, Kan. (WIBW) - Topeka Mayor Spencer Duncan said he was recently informed that two City employees had an unauthorized meeting discussing a proposed data center. Mayor Duncan said the two employees met with a legal representative and several Rural Water District 3 board members and discussed the water service and the proposed Compass data center project. Duncan said the meeting was completely unauthorized. In a statement on Facebook, he said: Duncan went on to say that the interim city manager will address the issue with the employees directly and that the appropriate actions will be taken. He emphasized that the matter is being taken seriously. All City staff are required to take any matters involving data centers directly to the interim city manager’s office, the mayor’s office, and the City Council. In addition, City legal counsel must be involved before considerations or further steps are taken. “Organizations seeking discussions about water service for a data center must bring those matters to the full governing body through the established public process. Staff cannot independently negotiate, make commitments or advance those requests.” The mayor emphasized that nothing discussed during the Friday meeting constitutes an approved City position, authorization, or commitment, and the City will not take any action based on those discussions. Future considerations must follow the required public process and receive appropriate governing body approval. The following actions and safeguards were put in place by the City and will remain in effect: - The City’s one-year moratorium on data centers within city limits remains in place. Friday’s meeting did not change or create an exception to it. - City Council approval is required for requests to provide City water to data centers outside city limits. The Council established that requirement on August 11 so these decisions would come before elected officials in public rather than be handled through administrative approval. - The City continues its policy and research work, including work with the Sustainability Advisory Board on standards addressing water use, energy demands, noise and other community impacts. Review of water capacity, infrastructure needs, utility impacts and economic considerations remains part of that work. - No annexation request for these projects is before the City, and the City is not advancing annexation steps on their behalf. Any future request would require its own consideration through the appropriate public process. - Public involvement remains essential. Any proposal requiring City action must come before the governing body with clear information, public discussion and an opportunity for residents to be heard. Duncan said the proposed projects discussed recently are outside of the Topeka city limits, where Shawnee County has zoning and land use authority. Find Duncan’s full statement on Facebook here. artigo.texto: Plataformas Broadcast Soluções de Dados e Conteúdos Soluções de Tecnologia 3 de novembro de 2026, às 17:40 Por Circe Bonatelli São Paulo, 03/11/2026 – As gestoras Emet Capital e B.real anunciaram nesta terça-feira, 3, a captação de R$ 120 milhões junto a investidores estrangeiros para o fundo de investimento em participações (FIP) Data Brasil Infra. O veículo é destinado ao desenvolvimento de terrenos com infraestrutura de energia para a instalação futura de data centers. “Nós compramos o terreno, ligamos a rede elétrica, construímos os prédios com as hacks de computadores e abrimos o espaço para locatários”, explicou Raffael Faustino, sócio e fundador da Emet Capital – a casa tem 17 fundos e atingiu R$ 1,5 bilhão em ativos sob gestão. A proposta é atender a demanda cada vez maior por infraestrutura digital no Brasil, puxada por expansão da computação em nuvem, inteligência artificial (IA) e maior consumo de dados. O veículo tem uma carteira de nove projetos e prevê investimentos de R$ 2,5 bilhões nos próximos três anos. A expectativa é levantar outros R$ 100 milhões até o começo do ano que vem para ampliar os investimentos. Os projetos estão distribuídos por Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Centro-Oeste e Nordeste. Entre esses projetos um fica em Seropédica, na Baixada Fluminense. O movimento se soma a uma corrida por investimentos no setor, em que a disponibilidade de energia, a proximidade de redes de fibra ótica e a previsibilidade regulatória são fatores decisivos. Se os projetos avançarem, podem atrair capital adicional e consolidar um pipeline de ativos, fortalecendo a presença das gestoras em um segmento de infraestrutura com potencial de crescimento e receitas de longo prazo. Coloque a eixos nas suas fontes preferidas do Google Veja nossas notícias com mais destaque nas suas buscas. Realizar o leilão de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em dezembro, no meio de uma discussão no Congresso sobre o rateio dos custos de contratação das baterias, é uma “irresponsabilidade regulatória”, afirmou a sócia do Fernanda De Paula Advocacia e Consultoria Jurídica, Fernanda De Paula. Em entrevista ao estúdio eixos, durante a EVEx Lisboa 2026, a advogada defendeu que a Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel) suspenda o cronograma da licitação para um diálogo transinstitucional, diante das perspectivas de mudança nas regras. Confira na íntegra. “Hoje, com a atual situação do país, é uma irresponsabilidade regulatória a gente fazer um leilão de baterias sem que a gente conheça todos os preços e todos os custos envolvidos. E por que eu estou dizendo isso? A gente tem hoje um cenário de modificação, de tentativa de modificação legislativa, que é importante”. Fernanda De Paula faz referência à aprovação, na Câmara dos Deputados, em outubro, do requerimento de urgência para o projeto de lei 3716/2026, que altera o rateio dos custos da contratação de sistemas de armazenamento (BESS). O PL, de autoria de Arnaldo Jardim (Cidadania/SP), altera a lei nº 15.269/2025, que estabelece que o custo do armazenamento é arcado pelas geradoras de energia. A nova proposta estabelece a divisão dos valores com os consumidores. A advogada cita o risco de que, uma vez aprovado o PL, que o leilão seja judicializado. “Se o projeto de lei passar, a gente teria que cancelar o leilão, refazer as fases de precificação. Porque já que isso vai para o consumidor final, isso vai ter um custo diferenciado. Até acho que na matemática isso não vai ter um impacto tão grande – a gente só está trocando quem paga os custos… Mas fato é que muda a matemática de pra onde a conta vai”, completou. Principais assuntos tratados: - Leilão de baterias de dezembro pode ser cancelado se o Congresso mudar o rateio, pois empresas já precificaram com a regra atual. - Lei 15.269 manda que o custo seja pago por quem gera, enquanto PL de Arnaldo Jardim e Danilo Forte defende dividir com os consumidores. - Cobrança de TUSD na entrada e na saída é criticada, pois outros países não cobram nada, e Aneel seguiu solução intermediária. - Advogada defende diálogo transinstitucional entre Aneel, Congresso, MME e TCU para suspender o leilão por 45 dias. - Adiamento gera menos insegurança que manter o certame com regra que pode mudar, pois insegurança jurídica eleva custo de capital. - Histórico de judicialização do LRCAP preocupa, e advogada defende fortalecimento de órgãos de controle. artigo.texto: A energia solar gera a maior parte da sua produção durante o dia, enquanto a demanda de eletricidade de muitas residências aumenta à noite. Os Sistemas de Armazenamento de Energia em Baterias (BESS) ajudam a armazenar o excedente de eletricidade para uso quando necessário, aumentando a capacidade de gerenciar proativamente as fontes de energia locais. Com base nessa necessidade, a GG Power desenvolveu o ENERGY HUB S16 NEW, projetado para famílias que utilizam energia solar, com um design adequado para atender às necessidades de longo prazo. A GG Power desenvolve baterias de armazenamento de energia para uso doméstico, visando aumentar o índice de nacionalização da produção. Com a crescente popularidade da energia solar, o desafio para as famílias vai além da simples geração de eletricidade limpa; também envolve o armazenamento e a utilização dessa energia no momento certo. Com o ENERGY HUB S16 NEW, a GG Power visa criar uma linha de baterias de armazenamento de energia "nacional", desenvolvida com base nas necessidades reais e na capacidade de produção das empresas vietnamitas. Este produto utiliza células de bateria Cornex de Grau A – um dos principais fabricantes mundiais de células de bateria – com características térmicas estáveis e uma vida útil projetada de até 8.000 ciclos de carga/descarga. A compatibilidade com muitos modelos populares de inversores híbridos o torna adequado tanto para novos sistemas quanto para atualizações de sistemas existentes. O produto possui classificação de proteção IP21, sendo adequado para instalação em ambientes internos ou protegidos. Seu design compacto e elegante, com conexões traseiras discretas, garante que o dispositivo se integre perfeitamente a qualquer ambiente. Uma característica notável do ENERGY HUB S16 NEW é seu foco na localização, desde a pesquisa até a produção. O produto é desenvolvido por uma equipe de engenheiros vietnamitas e fabricado em uma fábrica em Hung Yen , que ocupa aproximadamente 1,2 hectares, com um sistema de armazenamento de energia (BESS) dedicado com capacidade de até 5 GWh/ano. Simultaneamente, a GG Power está gradualmente construindo uma cadeia de valor nacional, conectando sua capacidade de produção com fornecedores vietnamitas. Atualmente, mais de 20 unidades nacionais participam da cadeia de suprimentos da empresa, com o objetivo de atingir um índice de nacionalização superior a 52% até 2027. Essa direção também se reflete no processo de aprimoramento da linha de produtos ENERGY HUB S16 PRE. Em colaboração com a An Vinh, a GG Power modernizou o revestimento com linhas mais refinadas, aplicando soldagem robótica, jateamento abrasivo e pintura eletrostática a pó. A NCI Vietnam (fornecedora de componentes de longa data e parceira da Honda Vietnam ) é responsável pela produção das etiquetas em relevo 3D para o logotipo e o nome do produto, substituindo o método anterior de serigrafia. A participação de parceiros nacionais contribui para aprimorar tanto a qualidade quanto a aparência dos produtos de armazenamento de energia "Made in Vietnam". Além da capacidade de produção, a GG Power concentra-se na capacidade de fornecer componentes e suporte pós-venda. A empresa construiu um sistema de escritórios de representação e armazéns de componentes nas três regiões do Vietnã, conectando fabricantes com distribuidores, instaladores e usuários. A bateria de armazenamento ENERGY HUB S16 NEW, popular em todo o país, vem com garantia de fábrica de 5 anos e suporte no local; o processo de recebimento de relatórios e fornecimento de suporte técnico no local é organizado para reduzir o tempo de processamento e minimizar o tempo de inatividade. Com a GG Power, o armazenamento de energia em baterias "nacional" atende às necessidades de muitas famílias, com o suporte da capacidade de produção nacional e do ecossistema da cadeia de suprimentos. De uma equipe de engenheiros vietnamitas, uma fábrica em Hung Yen, a uma rede de parceiros e serviços pós-venda em todo o país, a empresa está gradualmente aproximando o ENERGY HUB S16 NEW de 14 milhões de famílias vietnamitas, contribuindo para ampliar sua capacidade de usar energia limpa de forma proativa.

artigo.texto: The African Earth Energy Group (AEEG) is seeking an anchor industrial off-taker for its proposed 49 MW solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage system (BESS) project in Mpumalanga province, South Africa. The project aims to supply reliable and competitively priced renewable electricity to industrial and commercial consumers operating in the region. The proposed facility is strategically located within one of South Africa’s major industrial and smelting corridors. This location provides an opportunity to serve energy-intensive businesses that are looking for alternative electricity procurement options to manage rising power costs and address challenges associated with the national electricity grid. The project will combine utility-scale solar power generation with battery energy storage technology to provide a more stable and dependable electricity supply. Through long-term electricity wheeling arrangements or direct power procurement frameworks, AEEG intends to supply renewable energy to an industrial customer that can benefit from predictable electricity pricing and improved energy security. The integration of battery storage is expected to strengthen the project’s ability to support industrial electricity requirements. Energy storage systems can help manage fluctuations in solar generation by storing electricity produced during periods of strong sunlight and making it available when generation declines or demand increases. This approach can improve the reliability of renewable energy supply for businesses with significant electricity consumption. AEEG has already progressed several development activities for the project. These include detailed site assessments, grid integration planning and engagement with local stakeholders to align the development with regional requirements. These activities represent important steps towards preparing the project for implementation and future commercial operations. Finding a primary industrial off-taker is now a key priority for the company. Securing a long-term electricity buyer would help establish the commercial structure required to advance the project towards financial close. It would also provide greater certainty for investment and project development. The initiative reflects the growing role of private independent power producers (IPPs) in South Africa’s electricity sector. Industrial companies are increasingly exploring renewable energy procurement to reduce dependence on conventional electricity sources, manage operating expenses and meet corporate decarbonization targets. With its proposed combination of solar generation and battery storage, the 49 MW Middelburg project could contribute to strengthening industrial energy security while supporting South Africa’s broader transition towards cleaner electricity. artigo.texto: Google’s Suncatcher Prototype Space Data Center Comes Online and Runs AI in Orbit Google’s Suncatcher prototype space data center is operational and communicating with the ground after reaching orbit earlier this month aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 alongside more than 100 other spacecraft. A spokesperson said the satellite is operating nominally. The satellite carries four Google Tensor Processing Units and generates up to 1 kW of power, though it can run only one TPU at a time for about 20 minutes, complicating communications. After roughly three weeks of commissioning, engineers sent their first prompt, asking the onboard Gemma 4 model to write a haiku about space, and also requested a report on orbital conditions. Testing will now examine how the chips handle thermal stress and space radiation, which can cause bit flips that silently corrupt data. Ground tests suggested radiation would affect inference less than training. If successful, Google plans two more satellites in 2027 with greater power and inter-satellite optical links. Suncatcher stands out for planning high-speed links enabling distributed workloads across closely flying satellites. Both Google and SpaceX, in which Alphabet holds a significant stake, depend on a fully reusable Starship, with Suncatcher researchers estimating it would need about 1,800 flights to achieve key cost reductions. The project targets economical orbital infrastructure in the 2030s.

artigo.texto: Octopus explores home battery storage tech with CATL and Amperex The MoU sees Ampace and Octopus explore combining their hardware and software, respectively, in next-generation smart home energy storage solutions. Octopus Energy has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Xiamen Ampace Technology Limited (Ampace) for domestic energy storage systems. Ampace is a lithium-ion battery technology company formed as a joint venture (JV) in 2021 between Chinese OEM CATL and Hong Kong-headquartered battery manufacturer Amperex Technology Limited (ATL). The MoU sees Ampace and Octopus explore combining their hardware and software, respectively, in next-generation smart home energy storage solutions. Octopus said that the agreement brings together “industry heavyweights”, combining CATL and Ampace’s battery chemistry and manufacturing with the UK company’s software platform, smart tariffs and virtual power plant (VPP) capabilities. The MoU will see the companies collaborate to produce “safer, greener and far more affordable home batteries”. Octopus currently offers a heat pump range and an EV charger range and has announced it will begin offering a home battery range called Octopus Nook. Octopus Nook will be available as a 2kWh plug-in system and a wall-mounted system at 5kWh or 10kWh, both of which will be stackable. No further information, such as the cell technology it will use, is available. According to Raymond Ye, president of residential energy storage systems at Ampace: “By bringing together CATL’s leadership in battery innovation, Ampace’s expertise in energy storage technology and manufacturing, and Octopus Energy’s strengths in digital energy management and services, we see great potential to accelerate innovation and deliver greater value to the market.” It could see Octopus offer European customers home energy storage systems using next-generation battery chemistries, building on Ampace’s research into sodium-ion technology, high-density cell designs, and ultra-long lifecycle systems. The partnership will initially look at opportunities in European markets where Octopus has retail energy offices. Octopus and CATL have previously collaborated in a JV for battery swapping for electric heavy-duty vehicles in Europe, covered on our sister site EV Infrastructure News. CATL actually originated from ATL, which was founded by CATL's chairman and founder, Robin Zeng, in 1999 as a manufacturer of rechargeable lithium batteries. CATL was established as a spin-off in 2011. Read more about:

artigo.texto: Politics chat: Data centers are on everyone's minds going into Election Day With days until Election Day, polls show momentum for Democratic candidates and bipartisan distaste for data centers. AYESHA RASCOE, HOST: Heading into this last weekend before Election Day, nearly 50 million people have already voted, either in person or by mail. The total vote in 2022's midterms was 112 million. This year's on pace to beat that number. NPR senior national political correspondent Mara Liasson joins us now. Good morning, Mara. MARA LIASSON, BYLINE: Good morning. RASCOE: So where do things stand this morning from your point of view? LIASSON: Well, Republicans and Democrats agree privately that the House will most likely go to the Democrats. It's unclear about the margin, probably a bigger one than the tiny majority that Republicans have now. Both sides say they are optimistic about the Senate. Of course, someone has to be wrong. Either Democrats will win the Senate majority, or Republicans will hold onto it. The handful of races that are going to determine the majority in the Senate are all still polling within the margin of error. That means that they're too close to call. Democrats will probably pick up seats in the Senate, but it's not clear if they will get the net four pickups they need to take control. And the states that are going to determine that are Texas, Maine, Alaska, Ohio, Iowa and Kansas, a lot of red states. RASCOE: Campaigns are making their final arguments, and, you know, those are going to vary race to race. In general, though, are there any issues that have risen to the top of voters' minds that stands out to you? LIASSON: Yes, data centers. That was surprising. In the beginning of the cycle, it wasn't clear they would be such a big issue. States had been competing to get data centers to come to their states, but it turns out they are very unpopular. That sentiment is bipartisan. It's an example of the kind of economic populism that we see converging from the left and right. It's why you saw Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon appear at the same anti-AI conference. And data centers is the way that AI is most present to voters in their own communities. Majorities don't want them there. And it's caused some pretty dramatic flip-flops. Incumbent Texas Governor Greg Abbott courted data centers for years. All of a sudden, now he's for a moratorium. And I think they've become a proxy for the backlash against billionaires. You know, the rich get richer while you can't afford gas. And the debate over the data centers also illustrates another big theme of the campaign, which is that Donald Trump is on the opposite side of majority popular opinion. On issue after issue, this is true - on Iran, on tariffs. On data centers, he says he's for them. He's called them a golden goose for the economy. He was in Ohio in October at a rally with Republican incumbent Senator Jon Husted. He said, we want data centers. He says, you can't turn them off. They'll go to China. RASCOE: October has come and gone. Were there any so-called October surprises? LIASSON: Well, I would say the closest thing to an October surprise is the double Dan Sullivan situation in Alaska. The Republican governor there says he's starting an investigation. President Trump has asked his Department of Justice to investigate how Daniel J. Sullivan got on the ballot. The incumbent senator is Dan S. Sullivan. There was some reporting in The New York Times that the Mary Peltola campaign - she's the Democratic candidate - was deeply involved in recruiting Dan J. Sullivan. Peltola denies that. The big question is, is any of this illegal? RASCOE: I mean, that is a big question. Alaska's Supreme Court ruled in June that both Sullivans could appear on the ballot. And this is far from the first example of political parties, for lack of a better term, gaming the vote. LIASSON: That's right. It happens a lot. Both parties do it. There are some examples this cycle. And one of them in Ohio, a Republican group, spent more than $2 million to promote a socialist candidate in the Senate race named Greg Levy. They're hoping to pull away votes from the Democratic candidate, former Senator Sherrod Brown. So sometimes it's a person with a similar name, like in Alaska. Sometimes it's a person who's on the extreme of the opposite party, and the other party backs them in an effort to try to split the vote. Remember when Trump's allies tried to get Kanye West to run for president in hopes that he could split the Black vote? It's just unclear what, if any, laws these kinds of political shenanigans would break. RASCOE: And yet the Justice Department is moving forward with its lawsuit about this, right? LIASSON: That's right. They're asking a judge to separate all ballots in Alaska showing votes for the second Dan Sullivan, Dan J. Sullivan, until it can be determined if voters really meant to vote for him. Alaska officials say that would be impossible. The Trump administration has also filed a lawsuit to block the certification of the Alaska Senate race in case the Republican loses, but Trump doesn't have a good track record in court on these kinds of suits. Last week, U.S. judge Trina Thompson ordered the administration to stop threatening state and local election officials with prosecution if they didn't refuse to issue ballots to people the administration says may be ineligible to vote. So this all adds up to what Trump's critics argue is an effort to try to take control of elections, overturn the results if they don't go his way. RASCOE: That's NPR's Mara Liasson. Mara, thank you so much. LIASSON: You're welcome. Copyright © 2026 NPR. All rights reserved. Visit our website terms of use and permissions pages at www.npr.org for further information.
