artigo.texto: The city of Emporia has spoken and there will be no high-impact data center developments in the community for at least a decade. saw 4,346 votes for yes, meaning approval of the ban, and 2,891 votes for no in relation to the high-impact data center question, or question 2. Question 3, related to battery energy storage systems, saw 4,067 votes for yes and 3,117 votes for no. The questions appeared on the ballot after a citizen’s petition circulated earlier this year, with Emporia Neighbors United leading the effort. Founder and spokesman for Neighbors United Jay Vehige stated in an interview with KVOE News Tuesday night that the results indicate “a new generation in politics is here.” Leading the charge for voting no against the ban was Emporians For Progress. Spokesman Casey Woods noted throughout the past several months that there were concerns a yes vote on the ban could have significant negative implications for the community down the road, notably a reputation of “being closed for business.” Woods stated Tuesday night that while they respect the community’s decision, it does not change the economic challenges Emporia is currently facing. Woods also noted previously that there had been implications from outside entities that potential developments could be lost based on the outcome of the election. He told KVOE News he had some correspondence with such entities during election night and it was “not positive.” The city of Emporia had already taken several steps to prepare for a potential data center development before the election, including enacting policies and approving certain zoning. City Manager Trey Cocking, like Woods, says the city respects the voters’ decision and commended the community for showing up as it did at the polls. As for next steps, Cocking says that is still to be determined at this time. An important note: there is still a legal case pending a final decision on the petition question, with Senior Judge Glen Braun yet to issue a ruling on whether or not the petition was legislative or administrative in nature. Should it be deemed administrative, the prevailing theory has been that it will most likely be null and void. Cocking says there is no word as of yet as to when Braun will issue his ruling on the matter. Vehige, when asked, stated Emporia Neighbors United is very confident the ruling will go in their favor. For Woods, he still sees some glaring issues that need to be addressed with the petition’s wording regardless of the final ruling from Judge Braun. These were just two of the three Emporia-specific special questions on the ballot Tuesday night. Also up for vote was the question regarding a quarter-percent sales tax that would have served as the main funding mechanism for a new Emporia Recreation Center and updates to the Lee Beran Recreation Center. Voters ultimately voted down the tax by an unofficial total of 3,874 to 3,333. Executive director of the Emporia Recreation Center Amanda Gutierrez said that while the loss was discouraging, she was grateful for those who showed up to vote. Even so, Gutierrez said she and her team will continue to push for more recreational opportunities in the future. Adversely, Tuesday night’s election saw the passing of USD 251’s ballot questions 1 and 2. Question one asked if voters in the USD 251 boundaries should approve a nearly $26 million bond for a new high school, while question two asked if voters should approve a better than $5 million bond for a new athletics complex near Americus. KVOE caught up with superintendent of schools Bob Blair, who said he was grateful to the community members who showed up to vote in support of the two special questions, which he said will improve the district greatly. Moving forward, Blair said the district’s work to make the project a beneficial one for all parties involved is just beginning. In a close run for Kansas’ House District 60 seat, Republican Mark Schreiber won the race against Democrat Maddison Glover on Tuesday night– a relief, Schreiber said when KVOE caught up with him after the unofficial election results were released. As a first-time candidate at just 27 years old, Glover said she’s proud of how close she got to taking the seat. With official results still pending, Glover said she’s hopeful she’ll make up the difference. For Kansas House 76, Republican candidate Russel Stukey won the race with 1,907 votes. As he heads into Congress, Stukey said voters can count on him to hold up his end of the campaign bargain to keep local municipalities in control of their own local laws. In Lyon County, the race for the 13th District State Representative seat was close– Republican candidate Duane Droge won the seat by one vote against Democratic candidate Mark Remmert. Lyon County’s unofficial voter turnout came to just under 55 percent, according to Lyon County Election Officer Amie Jones. Jones says it was a good night for the election office, a result she attributes to her election staff. While the election is now complete, work is still ahead for election staff. artigo.texto: The money crunch that has hit AI in recent weeks is coming for the space industry, which shares DNA, investors, and market vibes with artificial intelligence. âIf youâre a high-quality, well-run company with a good balance sheet and a good business model, you are very well positioned because everyoneâs paying attention,â Dylan Taylor, CEO of Voyager Technologies, said on this weekâs episode of Compound Interest. Everyone else is âbeing cast aside.â Voyager builds space infrastructure for the Pentagon and defense contractors, and is working on a commercial space station, Starlab, to replace the International Space Station when it is retired in 2030. The company is publicly traded, which last month allowed it to raise $400 million on terms roughly in line with a hot convertible-debt market. âLow cost of capital [is] a secret weapon,â Taylor said, âbecause the first question is, âhow do you compete with SpaceX?ââ Even Elon Muskâs behemoth is feeling the squeeze: It throttled usage of its Grok AI bot this week because, as Musk said in an X post Sunday, it was getting too expensive. Taylor, like most space executives today, counts Musk as both a competitor (for contracts and capital) and collaborator (Voyagerâs hardware hitches a ride on SpaceXâs rockets). The space and AI trades are increasingly twinned, tapping into similar pools of capital, riding similar national-security vibes, and carrying similar potential of catastrophic escalation. âItâs the same thing,â Taylor said of the two, but for a different reason: their potential to reshape every corner of the economy. âEveryone is in the space industry,â he said. âThey just donât know it yet.â We also talked to Taylor about building data centers in space, which would sidestep the energy needs and political backlash back on Earth. And if they break? Just âbuild more,â is Taylorâs quintessentially American answer.

artigo.texto: Santa Cruz, na Zona Oeste do Rio, vai receber um empreendimento de data center com conclusão prevista para 2030. O projeto será o primeiro investimento de um fundo de R$ 120 milhões criado pelas gestoras Emet Capital e B.Real Capital, que concluíram nesta terça-feira (03/11) a captação de recursos junto a investidores estratégicos. A iniciativa faz parte de um plano de expansão da infraestrutura de armazenamento e processamento de dados no Brasil. Além do terreno em Santa Cruz, as gestoras já identificaram outras duas áreas para futuros empreendimentos, no Ceará e em São Paulo. Os três projetos têm demanda estimada em R$ 1 bilhão. Para viabilizar os investimentos, o fundo Data Brasil Infra FIP pretende abrir uma nova rodada de captação no primeiro trimestre de 2027, com a expectativa de levantar mais R$ 100 milhões. O plano é ainda mais amplo. O fundo tem nove projetos em seu pipeline, distribuídos por São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Minas Gerais, Centro-Oeste e Nordeste. Juntos, eles podem alcançar capacidade de 3,5 gigawatts (GW) e demandar R$ 2,5 bilhões em investimentos nos próximos três anos. A estratégia das gestoras é desenvolver terrenos com acesso garantido a redes elétricas de alta potência, estrutura necessária para a instalação de data centers. Depois, os espaços são destinados a grandes empresas de tecnologia, provedores de serviços digitais e companhias de inteligência artificial, por meio de contratos de locação de longo prazo. Segundo Raffael Faustino, diretor da Emet Capital, a disponibilidade de energia e a localização dos terrenos estão entre os principais fatores para viabilizar projetos desse tipo. A obtenção de autorizações para conexão elétrica de alta capacidade e a construção de subestações podem levar mais de dois anos. O Brasil concentra cerca de 48% da capacidade instalada de data centers da América Latina, segundo levantamento da consultoria imobiliária JLL. Já estimativas da Associação Brasileira das Empresas de Tecnologia da Informação e Comunicação (Brasscom) apontam que os investimentos em tecnologias digitais e infraestrutura no país podem chegar a R$ 2 trilhões até 2029.

artigo.texto: CNTE Named in BloombergNEF's Q4 2026 Tier 1 Energy Storage Manufacturers LONDON, Nov. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Contemporary Nebula Technology Energy Co., Ltd. (CNTE) has been included in BloombergNEF's (BNEF) Q4 2026 Tier 1 Energy Storage Manufacturers List, marking an important milestone in its global expansion and growing international market recognition. BloombergNEF's Tier 1 classification is a widely recognized industry benchmark based on manufacturers' commercial project deployment records, including project scale, independent customer relationships, and verified project experience. As project bankability and delivery capabilities become increasingly important, the classification provides a valuable reference for developers, investors, and industry stakeholders. CNTE's inclusion reflects its expanding international project experience and growing market acceptance, highlighting its continued progress in the global energy storage industry. Full-Scenario Energy Storage Solutions and Global Deployment Established in 2019 with investment from CATL, a global leader in battery technology, CNTE provides full-scenario energy storage solutions covering power generation, grid, and end-user applications, including utility-scale storage, commercial and industrial systems, microgrids, and integrated energy storage and EV charging solutions. CNTE has successfully delivered multiple utility-scale energy storage projects across Europe, particularly in Germany, demonstrating its capabilities in system integration and international project execution. Looking ahead, CNTE will continue advancing energy storage innovation, strengthening global partnerships, and expanding localized service capabilities to support renewable energy integration and the global energy transition. Who We Are CNTE (Contemporary Nebula Technology Energy) was founded in 2019 by Mr. Huang Shilin, co-founder of CATL, and today its second-largest shareholder. We integrate CATL LFP cells into complete systems in-house, with 12 GWh of production capacity, more than 10 GWh shipped worldwide across 2,600+ projects, a European service centre and a 500 MWh project reference in Germany.

artigo.texto: Contemporary Amperex Technology stock holds 39.1% EV battery share Published on 11/03/2026 at 17:11 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller, Editor-in-Chief AD HOC NEWS CATL extends global battery lead - CATL remained the world's largest EV battery supplier through September 2026. - Battery installations grew faster than the global market during the first nine months. - An expanding overseas automaker customer base strengthened CATL's position against BYD. Contemporary Amperex Technology retained its position as the world's largest electric-vehicle battery supplier through September 2026, according to a November 2 report by CnEVPost, which cited figures from South Korean market researcher SNE Research. CATL held a 39.1 percent global share, up from 37.5 percent a year earlier. Scale outpaces global demand CATL's battery installations reached 389.2 gigawatt-hours in the first nine months, an increase of 24.9 percent from the same period a year earlier. Global EV battery usage rose 19.7 percent to 994.5 gigawatt-hours, putting CATL's expansion ahead of the broader market. The figures cover battery-electric vehicles, plug-in hybrids and conventional hybrids. Global installations reached a monthly record of 145.1 gigawatt-hours in September, although year-on-year growth slowed to 15.8 percent. Overseas customers support position SNE Research said CATL continued to expand its overseas automaker customer base, while BYD's battery supply remained largely tied to its own vehicle sales. CATL and BYD together accounted for 54.3 percent of global usage, with BYD in second place at 15.2 percent. Seven Chinese suppliers in the global top ten held a combined 73.0 percent share, up from 69.5 percent a year earlier. The concentration highlights the scale advantage of Chinese producers, while CATL's international customer mix gives investors a separate indicator for growth beyond China's domestic vehicle market. artigo.texto: Five key takeaways from the renewable energy company's September-quarter results Juniper Green Energy reported consolidated revenue from operations of ₹344.66 crore in Q2 FY27, up 2.4 times year-on-year, while EBITDA rose 2.6 times to ₹339.55 crore. Total income increased 132% to ₹371.64 crore, and EBITDA margin expanded to 91.36% from 81.02% a year earlier. The company posted a consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of ₹53.56 crore, against a loss of ₹18.40 crore in Q2 FY26. Cash PAT rose 3.9 times to ₹152.55 crore. The results point to five key developments. 1. Operating scale is driving record earnings The sharp increase in revenue and EBITDA reflects the expansion of Juniper's operating portfolio. The company commissioned 1,036 MWp of renewable energy capacity and around 503 MWh of BESS during the first seven months of FY27. Its operational portfolio has reached 2,844 MWp of renewable capacity and 604 MWh of BESS. 2. Profitability is improving, but financing remains a major cost While EBITDA rose sharply, consolidated finance costs increased to ₹201.14 crore in Q2 FY27 from ₹96.52 crore a year earlier. Depreciation also rose to ₹98.99 crore from ₹57.99 crore. A rising interest rate cycle could impact those numbers further. With the capital-intensive nature of the business, the company's ability to translate operating earnings into sustained net profit will remain an important indicator as its portfolio expands. 3. BESS is emerging as a major growth driver Juniper is targeting approximately 4,500 MWh of BESS installations by June 2027 and 10,000 MWh by March 2028. Its total portfolio already includes 8,989 MWh of BESS capacity, operational and under construction. The targets point to a substantial expansion of storage alongside renewable generation, although the company has not provided a separate revenue or earnings outlook for the storage business. 4. A large project pipeline offers visibility Juniper's total portfolio stands at 11,218 MWp of renewable capacity and 8,989 MWh of BESS. The company says 98% of its portfolio is secured through long-term power purchase agreements, typically spanning 25 years, while 98% of offtakers carry ratings of A or above. It also has surplus grid connectivity of more than 5,200 MW available for future bids. 5. Growth continues to demand substantial capital Juniper has incurred ₹18,895 crore in cumulative capital expenditure through September 2026, including ₹2,591 crore in Q2 alone. Its consolidated borrowings remain substantial, reflecting the investment required to build its operating portfolio. The company also received an upgrade in its credit rating to AA- (Stable) from ICRA.

artigo.texto: Nós nos acostumamos a utilizar a inteligência artificial em tarefas cotidianas, como tirar dúvidas rápidas ou traduzir um texto. Fazemos isso diretamente do celular ou do computador, quase sem pensar na colossal infraestrutura que viabiliza cada uma dessas respostas. Por trás dessa facilidade aparente, opera uma cadeia física complexa que exige energia constante, resfriamento robusto e conectividade contínua. Enquanto essa capacidade se expande em solo terrestre, surge um novo horizonte computacional: transferir parte dessa carga de processamento para o espaço. O Google deu um primeiro passo concreto nessa direção. Em 30 de outubro, a empresa anunciou ter recebido, diretamente da órbita da Terra, uma resposta gerada pelo seu modelo aberto Gemma 4 por meio de uma unidade de processamento neural (TPU) — um chip dedicado com especificações de data center. O satélite, desenvolvido em parceria com a Planet e lançado em 1º de outubro em uma missão da SpaceX, integra o Project Suncatcher, programa voltado a pesquisas em computação orbital. Embora ainda não represente um data center espacial em pleno funcionamento, a validação técnica cumpriu seu papel: solicitou-se à IA a criação de um haikai temático sobre o cosmos. Durante uma janela de comunicação com a estação em solo, a equipe enviou o comando: escrever um haikai sobre a experiência no espaço. O haikai é um poema curto tradicional de origem japonesa, estruturado em três versos. A resposta foi transmitida quando o satélite sobrevoava Svalbard, na Noruega: "A esfera azul lá embaixo", "Os dados fluem com silenciosa elegância" e "A luz das estrelas alimenta meu núcleo". Mais do que a poesia em si, o marco técnico demonstrou que o hardware em órbita processou a instrução e transmitiu o resultado de volta à Terra com sucesso. Do haikai ao desafio da computação no espaço O experimento reforça uma estratégia de longo prazo do Google. Em 2016, a empresa apresentou publicamente suas TPUs — processadores projetados para acelerar cargas de trabalho de inteligência artificial que já eram utilizados internamente desde 2015. Esses chips atuam como alternativa às GPUs da NVIDIA, embora a cadeia produtiva permaneça interconectada: a Broadcom colabora no design dos componentes e a TSMC é responsável pela fabricação. O protótipo orbital carrega quatro TPUs a bordo, mas opera apenas uma unidade por vez em janelas curtas de cerca de 20 minutos, segundo informações do TechCrunch. Trata-se, portanto, de uma bancada de testes em voo, não de uma estrutura corporativa completa. O teste orbital traz um diferencial técnico importante, embora não seja a primeira execução de algoritmos de IA fora da Terra. Em 2020, a missão Φsat-1 da Agência Espacial Europeia adotou visão computacional em órbita para descartar imagens de satélite encobertas por nuvens antes da descida de dados. Posteriormente, em novembro de 2025, a Starcloud enviou ao espaço um satélite equipado com uma GPU NVIDIA H100 e anunciou no mês seguinte a execução do próprio modelo Gemma a bordo. O pioneirismo agora reivindicado pelo Google consiste em rodar com sucesso esse tipo de processamento em uma TPU projetada para data centers instalada no espaço. A ambição energética e os obstáculos térmicos Os planos do Project Suncatcher vão além de provas de conceito isoladas. O Google estuda a viabilidade de uma infraestrutura distribuída, composta por constelações de satélites com capacidade de processamento conectadas entre si por comunicação óptica a laser. A grande vantagem desse modelo reside na geração de energia: em determinadas órbitas de incidência solar quase ininterrupta, painéis solares poderiam captar até oito vezes mais eletricidade do que módulos equivalentes operando na superfície terrestre, viabilizando uma escala computacional inédita sem pressionar a matriz elétrica do planeta. Apesar do potencial, o ambiente espacial impõe desafios rigorosos. Embora exista a percepção comum de que o frio espacial ajudaria no resfriamento, o vácuo impede a convecção térmica por ausência de ar. Sem circulação atmosférica, o calor emitido pelos chips não se dissipa facilmente. Por isso, a empresa desenvolve circuitos térmicos com radiadores dedicados, submetidos previamente a câmaras de vácuo térmico. A isso se soma o bombardeio constante de radiação cósmica, que pode provocar falhas lógicas e degradação física nos semicondutores ao longo do tempo. Após o envio dos primeiros poemas e de diagnósticos técnicos da telemetria, as equipes preparam simulações de estresse para avaliar o comportamento das TPUs frente à radiação e aos ciclos térmicos extremos. O próximo marco anunciado prevê testes com dois satélites interligados em órbita a partir de 2027, avaliando a computação coordenada entre nós espaciais. A primeira resposta poética não transforma o espaço em um data center de imediato, mas confirma que o componente essencial dessa visão já consegue operar além da nossa atmosfera. artigo.texto: AMD Passes Silicon Market Stress Test, Nearly Doubles Data Center Sales The chipmaker entered the day bearing the weight of the market’s AI-nxiety after rival Intel’s disappointing third quarter result. Sign up for smart news, insights, and analysis on the biggest financial stories of the day. AMD entered Tuesday having beaten analysts’ top and bottom earnings estimates for three straight quarters. Make that four. But that’s just the narrow view. The US chipmaker also entered the day bearing the boulder-heavy weight of the market’s AI-nxiety after rival Intel’s wipeout last week following a disappointing third quarter result. AMD passed the Silicon Stress test and gifted semiconductor investors a sigh of relief. ‘Real Silicon and Real Revenue’ “The market spent October questioning whether AI capital spending converts into revenue and cash flow,” wrote Zacks Investment Research senior equity strategist Bryan Hayes, on Tuesday. “The debate shifted from capability to financing, and it took real casualties among the companies carrying debt to fund the buildout.” AMD certainly felt the pressure, with its shares down 23% in the last month. Last week, long-standing competitor Intel was hit even harder. Its $16.5 billion third quarter revenue was in line with expectations, but its executive’s fourth quarter revenue target of $15 billion to $16 billion came up short, kind of like your putting game. Intel’s stock nose-dived nearly 29% in a single day and is down more than 35% in the last week. Executives blamed the weak forecast on a worse-than-expected decline in the personal computer market, where manufacturers are getting slammed by rising memory costs. Global PC shipments plunged 21% in the third quarter, according to Counterpoint Research, weighing heavily on Intel’s legacy income. Still, there was a silver lining: Intel’s data center and AI segment rose 78% and made $3 billion in operating profit. Makers of central processing units (CPUs) like AMD and Intel spent years playing kid brother to Nvidia and its GPUs in the AI market. But with the advent of agentic AI like Meta’s wildly popular Muse, which requires the continuous general-purpose computing power of CPUs, their value has exploded. While AMD also makes CPUs for PCs, it’s not as exposed as its rival. Nearly two thirds of revenue comes from the data center unit, meaning what was a silver lining for Intel last week proved a golden ticket for AMD on Tuesday: - Revenue at AMD’s data center segment nearly doubled, climbing 97% year-over-year to a record $8.5 billion in the third quarter. Hayes, the Zacks equity strategist, said anything above $8.3 billion could be taken to mean AI spending “is landing on real silicon and real revenue.” - The Santa Clara-based chipmaker’s $13.4 billion in revenue and $7.2 billion gross profit came in ahead of expectations, and its $17 billion outlook for fourth quarter revenue is well ahead of the $16.2 billion average analyst estimate. Beyond the fourth quarter, CEO Lisa Su said last month AMD plans to “substantially increase our supply in 2027” to meet soaring demand, while Intel leader Lip-bu Tan expressed disappointment his firm can only supply about half of what customers want. Rally the Troops: Chipmakers had shown signs of life leading up to AMD’s report yesterday. Broadcom closed up more than 3% and Micron and Nvidia more than 2%. AMD shares, which traded up 8.3% after hours following its earnings report, are poised for gains today. Wall Street doesn’t see the upward trajectory stopping any time soon, either: The average $655 price target of 41 analysts surveyed by Zacks implies a 40% upside on AMD’s stock in the next 12 months.

artigo.texto: Com o crescimento das fontes renováveis, empresas buscam alternativas para aproveitar melhor a eletricidade produzida e enfrentar os desafios da transição energética. A Tecnogera anunciou a apresentação de um sistema de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) durante a Brazil WindPower 2026, realizada entre 27 e 29 de outubro, em São Paulo. A tecnologia permite armazenar eletricidade para utilização posterior e ganha importância diante da expansão das fontes eólica e solar. O objetivo é oferecer maior flexibilidade operacional, melhorar o aproveitamento da geração e contribuir para a estabilidade do sistema elétrico. O interesse pelo armazenamento acompanha uma mudança importante no setor energético. Com o avanço das fontes renováveis, cresce a necessidade de soluções capazes de administrar a eletricidade de maneira mais eficiente. Nesse cenário, as baterias BESS aparecem entre as tecnologias discutidas para atender às novas demandas da matriz elétrica brasileira. Baterias BESS permitem guardar eletricidade e melhorar o aproveitamento da geração eólica e solar O Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) é uma tecnologia desenvolvida para armazenar energia elétrica em baterias e disponibilizá-la posteriormente. Seu funcionamento permite maior flexibilidade na gestão da eletricidade, característica relevante para sistemas que utilizam fontes renováveis. Como a produção eólica e solar depende de condições naturais variáveis, o armazenamento oferece uma alternativa para administrar parte da energia gerada. - Unicamp e Princeton criam plataforma que calcula quanto custará descarbonizar o Brasil e já aponta onde instalar novas usinas até 2050; modelo compara rotas e revela o preço de cada escolha energética - Cientistas brasileiros criam máquina que transforma água e energia solar em hidrogênio verde e mistura combustível diretamente ao gás industrial sem precisar armazená-lo - Cientistas brasileiros usam laser e micro-ondas para fabricar peça de titânio que pode baratear a produção de hidrogênio verde e reduzir o consumo de energia - El Niño ameaça abastecimento de energia na Amazônia e Aneel recomenda instalar mais painéis solares e baterias para enfrentar secas extremas A aplicação dessa tecnologia está relacionada à busca por eficiência e segurança operacional. Ao permitir que a eletricidade seja armazenada, o BESS contribui para otimizar seu aproveitamento e apoiar a estabilidade do sistema elétrico. Essa capacidade explica por que o armazenamento passou a ocupar espaço nas discussões sobre a expansão das energias renováveis. Tecnogera leva tecnologia de armazenamento à Brazil WindPower 2026 para acompanhar mudanças no mercado energético A Tecnogera escolheu a Brazil WindPower 2026 para apresentar sua solução de armazenamento de energia em baterias. Com atuação em soluções de geração e armazenamento, a empresa pretende acompanhar as transformações do mercado e contribuir para os debates sobre novas demandas energéticas. A presença no encontro também representa uma oportunidade para fortalecer o relacionamento com clientes, parceiros e outros representantes do setor. Embora essas fontes tenham papel importante na evolução da matriz energética, suas características exigem atenção à flexibilidade operacional. Por esse motivo, tecnologias de armazenamento ganham relevância nas estratégias de gestão de energia. Os sistemas BESS surgem nesse contexto como alternativas para apoiar o aproveitamento da eletricidade produzida. A possibilidade de armazenar energia e utilizá-la posteriormente contribui para ampliar as opções de operação. Dessa forma, a tecnologia integra as discussões sobre eficiência, estabilidade e segurança do sistema elétrico brasileiro. Em sua edição de 2026, o evento reúne representantes do mercado para acompanhar tendências e discutir soluções relacionadas ao futuro da geração renovável. O armazenamento de energia aparece nesse debate como uma tecnologia capaz de apoiar a evolução do setor. A participação da Tecnogera está inserida nesse ambiente de discussão técnica e relacionamento empresarial. Ao apresentar seu sistema BESS, a companhia busca contribuir para o debate sobre tecnologias voltadas às novas necessidades do mercado. O encontro também permite acompanhar as mudanças relacionadas à geração, ao armazenamento e à gestão da eletricidade. Nesse cenário, o armazenamento em baterias representa uma alternativa para melhorar o aproveitamento da geração e apoiar a flexibilidade operacional. A tecnologia também participa das discussões sobre estabilidade e segurança do sistema elétrico. A apresentação anunciada pela Tecnogera durante a Brazil WindPower 2026 reflete esse interesse crescente pelo armazenamento de energia. artigo.texto: A Trane, divisão de soluções térmicas da Trane Technologies, programou para os dias 4 e 5 de novembro de 2026, durante o DCD Connect Brasil 2026 na capital paulista, a apresentação de uma tese técnica que preconiza o uso de arquiteturas híbridas de resfriamento para mitigar gargalos térmicos em data centers voltados a cargas de inteligência artificial. Segundo a companhia, a escalada de densidade de potência nos racks computacionais exige a convergência planejada entre sistemas tradicionais de expansão a ar e métodos diretos de resfriamento líquido, ajustados à realidade construtiva de cada empreendimento. De acordo com as informações divulgadas pela empresa, o debate será conduzido pelo engenheiro mecatrônico Victor Rodrigues, executivo de vendas e especialista em missão crítica da organização, durante o almoço de abertura do congresso no Sheraton São Paulo WTC Hotel. A fornecedora argumenta que instalações dedicadas ao treinamento e à inferência de modelos de linguagem de grande escala superaram os patamares térmicos que permitiam a operação exclusiva por insuflamento de ar, demandando revisões arquitetônicas imediatas por parte de operadores de hiperescala, empresas de colocation e fundos de investimento em infraestrutura digital. Escalada térmica das cargas de trabalho de alta densidade Conforme a análise apresentada pela fabricante, a proliferação acelerada de chips gráficos especializados (GPUs) e aceleradores neurais nos centros de processamento alterou substancialmente os parâmetros de dissipação de calor por metro quadrado. A Trane afirma que densidades térmicas que historicamente variavam entre 5 kW e 15 kW por rack agora ultrapassam com frequência a faixa de 40 kW a 100 kW em ambientes corporativos destinados a aprendizado profundo, inviabilizando o controle ambiental exclusivamente por corredores frios e ventiladores periféricos de precisão. A entidade técnica defende que a América Latina experimenta uma expansão de capacidade instalada de processamento concentrada principalmente em polos industriais de São Paulo, Querétaro, Santiago e Bogotá, regiões onde a disponibilidade de água para torres de arrefecimento evaporativo enfrenta crescente escrutínio regulatório e restrições de outorga. Diante desse panorama, a empresa aponta que estratégias combinadas passam a ser imperativas para equilibrar a eficiência do uso de energia (PUE) com metas rigorosas de conservação hídrica (WUE). Segundo os apontamentos técnicos da fornecedora, ignorar as limitações físicas de condutividade térmica do ar em densidades extremas compromete a integridade do silício e eleva exponencialmente o risco de paradas não programadas. A corporação alega que a introdução controlada de fluidos dielétricos ou água gelada diretamente no nível do chip permite capturar mais de 70% da carga térmica gerada, reservando o fluxo de ar para componentes periféricos do chassi, como memórias secundárias e fontes de alimentação redundantes. Transição técnica entre dissipação por ar e resfriamento líquido Na avaliação sustentada pela equipe técnica da Trane, a conversão de instalações legadas para ecossistemas inteiramente refrigerados por imersão total representa um dispêndio de capital frequentemente proibitivo e complexo para a maioria dos operadores. Por essa razão, a organização argumenta que as soluções de transição híbrida representam a rota mais pragmática para estender a vida útil de edificações já ativas, mantendo a compatibilidade com servidores convencionais enquanto se abrem zonas dedicadas à alta densidade. A tabela a seguir resume as características operacionais comparativas entre os vetores de gerenciamento térmico analisados pelas equipes de engenharia da empresa: A Trane sustenta que os operadores precisam mapear variáveis como a capacidade de suporte de carga do piso elevado, a pressurização de plenum e o espaço livre para unidades de distribuição de refrigerante (CDU) antes de autorizar a expansão de equipamentos. Segundo o posicionamento corporativo, decisões precipitadas de transição integral podem sobrecarregar a infraestrutura predial de bombeamento e demandar trocas desnecessárias de chillers centrais que ainda possuem amortização contábil pendente. Transformação dos modelos de manutenção e confiabilidade operacional Outro pilar central do material apresentado pela empresa envolve a substituição de contratos de assistência reativa por regimes preditivos contínuos, estruturados sobre governança de ciclo de vida e monitoramento de fluidos. A companhia declara que os sistemas que transportam fluidos refrigerantes diretamente para as placas-mãe de servidores operam sob margens mínimas de tolerância a vazamentos e oscilações de pressão, o que demanda instrumentação analítica e telemetria avançada ininterrupta. Entre as diretrizes de confiabilidade operacional detalhadas pela fornecedora para projetos de missão crítica destacam-se: - Gestão preditiva de pressão diferencial: monitoramento contínuo de circuitos fechados para detecção de microvazamentos de fluidos refrigerantes antes de danos aos componentes semicondutores. - Controle dinâmico de temperatura de entrada de água: parametrização de chillers e trocadores de calor para maximizar períodos de resfriamento gratuito (free cooling), reduzindo o acionamento de compressores elétricos. - Planejamento de redundância N+1 e 2N: dimensionamento de bombas e loops secundários de distribuição para viabilizar manutenção preventiva em pleno regime de carga computacional máxima. - Análise físico-química de fluidos intermediários: verificação periódica de condutividade, pH e inibidores de corrosão em circuitos de líquido direto para evitar incrustações em microcanais de cobre. O executivo da Trane pretende enfatizar durante o DCD Connect Brasil que o custo total de propriedade (TCO) de um data center de inteligência artificial é determinado em mais de 40% pelo consumo energético de seus subsistemas de suporte térmico ao longo de uma década de operação contínua. artigo.texto: Humanoid robots are an emerging technology that promises to revolutionize society. Designed and modeled on the human form, humanoid robots can navigate a world made for humans, and it is their versatility that sets them apart from specialized robots, such as automated guided vehicles (AGVs). Similar to AGVs, humanoid robots need an energy source that can reliably supply power to ensure full operation for as long as required. While current battery technology has been successful in demonstrating humanoid robot potential, IDTechEx’s new report Batteries for Humanoid Robots 2027-2037: Technologies, Players, and Forecasts focuses on the technologies that will lead humanoid robots into widespread adoption in the market, reaching 10.5 GWh of battery demand by 2037. IDTechEx highlights the suitability of current and emerging battery chemistries for humanoid robots. The comparisons illustrate trade-offs between battery performance and technological maturity across different chemistries. Which battery technologies are employed in humanoid robots today? The energy density of a battery used to power a humanoid robot needs to be high enough that it can complete power-intensive tasks and continue operating afterwards. Currently, NMC-based lithium-ion batteries are the most common technology employed by humanoid robots. They balance a suitably high energy density with the prerequisite specifications of humanoids, that is that they require batteries with the potential to be fast-charged, a good cycle life, and a technology mature enough that they are already, or close to being, commercialized. The energy density of NMC cathodes can also be improved by increasing the nickel-content in the cathode, which can boost performance and reduce dependence on costly and supply-constrained cobalt. LFP cathodes are a chemistry considered not energy dense enough to be able to support the general demand of humanoid robots. Since NMC batteries are widely adopted for use in a plethora of other applications, NMC-based lithium-ion batteries are in great supply to support the growth of the humanoid robot market today, and beyond. IDTechEx’s new “Batteries for Humanoid Robots 2027-2037: Technologies, Players, and Forecasts” report compares lithium-ion NMC cathode chemistries (mid-, high-, and ultra high-nickel) as current technology that can support humanoid robot growth. The report also assesses solid-state and lithium-sulfur batteries as key future technology options for implementation in humanoid robots. What are the benefits of adopting emerging technologies? Solid-state Solid-state batteries are a technology that has seen huge capital investment in their development, especially from the automotive industry. A solid-state battery differs from a conventional lithium-ion cell in so much as it removes the liquid electrolyte and replaces it with a solid one. The cell is then composed of an anode, a cathode and solid electrolyte, which also removes the need for a separator. The benefit of using solid-state batteries is primarily their increased energy density of~400-500+ Wh/kg. Lithium metal, which has a high specific capacity, can be utilized as the anode and paired with high-voltage, high-energy-density cathodes (including NMC), thereby increasing the overall energy density of the cell. The removal of the flammable electrolyte improves the overall safety of the cell. Since humanoid robots will operate in close proximity to humans, enhancing safety will reduce the harm to humans in the case of cell failure. In addition, removing the separator allows for tighter packing of materials in the cell, which can improve volumetric energy density. This means a greater proportion of the battery volume within the humanoid can be occupied by active material, enabling the storage of more energy and an extension of operational capacity. However, mass production of solid-state batteries is not due to begin until the end of the 2020’s with key battery manufacturers such as BYD and Toyota driving this. With no scalable production of reliable solid electrolytes, and problems with the interface contact between the electrode and solid electrolyte, the adoption of solid-state batteries into humanoid robots is still some years away; however, it is a matter of when, not if, they will be adopted. Lithium-sulfur Lithium-sulfur cells also employ a lithium metal anode which is paired with a carbon/sulfur cathode. Together, these deliver a high theoretical energy density, which translate to longer operational times for the humanoid. This is also one of the key drivers for humanoid manufacturers opting for lithium-sulfur over solid-state in the future. Moreover, their potential to lower the overall cost of the battery due to the use of abundant and cheap sulfur in the lithium-sulfur cathode also makes them an attractive alternative to solid state batteries will include more complex materials. However, there exist many limitations to their widespread adoption, including poor cycle lives and an inability to withstand fast charging – both caused by a parasitic process termed “polysulfide-shuttle”. This triggers prolonged and sometimes rapid degradation of the cell by reducing the amount of active material over successive cycles. The consequence for the humanoid will be more frequent replacements of the battery packs. The continued research and development of lithium-sulfur batteries is crucial to overcoming this effect. Their commercialization is not expected until the early 2030’s leading to them making up only a small amount of the market by 2037. Main image: Courtesy of Longsing Energy

artigo.texto: Modaso Energy, a company under MISA Group, has partnered with Zimbabwean renewable energy developer Tatanga Energy to develop the 278 MW Guruve-Mazowe (Chikonyora) Hybrid Renewable Energy Project in Mashonaland Central, Zimbabwe. The project is expected to become the country’s first utility-scale wind farm and the first utility-scale facility outside South Africa in sub-Saharan Africa to integrate wind, solar power and battery storage at a single location. The proposed project will comprise 128 MW of wind power capacity, 100 MWac of solar photovoltaic (PV) capacity and a 50 MW/100 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS). All three components will operate through a single 100 MW connection to the national electricity grid. The facility is expected to generate approximately 550 GWh of clean electricity annually, equivalent to around 5% of Zimbabwe’s total national power generation. Tatanga Energy initiated the development in 2021 and is responsible for local project operations, including land acquisition, community engagement, permitting and coordination with government authorities. Modaso Energy is leading the technical development and financial structuring. The company has redesigned the original wind-only proposal into an integrated renewable energy project combining three technologies. It is also overseeing electricity offtake arrangements, contracting and debt financing. MISA Group, headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, is providing financial backing and facilitating connections with international lenders and investors. Zimbabwe’s state-owned power utility, ZESA, is expected to serve as the primary electricity buyer. Negotiations are underway for the Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) and Use of System Agreement. Meanwhile, Africa GreenCo, through its subsidiary ZimGreenCo, has signed Heads of Terms to purchase a portion of the project’s electricity under a long-term arrangement. Additional power could be traded through the Southern African Power Pool, providing access to regional electricity markets. Standard Bank has agreed to a debt term sheet and will act as the appointed lead arranger for the project’s debt financing. The development represents an estimated foreign direct investment of approximately USD 300 million. Financial close is expected in mid-2027, with construction scheduled to follow. The project is targeting commercial operations in 2029. The integration of wind, solar and battery storage is expected to improve electricity generation throughout the day by balancing the different production profiles of the technologies. The facility is designed to achieve an average grid capacity factor of more than 60%. According to the project details, this hybrid configuration could deliver approximately 40% more energy through a single grid connection compared with standalone renewable energy systems. The project is also expected to strengthen Zimbabwe’s electricity supply by reducing dependence on rainfall, Kariba Dam water levels and imported fossil fuels. Its battery storage system will provide fast-response grid support, helping improve power system reliability and flexibility. The development is expected to create around 1,000 construction jobs, with priority given to local workers, while introducing specialised skills in wind energy and hybrid power plant management. It is projected to avoid approximately 0.5 million tonnes of carbon emissions annually, contributing around 11% towards Zimbabwe’s National Renewable Energy Policy target of 2,100 MW by 2030. The project will also finance permanent road improvements along the turbine transportation route and requires no community resettlement. artigo.texto: The Union Cabinet on November 4 approved a Rs 14,500-crore viability gap funding (VGF) scheme to support the development of 92 GWh of grid-scale energy storage capacity by FY31, as India looks to expand storage infrastructure to integrate a larger share of renewable energy into its electricity grid. The scheme will support the development of 60 GWh of pumped hydro storage capacity, 30 GWh of battery energy storage systems (BESS) and 2 GWh of alternative storage technologies. The projects are expected to entail a total investment of Rs 97,600 crore, with the government providing financial support over FY27 to FY31. The scheme is aimed at improving the financial viability of large-scale storage projects, which are critical to managing the intermittent generation of solar and wind power and ensuring round-the-clock electricity supply. The proposed capacity addition is equivalent to 170% of India’s existing grid-scale energy storage capacity and will contribute towards meeting the country’s projected requirement of 411 GWh by FY32. According to the Central Electricity Authority's (CEA) National Electricity Plan, India will require 411.4 GWh of energy storage capacity by 2031-32, comprising 236.22 GWh of battery energy storage systems and 175.18 GWh of pumped hydro storage. The requirement is projected to reach 336.4 GWh by 2029-30. The 92 GWh capacity supported under the newly approved VGF scheme would meet around 22% of the projected storage requirement by FY32. Under the scheme, energy storage capacity will be allocated through a tariff-based competitive bidding process. Public and private sector electricity distribution companies will be eligible for viability gap funding for battery storage and pumped hydro projects, while alternative storage technology projects can be implemented by public and private sector entities. In a move to promote domestic manufacturing, battery storage projects supported under the scheme will be subject to a minimum domestic content requirement of 40%. The government said the provision is intended to encourage indigenous manufacturing, create opportunities for domestic industry and reduce dependence on imported components. The scheme is also expected to complement existing supply-side incentives for battery manufacturing and strengthen India’s energy storage supply chain. The government’s push for large-scale energy storage comes amid rising renewable energy capacity and the need for greater flexibility in the power grid. Storage systems can help absorb surplus renewable electricity during periods of high generation and release it when generation falls or demand rises, reducing the need for conventional power generation to balance the grid. The Cabinet said the scheme would strengthen grid stability, improve renewable energy integration and support the availability of reliable and affordable round-the-clock power. The latest approval builds on the government's earlier efforts to make battery storage projects financially viable through viability gap funding. In September 2023, the Cabinet approved a Rs 3,760-crore budgetary support scheme to develop 4 GWh of battery storage capacity, which was subsequently expanded to around 13.85 GWh as battery prices declined. In June 2025, the Power Ministry also extended VGF support for another 30 GWh of battery storage capacity, with Rs 5,400 crore in financial support from the Power System Development Fund. The latest scheme expands the government's support to include pumped hydro and alternative storage technologies.

Publicly traded, long-duration focus According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Flow Battery market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The global flow battery market is transitioning from a niche, demonstration-phase technology to a commercially bankable solution for long-duration energy storage (LDES), driven by the structural inadequacy of lithium-ion batteries for applications exceeding 4-6 hours. Demand is architecting around utility-scale renewable integration mandates and grid modernization projects, where the technology's inherent safety, long cycle life, and power/energy decoupling offer a compelling total cost of ownership proposition over a 20-year asset life. Supply chain resilience is a critical vulnerability, with key electrolyte materials (vanadium, organic compounds) and specialized components (membranes, pumps, stack assemblies) facing concentration risks, scale-up challenges, and qualification timelines that lag behind demand projections. Project economics are dominated by upfront capital expenditure, with electrolyte cost representing a significant, recoverable portion of the system value. Bankability hinges on proven system performance, robust warranties, and the credibility of off-take agreements for ancillary grid services. The competitive landscape is bifurcating between vertically integrated technology developers controlling core IP (electrolyte, stack) and system integrators/EPCs specializing in balance-of-plant engineering, grid interconnection, and project delivery. Geographic deployment is clustering in regions with aggressive renewable penetration targets, supportive LDES policy mechanisms, and grids experiencing congestion or stability challenges, creating distinct demand hubs. Safety and standardization are emerging as key market enablers. The non-flammable aqueous electrolyte of most flow batteries significantly reduces fire suppression costs and insurance premiums, but a lack of uniform international standards for performance reporting and testing creates friction in procurement. The technology stack's success is inextricably linked to the power conversion system and energy management system. Efficiency losses at the PCS and suboptimal control logic can erode the core economic advantages, making integrator expertise a critical differentiator. Market growth to 2035 will be constrained not by demand potential but by the pace of manufacturing scale-up, supply chain maturation for critical materials, and the ability of the industry to deliver standardized, modular systems that reduce soft costs and EPC complexity. Investors and developers must model scenarios based on electrolyte price volatility, local content requirements, and the evolving policy landscape for long-duration storage procurement. The baseline scenario for the global flow battery market through 2035 anticipates robust expansion, with deployment accelerating as utilities and grid operators increasingly recognize the limitations of lithium-ion chemistry for long-duration applications. The market is forecast to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 15.2% from 2026 to 2035, reaching a market index of 410 by 2035 (2025=100). This growth is underpinned by the structural need for storage durations exceeding 4-6 hours, where flow batteries' independent scaling of power and energy capacity provides a distinct cost advantage. The baseline assumes continued policy support in key markets, particularly China, the United States, and Europe, where LDES procurement targets and capacity remuneration mechanisms are being established. Supply chain constraints, particularly for vanadium electrolyte and specialized membranes, are expected to ease gradually as new production capacity comes online and alternative chemistries gain commercial traction. However, the pace of manufacturing scale-up and the industry's ability to standardize modular systems will determine the actual growth trajectory. Project economics will improve as electrolyte leasing models and recycling infrastructure mature, reducing upfront capital burdens. The competitive landscape will see consolidation among technology developers, with vertically integrated players controlling core IP gaining market share. Geographically, Asia-Pacific will maintain its dominance, driven by China's aggressive renewable build-out and grid modernization investments, while North America and Europe will see accelerated deployment supported by policy frameworks. The baseline scenario does not assume breakthrough cost reductions beyond current learning rates but does incorporate expected improvements in stack efficiency and manufacturing automation. Risks to the outlook include delays in grid interconnection, volatility in vanadium prices, and slower-than-expected development of international standards for performance and safety. Electric utilities and grid operators represent the largest and fastest-growing end-use segment for flow batteries, driven by the need to integrate increasing shares of variable renewable generation and maintain grid stability. artigo.texto: IOI Corporation Berhad has entered into a strategic renewable energy partnership with Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) and a consortium of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to jointly develop a 500 MWac large-scale solar photovoltaic project integrated with a 250 MW/1,000 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) in Malaysia. The project marks IOI’s first participation in a large-scale renewable energy development under the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS). The agreement was signed on 3 November 2026 through IOI’s wholly owned subsidiary, Luminous Aspect Sdn Bhd, which entered into a joint venture and shareholders’ agreement with TNB Renewables Sdn Bhd (TRe) and CSP 500MW Sdn Bhd, representing a consortium of SMEs. The partnership aims to develop the solar and energy storage project through Bahau Energy Ventures Sdn Bhd, an established renewable energy development company. Under the agreed ownership structure, TRe, a wholly owned subsidiary of TNB, will hold a 70% stake in the project development company. Luminous Aspect will own 25%, while the consortium of SMEs will hold the remaining 5% shareholding. The agreement also includes a long-term land lease arrangement between the development company and IOI for approximately 1,300 acres of land located in Bahau, Negeri Sembilan. The project will be supported by a long-term renewable energy offtake agreement between TNB and DayOne Data Centres Limited, a Singapore-headquartered global digital infrastructure platform. Under the agreement announced on 11 June 2025, DayOne is expected to procure up to 500 MWac of renewable energy over a 21-year period to meet the electricity requirements of its data centre operations in Malaysia. The integration of a large-scale battery energy storage system is expected to support renewable energy supply by providing storage capacity and improving the availability of solar power. The project will also contribute to meeting the growing electricity demand from Malaysia’s expanding digital infrastructure and data centre industry. IOI Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Dato’ Lee Yeow Chor said the partnership provides an opportunity to participate in one of Malaysia’s largest solar and energy storage developments under the CRESS framework. He highlighted that the long-term offtake arrangement with an established data centre operator is expected to generate stable recurring income for IOI through its shareholding in the development company and its role as the project land lessor. The investment aligns with IOI’s Five-Year Strategic Roadmap for 2025–2029, which focuses on expanding its renewable energy portfolio and supporting Malaysia’s transition towards a low-carbon energy future. artigo.texto: Marvell compra Lumentum em negócio de US$ 115 bilhões em aposta no mercado de data centers para IA A Marvell Technology anunciou um acordo para comprar a fabricante de componentes ópticos Lumentum em uma transação de US$ 115 bilhões inteiramente em ações, incluindo dívidas, à medida que a fabricante de chips personalizados intensifica seu desafio à rival de maior porte, a Broadcom , em meio a um boom de gastos com inteligência artificial (IA). O negócio, anunciado nesta segunda-feira, é um dos maiores de 2026 e está entre as apostas corporativas mais ousadas até agora no boom da IA, que os executivos do setor de chips esperam que sustente a demanda da indústria por muitos anos. Ao adquirir a Lumentum — uma empresa com cerca de metade do seu tamanho —, a Marvell aposta que o boom de gastos com IA das grandes empresas de tecnologia veio para ficar e que a demanda por componentes ópticos usados para transmitir dados em alta velocidade continuará superando a oferta. Segundo o acordo, a Marvell pagará US$ 1.132 por ação em ações, um prêmio de 23,9% em relação ao último preço de fechamento não afetado da Lumentum em 28 de outubro, antes que as negociações fossem divulgadas pela primeira vez. Isso confere ao negócio um valor patrimonial de US$ 102,54 bilhões. A Marvell afirmou que a transação ampliará o mercado total acessível da empresa resultante da fusão para US$ 550 bilhões. Suas ações subiram 2,8% no pré-mercado, enquanto as negociações com as ações da Lumentum foram suspensas. A Nvidia , gigante dos chips de IA, investiu US$ 2 bilhões tanto na Marvell quanto na Lumentum no início deste ano. Há apenas três anos, a Marvell era uma fabricante de chips relativamente desconhecida. Mas, desde então, seu valor de mercado disparou para mais de US$ 170 bilhões, graças ao seu papel em ajudar gigantes da tecnologia, como a Amazon , a desenvolver chips de IA personalizados e tecnologia de rede para data centers. O acordo firmado nesta segunda-feira também pode fortalecer ainda mais a Marvell em sua disputa com a rival Broadcom, que há muito tempo é a principal parceira de chips personalizados do Google, de propriedade da Alphabet , e oferece aos clientes uma gama mais ampla de hardware de IA para data centers sob o mesmo teto. A Marvell conquistou uma de suas maiores vitórias em agosto, ao assinar um acordo para fornecer chips que atuam em conjunto com os processadores de IA do Google, com um valor de vendas de até US$ 120 bilhões até o ano fiscal de 2033, concedendo ao gigante das buscas o direito de adquirir uma participação de US$12,2 bilhões.

artigo.texto: From Carbon Compliance To Carbon Commerce: India’s Market Enters A New Phase India’s Carbon Credit Trading Scheme is shifting emissions management from voluntary ESG reporting to a regulatory requirement, creating new compliance obligations and potential revenue opportunities for businesses A few years ago, if you asked a company why it was buying carbon credits, the genuine answer would be "to look good." Carbon Credits were added to the company’s annual Sustainability Report alongside the tree planting picture so that the ESG slide deck felt finished. And that era is over and it’s going to end much quicker in India than most people realize. The change is not philosophical. It is regulatory, and it has a timeline attached to it. On 28 June 2023 the Ministry of Power announced the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, 2023 under section 14(w) of the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, which set the stage for what has now become the Indian Carbon Market. The Offset Mechanism, which was a second track to be added by amendment in December 2023, enables non-obligated companies to submit voluntary emission reduction, removal or avoidance projects and earn tradable credits. CCTS idea was that energy-intensive firms to be assigned a target for greenhouse gas emitted per unit of output, firms that meet the target earn tradable Carbon Credit Certificates, and firms that do not meet it must buy certificates or pay a penalty. The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) had set binding emission intensity targets for 7 energy-intensive sectors, aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali, pulp and paper, petroleum refining, petrochemicals and textiles, and more than 490 industrial entities from 2025-26 compliance year. Two more sectors, iron and steel and fertilisers, were also incorporated, taking the overall number to 740 companies and more than 700 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent, making it the biggest emissions trading systems in the world. Cement is a good place to see what this shift means on the ground. The sector accounts for about 177 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent a year, or about 6 per cent of India’s industrial output, and that’s through 186 companies. These plants are now required to set emission intensity targets, which typically start with 2 to 3 per cent cut in 2025-26 and can increase to 3 to 15 per cent the following year, depending on the sub-sector. Steel has a similar challenge. Plants doing blast-furnace basic-oxygen-furnace are benchmarked against 1.46 tonnes of CO2 equivalent per tonne of crude steel and the targets only get tighter from here on out. As Carbon Credit Trading Schemes (CCTS) take shape globally, adherence will increasingly influence how Indian companies compete in export markets. The European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) contains a carbon-linked tariff on cement, steel, aluminium, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity from countries that do not price carbon domestically. By putting a domestic price on those sectors, CCTS gives Indian exporters a way to show they are already paying for their emissions at home, which directly lowers what they owe at the EU border. For emissions-intensive industries, building carbon efficiency and credible emissions management into operations can become a strategic advantage—helping businesses meet evolving international requirements, protect market access and strengthen their position in global supply chains and is more than compliance departments. The international carbon credit market is opening up a significant opportunity, with India’s emerging partnership with Japan offering one of the first real examples of how this market could evolve. On 8 June 2026, the two countries signed the Rules of Implementation for their Joint Crediting Mechanism, a joint effort under Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement providing Indian project developers with a way to bring in Japanese investment and technology for renewable energy, green hydrogen, sustainable aviation fuel and carbon capture and to issue credits that both countries can count on when it comes to meeting their own climate targets. It’s the sort of bilateral plumbing that seems dry initially until you realise that it is the money that gets into projects. Green hydrogen is where this gets interesting for Indian industry. Companies like Reliance Industries, Indian Oil and Adani Enterprises already have serious investment in this area. Government officials have also said that India is in talks with Japan and other partners on bilateral deals to link carbon credits with green hydrogen production in exchange for investment and firm offtake. In that case, if these deals actually happen, they solve two problems for a hydrogen developer at once: the buyer for the credits and the buyer for the fuel. All of this doesn’t work if the credits are not credible, and the market has learned that lesson the hard way. Years of loosely verified offsets, double-counted reductions and vague methodology have made buyers far more wary of what they are actually purchasing. The response in India has been to put verification into the system itself, satellite monitoring, digital registries and third-party validation are now standard features instead of nice-to-have features, and CCTS’s offset mechanism has been designed to be accessible to small project developers and rural communities, not just large industrial players at the heart of compliance. For a company that is producing verified emission reductions, such as renewable energy, sustainable agriculture, ecosystem restoration or industrial decarbonisation, credits have become a revenue line that investors would like to see properly modelled - not just a footnote. And for the energy-hungry companies that are now in CCTS, it is no longer whether to be active in carbon markets. It is how fast they build up the internal capacity to do it well, because the targets only rise from here, and the costs of not being prepared rise every compliance c

artigo.texto: OS DATA CENTERS PODEM PREJUDICAR O PARTIDO DE TRUMP NAS ELEIÇÕES DOS EUA? O repórter do Estadão, Daniel Gateno, fala sobre o documentário “Estadão na América”, que estreia nesta semana, e o medo dos americanos com o futuro dos Estados. A OpenAI propôs renomear os data centers para “centros de computação de IA”, como parte de uma campanha de relações públicas para se alinhar ao possível novo cenário político dos Estados Unidos após as eleições de meio mandato, conforme noticiou a Axios na segunda-feira (2). A startup já até estreou a nova terminologia ao anunciar seu “Programa de Proteção da Rede Elétrica”. Um dos objetivos da mudança de nome é tentar melhorar a reputação das instalações em que funcionam a infraestrutura por trás das soluções de inteligência artificial. Além disso, a empresa estaria se preparando para lidar com um cenário regulatório mais hostil caso o Partido Democrata conquiste a maioria da Câmara e do Senado, como destaca a reportagem. Estratégia inclui mais mudanças Responsável por liderar a campanha, Chris Lehane, diretor de assuntos globais da OpenAI, disse que as eleições realizadas neste início de novembro funcionam como uma espécie de “trailer” para o que acontecerá daqui a dois anos. Para ele, a IA será um dos temas centrais da eleição presidencial de 2028 nos EUA. - Dessa forma, a dona do ChatGPT planeja influenciar o debate em torno da tecnologia, começando pela troca de nome dos data centers; - A inciativa liderada pela empresa inclui várias outras propostas, como a definição de “limites de velocidade para a IA”, com salvaguardas obrigatórias para frear modelos poderosos; - Fazer as pessoas enxergarem a IA como algo positivo para a sua carreira profissional e as tarefas do dia a dia também está nos planos; - Outra ideia é pressionar a Casa Branca para que os EUA desenvolvam padrões globais da tecnologia baseados em valores democráticos. Quanto ao uso do termo “campos de computação de IA”, a empresa acredita que ele descreve melhor o papel dos centros de dados. “São investimentos de longo prazo em computação, infraestrutura de energia e mão de obra qualificada”, disse um porta-voz da startup ao Business Insider. Porém, os esforços para tentar melhorar a imagem dos data centers junto à população não têm obtido bons resultados. Como lembra a publicação, uma pesquisa recente do Pew Research Center mostrou que 54% dos americanos consideram essas instalações prejudiciais ao meio ambiente. Críticas à proposta A ideia de chamar os data centers de campos de computação de IA não foi bem recebida por grupos ativistas como o PauseAI US. A fundadora da entidade, Holly Elmore, disse ao The Verge que a preocupação não é a nomenclatura e sim “os gigantescos e poluentes projetos de construção” associados às empresas de IA. Pensando de maneira semelhante, a diretora do Centro para Justiça Ambiental e Climática da NAACP, Abre’ Conner, tratou a mudança como uma solução ineficaz. “Mudar o nome não resolve o problema e dá a impressão de que a saúde das pessoas e o nosso meio ambiente são problemas de relações públicas, e não preocupações ambientais e climáticas”, disse ela à reportagem. Recentemente, Donald Trump mudou oficialmente o nome da IA no país e chamou de inimigo quem se recusar a adotar o termo superinteligência. Saiba mais nesta matéria. artigo.texto: Contemporary Amperex Technology stock retains EV battery lead at 39.1% Published on 11/02/2026 at 09:04 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller, Editor-in-Chief AD HOC NEWS Global battery demand stays strong - CATL's battery installations grew faster than the global market through September. - CATL continued expanding its overseas automaker customer base while retaining a substantial lead over BYD. - Chinese manufacturers increased their combined presence among the world's leading battery suppliers. Contemporary Amperex Technology retained its position as the world's largest electric-vehicle battery maker through September, according to CnEVPost, which cited figures from South Korean market researcher SNE Research published on Monday, November 2, 2026. CATL widens its global lead CATL recorded 389.2 gigawatt-hours of battery installations in the first nine months of 2026, up 24.9 percent from a year earlier. Its global share reached 39.1 percent, compared with 37.5 percent in the same period of 2025. Global battery usage rose 19.7 percent to 994.5 gigawatt-hours during the period. CATL therefore expanded faster than the overall market, although its share slipped from 39.4 percent in January through August as September growth moderated. Chinese suppliers dominate rankings BYD ranked second with 150.9 gigawatt-hours of installations and a 15.2 percent share. CATL and BYD together accounted for 54.3 percent of global usage, while seven Chinese companies in the top ten held a combined 73.0 percent. The market data also showed a widening difference in business exposure. SNE Research said CATL continued to expand its overseas automaker customer base, while BYD's battery supply remained largely linked to its own vehicle sales. CATL's lead is therefore supported by both scale and a broader customer mix, but monthly share movements underline the competitive pressure in China's battery market. Investor focus shifts to execution The figures strengthen CATL's standing in a growing global market, yet the slower September expansion and intense competition remain relevant for investors. The company's ability to convert international demand into profitable production will be important as Chinese battery makers compete for automaker contracts and energy-storage growth. China's broader market backdrop can be followed through current reports on the Shanghai Composite. artigo.texto: Chemists have developed a graphene-armoured anode designed to overcome sodium-ion batteries’ trade-off between charging speed and lifespan. Interest in sodium-ion batteries has grown in recent years as researchers seek more sustainable alternatives to lithium-ion technology. Sodium is approximately 1000 times more abundant than lithium, potentially easing supply-chain constraints and reducing battery costs, although overall environmental impact depends on other components in the battery, supply chains and manufacturing. Sodium-ion batteries also offer several advantages, including high power output, rapid charging and reliable operation at low temperatures. However, sodium-ion batteries currently still exhibit lower power density and energy density than their lithium-ion counterparts. Researchers in China have now addressed this trade-off by using ultrathin nanosheets of titanium dioxide wrapped in a graphene-based protective shell to create a battery anode. This offers a potential route to high-power sodium-ion batteries, with the key advance being not a new battery ingredient but a structural design that combines fast charging and long life under more demanding electrode conditions. This architecture, says Wei Li at Fudan University, China, does several jobs at once. The nanosheets allow sodium ions to move in and out easily, helping the electrode charge and discharge quickly, while the graphene coating improves electrical conductivity and helps protect the anode’s structure. ‘Our design combines fast energy storage with long cycle life, even when considerably more active material is packed onto the electrode,’ he adds. In tests, the electrode retained more than 90% of its capacity after 3000 cycles at a relatively high active-material loading. ‘Practical charging speed also depends on the cathode electrode and electrolyte,’ says Li. ‘Both must keep pace with our electrode and remain stable during repeated fast charging.’ The anode was made using established processing steps: forming the particles, coating them with carbon and heat-treating the material. ‘However, familiarity does not establish industrial scalability,’ says Li. ‘Maintaining the same thin sheets and uniform graphene wrapping across large batches remains unproven. We would need to demonstrate consistent quality, yield and performance using larger equipment, while assessing energy use and processing costs.’ Tengfei Song, a research fellow at the University of Birmingham, UK, who was not involved in the study, agrees. ‘This is a strong piece of fundamental research,’ he says. ‘The authors show that careful nanoscale and interfacial design can give a titanium dioxide anode unusually fast sodium-ion storage kinetics and very long cycle life, even at relatively high mass loading. However, I would see it mainly as a high-power materials concept rather than a commercially ready anode material.’ Although the material’s large surface area helps it store sodium quickly, it could make manufacturing more difficult and costly at scale, Song adds. ‘The main next step would be testing under more realistic full-cell conditions,’ says Song. This would mean testing the material in larger batteries, using practical amounts of active material and without the need for extra sodium to compensate for early losses. A test cell to emulate a normal battery environment would help establish whether the anode’s fast charging and long cycle life translate into useful energy storage in a practical battery, he concludes. References Y Wan et al, J. Am. Chem. Soc., 2026, DOI: 10.1021/jacs.6c13892

artigo.texto: Global energy storage owner-operator BW ESS has started commercial operations for the first phase of its Hams Hall battery energy storage system (BESS) in the West Midlands. The milestone brings 350 MW/1243 MWh of storage capacity into commercial operation, the largest BESS by storage capacity (MWh) in Europe and a significant step forward in the delivery of infrastructure supporting the UK’s transition to a cleaner, more resilient energy system. Located adjacent to National Grid’s Hams Hall substation, the project will help balance variable electricity demand and intermittent renewable generation, supporting greater integration of renewable energy while strengthening grid resilience and energy security. The project reached commercial operation just 20 days after energisation. From commissioning and testing to operational readiness, BW ESS worked closely with partners including Sungrow, Energy-IO, National Grid, and NESO. Achieving this milestone safely and efficiently reflects the engineering expertise, rigorous preparation, and close co-ordination behind Hams Hall, as well as the technical capability and commitment of everyone involved. Hams Hall’s capacity will increase to 400 MW/1424 MWh following completion of its second phase. At full capacity, the project will be capable of supporting the electricity needs of around 1.3 million homes for up to 3.5 hours, which is approximately equivalent to the number of households across Greater Manchester. Erik Strømsø, CEO and Co-Founder of BW ESS, commented: “The start of commercial operations at Hams Hall is a landmark moment for BW ESS and a significant addition to Europe’s energy infrastructure. The project was built and commissioned on budget and ahead of schedule, which is a remarkable achievement for a system of this scale and complexity and a testament to the dedication and expertise of our team, and the commitment and collaboration of our partners.” Long-term revenues for the project are underpinned by a 10-year floor and optimisation agreement with EDF and financing was recently secured from lenders OCBC, Rabobank, and Société Générale. Hams Hall forms part of BW ESS’ 2.6 GWh Ardenham portfolio, co-owned with leading energy and decarbonisation investor AIP Management. Its entry into commercial operations expands BW ESS’ operating presence in the UK, alongside the 331 MWh Bramley BESS in Hampshire. The company also has 857 MWh under construction at Berkswell and a broader UK development pipeline spanning multiple gigawatt hours. artigo.texto: Italy connected 1.74 GW of new solar photovoltaic (PV) capacity in the third quarter of 2026, registering a 37% increase compared to the 1.269 GW added during the same period in 2025. The country’s solar market continued to expand during the first nine months of the year, with total new installations reaching 4.834 GW through 147,632 newly connected systems. According to data compiled by ITALIA SOLARE from Terna’s Gaudì database, Italy had 2,314,113 connected photovoltaic systems as of September 30, 2026, representing a cumulative installed capacity of 48.347 GW. During the third quarter alone, 58,459 new systems were connected, compared to 38,660 in the previous quarter, marking a 34% increase. Newly connected capacity also increased by 5% compared to the second quarter. The growth was mainly driven by utility-scale and commercial and industrial (C&I) installations. During the first nine months of 2026, utility-scale projects with capacities of 1 MW and above added 2,241 MW through 473 installations, accounting for 46% of the total new capacity. The C&I segment, covering systems between 20 kW and 1 MW, contributed 1,697 MW from 11,905 installations, representing 35%. Residential installations of up to 20 kW added 897 MW through 135,254 connections, accounting for 19%. During the third quarter, utility-scale installations contributed 858 MW, including 394 MW from projects between 1 MW and 10 MW and 464 MW from projects above 10 MW. C&I installations added 543 MW, while residential systems contributed 341 MW. Geographically, Sicily led Italy in newly connected solar capacity during the first nine months, adding 686 MW. Lombardy followed with 644 MW, ahead of Piedmont with 498 MW, Veneto with 463 MW, Emilia-Romagna with 443 MW and Lazio with 432 MW. Lombardy recorded the highest number of new installations, with 22,999 systems, followed by Veneto with 18,099. Italy’s energy storage market also continued to expand, approaching the 20 GWh milestone. By September 30, 2026, the country had connected 984,829 electrochemical storage systems with a combined capacity of 19,983 MWh and a power output of 8,338 MW. Of the total capacity, 12,552 MWh was associated with photovoltaic installations, while 7,368 MWh came from standalone storage systems. During the first nine months, 1,953 MWh of new storage capacity was connected, including 1,486 MWh associated with solar installations and 467 MWh from standalone systems. In the third quarter, photovoltaic-linked storage added 480 MWh of capacity and 252 MW of power through 31,039 new connections. This represented a 15% increase in capacity compared to the same quarter in 2025. Lombardy also led the photovoltaic-linked storage segment, adding 206 MWh during the first nine months, followed by Emilia-Romagna with 155 MWh, Veneto with 146 MWh and Sicily with 144 MWh. ITALIA SOLARE highlighted the growing importance of utility-scale solar and energy storage in Italy’s energy transition, while emphasising the need to continue supporting distributed generation, self-consumption and regulatory improvements to accelerate storage deployment.
